title: Add NVIDIA Parakeet STT provider (local, streaming-capable) — nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
description:
## Why
User explicitly asked for this 'at the very top' — Parakeet is a fast on-device model that supports streaming, which Whisper does not natively. Hosted at https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 (NVIDIA NeMo).

## Scope
- New provider plugin `parakeet_stt` next to existing `faster_whisper_stt` in `backend/app/providers/`.
- Local execution. Auto-download model to `~/.johnny/parakeet-models/` (mirror the Piper/Whisper bind-mount pattern from the `piper-voice-catalog-307-fix` memory — host bind mount, not Docker named volume).
- Expose both batch (one-shot transcribe) AND streaming (partial-result) interfaces, even though streaming consumer ships in Johnny-stt.3.
- Provider config schema: device (cpu/cuda/mps), language, beam size.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Provider listed in `providers/loader.py` and `providers/schema.py` and discoverable via the STT catalog.
- [ ] Transcribes a 10-second WAV fixture in `backend/tests/fixtures/audio/` with WER no worse than the `faster_whisper` baseline on the same fixture.
- [ ] Passes the same contract tests as `faster_whisper_stt` (instantiate, transcribe bytes, transcribe stream).
- [ ] Model bundle downloads idempotently; second start uses cached model and emits no network calls.
- [ ] Appears in the STT catalog UI (Johnny-stt.2) and Test button returns a non-empty transcript.
- [ ] License documented in the provider's docstring/README section (NeMo / HF model card).

## Validation
- Unit + integration tests in `backend/tests/providers/test_parakeet_stt.py`.
- `@pytest.mark.network` for the live HuggingFace download test (per project rule — mocks miss redirect-shape bugs, see `piper-voice-catalog-307-fix`).
- **Browser (chrome-devtools MCP):** navigate to STT settings → confirm 'Parakeet' appears in the provider list → click Test → assert transcript text node renders → screenshot for PR.

## Open questions
- Confirm Parakeet works under Johnny's Linux/Docker worker (Python 3.14 venv). NeMo prefers CUDA but CPU is supported.

## Depends on
- Johnny-stt.2 (catalog UI must exist first so Parakeet has somewhere to be tested from the UI)

title: Playground: every audio stream rejected with 'Audio stream ended: session not active' — regression from Johnny-ckz.14
description:
## Context
Johnny-ckz.14 ('STT artifacts trigger AI replies — no noise-floor / floor-management gate') was closed in commit d233d39. Since that landed, the playground is **completely unusable**: every audio stream is rejected immediately with `'Audio stream ended: session not active'`. No transcription, no replies, no usable voice mode at all.

This fully reverses the intent of Johnny-ckz.14: instead of dropping only noise turns, the new gating drops **every** turn, including legitimate speech.

## Current behavior
- User opens /playground, starts a session, speaks.
- Playground shows the error toast / chat row: `Audio stream ended: session not active`.
- Happens on every utterance, including obvious real speech.
- No bot reply is produced.

## Expected behavior
- Real user utterances reach the LLM and produce a reply, as they did before Johnny-ckz.14.
- Only noise / single-filler / dot-sequence transcripts are dropped (the original Johnny-ckz.14 intent).
- The session stays 'active' for the full duration the user has the playground open, regardless of noise-gate decisions on individual chunks.

## Repro
1. Start the local stack (`./run.sh`).
2. Open the playground (`/playground`).
3. Start a session, grant mic permission.
4. Say anything ('hello', 'yes', 'testing one two three').
5. Observe: error `Audio stream ended: session not active` in the chat, no reply.

## Related
- Regression from Johnny-ckz.14 (commit d233d39).
- Same surface as Johnny-ckz.11 (playground audio playback) and Johnny-ckz.10 (playground validation).
- Re-run Johnny-ckz.14's test plan end-to-end once this is fixed.

## Likely surface (hint, not prescription)
The message 'Audio stream ended: session not active' sounds like the noise-gate or floor-manager is mutating session state (marking the session inactive) when it decides to drop a chunk, instead of just dropping the chunk and leaving the session alive. Bisect against d233d39; check the WebSocket / audio-stream lifecycle in the playground route handler and any new gate code introduced for Johnny-ckz.14.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Saying a clear real utterance ('yes', 'hello', 'testing one two three') in /playground produces a normal bot reply — no 'Audio stream ended' error.
- [ ] The session remains active across multiple consecutive utterances; a single dropped/noise chunk does NOT end the session.
- [ ] Johnny-ckz.14's original guarantees still hold (regression-test, do not roll back): 60-second silent window produces zero ghost replies; single-noise tokens are dropped at the gate.
- [ ] Both the 'let real speech through' path AND the 'drop noise' path are covered by automated tests so this can't silently break again.
- [ ] The activity log (where present) shows each path correctly: dropped-noise vs. accepted-turn.

## Validation — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP
- navigate_page → /playground
- take_snapshot (initial)
- Drive: grant mic, start session
- evaluate_script to inject a known WAV (real speech, e.g. 'testing one two three') into the mic stream OR drive the existing fixture path
- wait_for the bot reply DOM node; assert it appears
- list_console_messages and list_network_requests — assert no 'Audio stream ended' errors and at least one outbound LLM call
- Drive a silence period (≥ 30s); assert no ghost reply (regression check on Johnny-ckz.14)
- Drive a known noise burst; assert the chunk is dropped silently but session stays active
- take_screenshot of: real-utterance reply, silent-window with no replies, session-still-active state
- Attach all screenshots to the PR
close_reason: No longer relevant — user confirmed in-session that the 'Audio stream ended: session not active' regression is not reproducing / no longer in scope. Filed and immediately retracted in the same session.

title: Playground: STT artifacts ('you', 'uh', '...' dot sequences) trigger AI replies — no noise-floor / floor-management gate before invoking LLM
description:
## Symptom

Mic noise (not real speech) gets transcribed as nonsense tokens and the bot replies to them. Confirmed by user:

> 'speech to text sometimes might be just add some sort of I don't know like "you" or maybe "ah" or maybe just plain "............" dot sequence, And the AI is being triggered on that.'

Observed STT outputs that trigger a reply when no user actually spoke:
- Single filler tokens: you, ah, uh, hm
- Dot / ellipsis sequences: ............
- Likely other low-content fragments (any combination of these)

Result: the bot 'replies' to noise, taking the conversational floor when the user didn't actually take a turn. This makes the playground feel possessed — the bot keeps interjecting on its own.

## Why this is P0

This destroys the usefulness of voice mode entirely. The user cannot have a normal conversation with the bot because every cough / keyboard click / background noise / silent-but-noisy mic produces a ghost turn the bot responds to.

## Likely cause

Two layers are probably both contributing:

1. **STT-side**: the STT provider (cloud or local Whisper) is being fed continuous audio with no VAD gate, and emits short hallucinated tokens during silence / noise. This is a known behaviour for these models — they always try to produce something.
2. **Router-side**: there is no 'should the bot actually respond to this?' gate between STT and the LLM. Whatever STT emits becomes a user turn, and the LLM dutifully replies.

Fix needs both — even with a good VAD, garbage will occasionally slip through, so the router needs a gate too.

## Fix shape (investigation, not prescription)

Layered defence — at least two of these, ideally all:

- **VAD gate before STT**: only feed STT audio segments where VAD says 'speech is present'. Don't transcribe silence / pure noise. (Probably the highest-leverage fix.)
- **Minimum-content filter on STT output**: discard transcripts shorter than N characters or fewer than M tokens (e.g. anything ≤ 2 chars or ≤ 1 token), and discard transcripts that are entirely from a noise-token stoplist (you, uh, hm, mm, dot/ellipsis sequences, single letters, common one-syllable interjections). Tune the stoplist over time.
- **STT confidence threshold (if the provider exposes one)**: discard transcripts below a confidence floor.
- **Minimum-utterance-duration filter on VAD**: require ≥ ~250-400 ms of detected speech before counting it as a turn.
- **Router-side 'is this a real turn?' check** as a last line of defence: if the transcript looks empty / one-noise-token / pure punctuation, the router does not invoke the LLM at all and the bot stays silent.

All of these should be configurable per-provider (some providers may have built-in VAD that's already good and shouldn't be double-gated).

## Out of scope

- Distinguishing the user's voice from another person in the room (speaker diarization). Separate, harder problem.
- Wake-word activation. Separate feature if we ever want it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. With the user silent (only ambient mic noise: keyboard, breathing, room hum) for ≥ 60 s, the bot emits **zero** spontaneous replies. No ghost turns.
2. Single-noise-token transcripts (you, uh, hm, dot sequences, single letters) never reach the LLM; they're dropped at the gate and visibly logged as 'filtered noise' (so we can audit / tune the stoplist).
3. Real user turns still go through unchanged — short legitimate utterances ('yes', 'no', 'okay') are not falsely dropped. Acceptance includes a regression test: a user saying 'yes' is treated as a real turn.
4. The filtering is per-provider configurable, with sane defaults.
5. The activity log (Johnny-ckz.7, once it lands) records each dropped 'noise turn' as an event so the operator can see what the gate caught and tune.
6. Validated via chrome-devtools MCP.

## Testing approach — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

- Open the playground in chrome-devtools MCP and start a session.
- evaluate_script to capture a 60 s window where the user does nothing (or pipe in synthetic noise / silence).
- list_network_requests and assert zero outbound LLM-call requests during that window.
- take_snapshot the activity / event log and assert dropped-noise entries are visible if any noise was filtered.
- Drive a series of short real utterances ('yes', 'no', 'okay', 'thanks') and assert each one DOES produce a bot reply (regression check: don't over-filter).
- Drive a noise-burst (cough sound) and assert no LLM call fires.
- Capture screenshots: idle state with no replies, log showing filtered entries, real-utterance reply.

## Related

- [[playground-live-mode-no-audio-playback-critical-plus-needs-template-driven-mode-picker-volume-control-and-resume-from-session-page-ux]] (Johnny-ckz.11) — same surface.
- [[validate-in-browser-live-chat-live-talking-johnny-ckz-6-end-to-end-via-chrome-devtools-mcp-pure-verification-file-follow-up-bugs-for-any-gap]] (Johnny-ckz.10) — should have caught this.
- [[in-browser-voice-text-chat-with-the-bot-per-event-try-with-bot-button-plus-standalone-playground]] (Johnny-ckz.6) — parent feature.
- [[per-session-activity-timing-log-surfaced-in-chat-history-per-turn-pipeline-events-with-durations]] (Johnny-ckz.7) — must record dropped-noise events so the gate can be audited / tuned.
design: Layered defence: VAD gate before STT (don't transcribe silence/noise), minimum-content + stoplist filter on STT output, optional STT confidence threshold, minimum-utterance-duration on VAD, and a router-side 'is this a real turn?' check as last line of defence. Per-provider configurable so providers with built-in VAD aren't double-gated. Dropped events emit to the activity log (Johnny-ckz.7) so the stoplist can be audited and tuned over time.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Bot emits zero spontaneous replies during a 60s silent-window test. (2) Single-noise-token transcripts ('you', 'uh', dot sequences, single letters) are dropped at the gate, never reach the LLM, and are logged. (3) Real short utterances ('yes', 'no', 'okay') still produce a reply — no false-drop regression. (4) Filtering is per-provider configurable with sane defaults. (5) Activity log records dropped-noise events. (6) chrome-devtools MCP validation captures idle silence, real-utterance reply, and the dropped-noise log entries.

title: Playground: voice barge-in does nothing — bot ignores user speech mid-utterance (interrupt bug recurring on WebRTC transport)
description:
## Symptom

In the in-browser playground (and the per-event 'Try with bot' surface), while the bot is speaking, the user cannot interrupt it by talking. Confirmed by user:

> 'interruption approach doesn't work at all. also yes we cannot mute if if the agent saying something for a long time we cannot interrupt it.'

Attempt today: speak over the bot. Result: bot keeps speaking, ignores the user's voice. No UI mute / stop button is being used (and may not exist as a fallback).

## Why this is P0

Without working interrupt, the playground cannot be used to test the very thing it was built to test — interrupt behaviour — and any long bot reply traps the user with no escape except closing the tab.

## Why this is recurring

Voice-interrupt was already 'fixed' on the meet-worker / Google Meet transport (commit abe48a7: 'Johnny-ze3 Voice interrupt doesn't actually work end-to-end' was closed). The playground uses a **different transport** (browser-direct WebRTC, no meet-worker) — so either the interrupt fix didn't reach this code path, or the playground is bypassing the floor-management logic the meet-worker uses. Treat this as the same logical bug surfacing on a new surface, not a brand-new failure mode.

## Investigation pointers (not prescriptive)

- Is STT actually running while TTS is playing in this transport? On the meet-worker side, stt-transcription-of-participants-must-never-pause-while-bot-is-speaking-or-thinking (Johnny-har) was the original gate. If the playground transport pauses STT during TTS, voice barge-in cannot work — fix that first.
- Is the user's audio reaching STT at all during bot speech? Check the WebRTC inbound audio track and confirm it's still being captured and fed to STT.
- Once STT is producing partials during bot speech, is the interrupt signal being routed to the TTS adapter / audio pipeline? In the meet-worker the contract is 'stop the TTS subprocess + drain the output queue'. The browser-WebRTC path needs the same contract.
- Latency budget should match Johnny-ckz.4's (user speech end → bot audio cut < 500 ms p95).

## Fallback control (also missing)

In addition to voice barge-in, there is no visible UI button to stop / mute the bot while it speaks. Even with voice barge-in working, a visible 'Stop' (or 'Interrupt') button on the live UI is required so the user always has an explicit escape hatch — clicking it must cut TTS within ~300 ms.

## Acceptance criteria

1. While the bot is speaking, the user can talk over it ('stop', 'wait', any natural interrupt) and the bot's audio is cut within Johnny-ckz.4's latency budget (user speech end → bot audio cut < 500 ms p95).
2. The user's interrupting speech lands in transcript_chunks (proves STT did not pause during bot speech).
3. A visible 'Stop' (or equivalent) button exists in the live playground UI and cuts TTS within ~300 ms when clicked.
4. After an interrupt, the bot yields the floor (does not emit a follow-up utterance unless the user's interrupt requested one — same contract as the harness from Johnny-ckz.4).
5. Same behaviour on the standalone /playground surface and on the per-event 'Try with bot' surface.
6. Validated via chrome-devtools MCP per the AGENTS.md top rule.

## Testing approach — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

- Start a playground session, drive a user turn that triggers a long reply.
- Mid-reply, simulate a 'stop' utterance (use the Speaker harness from Johnny-ckz.4 if available; otherwise drive via captured audio + evaluate_script).
- evaluate_script on the audio element to capture the timestamp when currentTime stops advancing (the cut).
- list_network_requests to capture STT request/response timestamps during bot speech.
- Compute end-to-end latency: user speech end → audio cut. Assert < 500 ms p95 over ≥10 runs.
- Click the 'Stop' button mid-reply and evaluate_script to confirm the cut within ~300 ms.
- Repeat the same sequence on the per-event 'Try with bot' surface.
- Screenshots of the live session before / after the interrupt embedded in the PR.

## Related

- [[playground-live-mode-no-audio-playback-critical-plus-needs-template-driven-mode-picker-volume-control-and-resume-from-session-page-ux]] (Johnny-ckz.11) — same surface; this bug should be fixed alongside or as part of that rebuild.
- [[validate-in-browser-live-chat-live-talking-johnny-ckz-6-end-to-end-via-chrome-devtools-mcp-pure-verification-file-follow-up-bugs-for-any-gap]] (Johnny-ckz.10) — should have caught this; this bug is the kind of thing that task is meant to surface.
- [[in-browser-voice-text-chat-with-the-bot-per-event-try-with-bot-button-plus-standalone-playground]] (Johnny-ckz.6) — parent feature.
- [[run-the-two-bot-voice-interrupt-harness-end-to-end-against-real-models-fix-any-bugs-it-surfaces]] (Johnny-ckz.4) — the latency budget this bug must hit.
design: Mirror the meet-worker interrupt contract on the playground's WebRTC transport. Ensure STT runs during TTS playback in this transport (cf. Johnny-har contract). Interrupt signal must drain the TTS output queue and stop the TTS adapter — same authoritative cut the meet-worker path uses, no separate playground logic. Add a visible Stop control wired to the same cut path so the user always has a UI escape hatch.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Voice barge-in cuts bot audio within 500 ms p95 of user-speech-end. (2) User's interrupting speech persists in transcript_chunks. (3) Visible Stop button in playground live UI cuts TTS within ~300 ms when clicked. (4) Bot yields the floor after interrupt (no follow-up unless requested by the interrupt itself). (5) Same behavior on /playground and per-event 'Try with bot'. (6) chrome-devtools MCP validation with ≥10 measured runs and PR screenshots.

title: Playground audio path never opens WebSocket — no voice, no bot replies (Johnny-ckz.6 regression)
description:
## Why this exists

Validation under [[validate-in-browser-live-chat-live-talking-johnny-ckz-6-end-to-end-via-chrome-devtools-mcp-pure-verification-file-follow-up-bugs-for-any-gap]] (Johnny-ckz.10) drove the playground end-to-end via chrome-devtools MCP. Despite the playground showing "audio ready" and the `browserAudio.ts` module being loaded, **no WebSocket connection to `/ws/sessions/{id}/audio` is ever opened by the page**, no `<audio>` element is created, and no audio is ever heard. The bot also never produces a spoken or text utterance.

## Reproduction (chrome-devtools MCP trace)

1. Navigate to `http://localhost:5173/playground` — page mounts a fresh session (POST `/sessions/browser/start` → 201, session 224 created, `source: browser`).
2. The session row is created in DB with `audio_ws_path: /ws/sessions/{id}/audio` (verified via `GET /sessions/224`).
3. `evaluate_script(() => document.querySelectorAll('audio,video').length)` → **0**.
4. `list_network_requests` filtered to `resourceTypes: ['websocket']` over the entire session lifetime → **empty**. (113 total network requests, none of them WebSocket.)
5. `performance.getEntriesByType('resource').filter(r => r.name.includes('/ws/'))` → **empty**.
6. Type "Hello can you hear me?" into the text input and click Send. POST `/sessions/browser/224/text` returns 202.
7. Wait 30+ seconds. UI still shows "Idle". DB state for session 224:
   - `transcripts` grows (mostly STT hallucinations from silence — see linked bug).
   - `utterances: []`
   - `decisions: []`

So the user types, the request is accepted, but no bot reply is ever produced, no audio is ever scheduled, no WS is ever opened.

## What `browserAudio.ts` says SHOULD happen

`frontend/src/lib/browserAudio.ts:9` documents the contract:

> The browser captures audio from the user's mic with `getUserMedia`, downsamples it to 16 kHz mono signed-16-bit PCM via an `AudioWorkletNode`, and sends each 20 ms frame as a binary WebSocket message to `/ws/sessions/{id}/audio`. Incoming TTS frames are decoded to `Float32` samples and pushed through the same `AudioContext` for playback.

This is what the validation expected to find and didn't. The "audio ready" badge in the UI is lying.

## Likely root causes (do not over-fit — find the real one)

- `/playground` page calls `startBrowserSession` (the REST POST) but never calls `startBrowserAudioSession` (the WS+audio wiring in browserAudio.ts). Most likely a missing call in `src/routes/playground/+page.svelte`.
- Or `startBrowserAudioSession` is being called but the resulting promise rejects silently (e.g. mic permission, AudioWorklet load error) and the UI doesn't surface the error — the "audio ready" badge would still render because it isn't gated on `isLive()`.
- Backend `barge-in classifier` is also failing with `httpx.ReadTimeout` against the openai-compatible LLM (see worker logs: `barge-in classifier failed for session=224 — leaving current response running`). Even after fixing the front-end WS gap, the LLM timeout may still suppress replies.

## Acceptance

1. Opening `/playground` and clicking Start opens a WebSocket to `/ws/sessions/{id}/audio` (visible in chrome-devtools MCP `list_network_requests` with `resourceTypes: ['websocket']`).
2. Typing text into the input and clicking Send produces an `utterance` row in the DB AND an audible TTS reply through the browser's speakers within ~10s.
3. `evaluate_script` shows the AudioContext is `running` and at least one buffer source has been scheduled (`scheduledOutputs > 0`) when the bot speaks.
4. End session tears down the WS, releases the AudioContext, and stops the mic track.
5. The "audio ready" badge accurately reflects `isLive()` — it should not show when no WS is open.
6. Verified end-to-end via chrome-devtools MCP and screenshots attached to the PR.

## Evidence artifacts (captured in this run)

- Screenshots: `.validation-ckz10-artifacts/01-playground-live-session.png`, `03-after-text-sent.png`, `06-after-end-session.png`
- Worker logs (LLM ReadTimeout): `barge-in classifier failed for session=224 — leaving current response running` (5 occurrences over the session lifetime).
- DB rows: session 224 ended with 12 transcripts, 0 utterances, 0 decisions. Session 226 (via Try-with-bot) ended with 2 transcripts, 0 utterances, 1 decision (the one decision was `should_speak=false` on silence).
close_reason: No longer relevant — superseded by recent playground work (Johnny-ckz.11 audio-playback fix, Johnny-ckz.14 noise gate). Any remaining playground audio failures are now tracked under Johnny-ckz.16 ('Audio stream ended: session not active' regression from Johnny-ckz.14).

title: Playground / live mode: no audio playback (critical) + needs template-driven mode picker, volume control, and resume-from-session-page UX
description:
## Why this exists

The playground / live-mode surface from [[in-browser-voice-text-chat-with-the-bot-per-event-try-with-bot-button-plus-standalone-playground]] (Johnny-ckz.6) has critical problems that make it unusable as the testing playground it was supposed to be:

- **Audio is silent.** The user can SEE the bot's transcription appear in the UI, but hears nothing through speakers. This makes the playground useless for its primary purpose — talking to the bot voice-to-voice.
- **Configuration is anemic.** The current playground only exposes Persona and a custom system prompt. The whole point of a playground is to simulate every behavior the real bot supports — auto-mode, approval-mode, and any other decision modes that exist — against any template. Right now the user cannot exercise those code paths in the playground at all.
- **No volume control.** Even when audio works, the user needs to adjust speaker volume mid-session without leaving the page.
- **No way back into a live session.** If the user accidentally closes the playground browser tab, the live session is effectively lost — the session detail page does not offer a way to re-attach to (or re-open) the running session.

## CRITICAL — fix the audio bug first

This is the blocker. The rest of the task is meaningless until the user can hear the bot.

Symptom (user-reported):
> 'I can see the transcription and everything but I don't hear what they say to me.'

Investigation pointers (do not over-fit to these — the goal is to find and fix the root cause, not to chase a guess):
- Is TTS output actually being sent to the browser, or is the audio bridge buffering / dropping it? Inspect via chrome-devtools MCP list_network_requests for the audio stream and check the audio element's readyState, muted, volume, currentTime.
- Is the audio element being created at all? evaluate_script to enumerate document.querySelectorAll('audio,video') and check the source.
- Is the WebRTC track being received but with the wrong sample rate, codec, or kind? Check RTCPeerConnection.getReceivers() and the inbound RTP stats.
- Is the user's TTS provider configured + active? (Cross-check with the active-provider state surfaced after the schema-drift fix from [[bot-sessions-schema-drift-orm-expects-source-and-playground-overrides-columns-that-don-t-exist-worker-monitor-plus-sessions-active-both-500]] (Johnny-ckz.9) lands.)
- Auto-play policy: did the browser block playback because the audio started before a user gesture? If so, the UI needs an explicit 'unmute' / 'start' button or the audio must be unlocked at click-time.

Acceptance for the audio bug specifically: the user clicks 'Start' in the playground, says hello, and HEARS the bot reply in their speakers. Verified in chrome-devtools MCP by evaluate_script-ing the audio element's currentTime increasing while bot TTS is playing.

## Required: template + mode picker (simulate the whole bot, not just persona)

Today's playground configuration surface is two fields: Persona + custom system prompt. That covers ~5% of what the playground needs to simulate. The playground must let the user exercise EVERY behavior the real bot supports against any template the system supports.

What the configuration surface must include:

- **Template picker** — choose any session template the rest of the system recognises. The playground must respect the template's defaults exactly the way a real-event session would.
- **Decision mode picker** — auto mode, approval mode, and any other modes the bot ships (observer / silent / etc — whatever the live code paths are). Switching modes in the playground must drive the same code paths the real bot uses; don't fork the logic.
- **Per-session provider overrides** — already in scope from Johnny-ckz.6 (TTS / STT / LLM override). Make sure all three are surfaced, not just one.
- **Persona + custom system prompt** — keep what's there.
- **Optional context injection** — paste in fake calendar event metadata, attendees, linked-doc snippets — so the playground can simulate per-event surfaces without an actual event.
- **Sensible defaults** — every field has a reasonable default so a user who just wants to chat picks Start and goes; advanced knobs are expanded on demand.

If 'modes' / 'templates' / 'approval gate' don't fully exist yet in the codebase: this task does not introduce them — it surfaces whatever DOES exist. If a real mode is missing entirely from the bot, file a separate bug; don't fake it in the playground.

## Required: volume control during the live session

In the live session UI, while the user is talking to the bot:

- A visible volume slider that adjusts speaker (bot output) volume in real time.
- A mic-input level indicator so the user knows their voice is being captured.
- A mute toggle (mic + speaker independent).
- The volume setting persists across reloads of the same session.

## Required: re-open / re-attach to a live session from the session page

If the user closes the playground tab while a session is live, they currently lose access to it. Required:

- The session detail page detects when its session is still 'live' (server-side: WebRTC transport still open, container or transport active).
- A 'Reopen playground' (or 'Rejoin') button on the session page that re-mounts the live UI for that session — same controls, same audio routing, same in-flight conversation context.
- If the underlying transport has timed out / been closed, the button gracefully transitions to an 'end + restart' option rather than 500ing.
- Closing the playground tab does NOT terminate the session unless the user explicitly clicks End — closing is just disconnect-from-this-tab.

## Required: 'good UI interface'

The user explicitly asked for the UI to actually be good — not a placeholder. Requirements:

- A clear visual distinction between idle / listening / thinking / speaking states so the user always knows what the bot is doing.
- Live transcript on the left or top, controls on the right (or below), audio output state always visible.
- Provider / mode / template currently in effect shown as small chips so the user can verify the configuration without leaving the live view.
- Responsive layout — desktop primary, tablet should not break.
- Empty / error states designed (no console-error-only failures).

Don't over-engineer; do meet the bar that this is a real first-class surface.

## Out of scope

- Building the underlying decision modes themselves — only exposing them in the playground.
- Multi-user playground (a second human joining the session).
- Recording / exporting the playground conversation (covered by activity log work in Johnny-ckz.7).

## Acceptance criteria

1. User clicks Start in a playground session, speaks, and HEARS the bot reply through their speakers. Verified by evaluate_script against the audio element.
2. Playground configuration UI lets the user pick: template, decision mode (auto / approval / etc — whatever the real bot supports), TTS / STT / LLM overrides, persona, custom system prompt, optional context injection.
3. Switching decision mode in the playground drives the same code paths the real bot uses (no playground-only fork).
4. Volume slider in the live UI adjusts bot audio in real time; mic level indicator and mute toggles work.
5. Closing the playground tab leaves the session live (verified by host-side docker ps or session-state check); reopening the session detail page shows a 'Reopen' button that re-mounts the live UI on the same in-flight session.
6. The UI clearly conveys idle / listening / thinking / speaking states.
7. Per-session provider/mode/template overrides do NOT mutate global settings (verified by checking providers page after End).
8. Every behavior above is validated via chrome-devtools MCP with screenshots in the PR.

## Testing approach — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

Per the AGENTS.md top rule and per [[validate-in-browser-live-chat-live-talking-johnny-ckz-6-end-to-end-via-chrome-devtools-mcp-pure-verification-file-follow-up-bugs-for-any-gap]] (Johnny-ckz.10) — every UI behavior below must be exercised in the real browser via chrome-devtools MCP, with captured artifacts:

- **Audio works**: start a session, drive a user turn, evaluate_script to confirm audio element currentTime advances and muted=false; list_network_requests to confirm an audio stream is open; screenshot the live session with the 'speaking' indicator on.
- **Template + mode picker**: navigate to playground, take_snapshot of the configuration form, confirm template / mode / override / persona / prompt / context fields all present. Pick approval mode, drive a turn, assert approval gating UI appears (the same one the real bot uses).
- **Volume control**: drag the volume slider via evaluate_script or mcp__chrome-devtools__fill; evaluate_script to confirm the audio element's volume property changes.
- **Mic indicator + mute**: drive audio in, confirm the level indicator moves; click mute, confirm the WebRTC track is disabled (getSenders()[*].track.enabled === false).
- **Tab-close survival + reopen**: start a session, mcp__chrome-devtools__close_page (or close the tab), confirm via host docker ps + an API call that the session is still live; open the session detail page in a new tab, click Reopen, confirm the live UI mounts and the conversation continues from where it was.
- **State indicators**: take_snapshot mid-thinking and mid-speaking, assert the state badge / animation in the DOM reflects the right state.
- **Override scope isolation**: pick non-default TTS / STT / LLM in the playground, end the session, navigate to providers page, evaluate_script to confirm globals unchanged.

Screenshots of every check above must be embedded in the PR description.

## Related

- Blocks / blocked-by [[bot-sessions-schema-drift-orm-expects-source-and-playground-overrides-columns-that-don-t-exist-worker-monitor-plus-sessions-active-both-500]] (Johnny-ckz.9) — must be fixed first.
- [[in-browser-voice-text-chat-with-the-bot-per-event-try-with-bot-button-plus-standalone-playground]] (Johnny-ckz.6) — original feature.
- [[validate-in-browser-live-chat-live-talking-johnny-ckz-6-end-to-end-via-chrome-devtools-mcp-pure-verification-file-follow-up-bugs-for-any-gap]] (Johnny-ckz.10) — this task is what Johnny-ckz.10's validation pass should have surfaced; treat the two as collaborators on closing the loop on Johnny-ckz.6.
- [[active-session-leave-now-button-ui-marks-session-ended-but-bot-stays-in-the-google-meet]] (Johnny-ajc) — same end-session contract; reuse the leave teardown so we don't repeat that bug.
design: Audio bug: investigate audio element wiring, WebRTC receivers + inbound RTP stats, sample rate / codec mismatch, browser autoplay policy (start audio on user gesture). Configuration: surface, do not invent — every mode shown must map to an existing real-bot code path. Override scope: per-session override layer on top of the provider registry, never mutates active selection. Reopen: session-detail UI checks server-side session liveness, mounts the same live UI component, reuses the same WebRTC token/transport. Close-tab survival: tab close releases the local peer connection but does not terminate the session row; only explicit End does. UI states: derive from a single session-state machine the live UI subscribes to.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Audio plays — user speaks in playground and hears the bot reply through speakers (chrome-devtools MCP confirms audio.currentTime advances). (2) Configuration UI exposes template + decision mode (auto/approval/etc — every mode the real bot supports) + TTS/STT/LLM overrides + persona + custom system prompt + optional context injection. (3) Switching mode drives the same real-bot code paths (no fork). (4) Volume slider, mic-level indicator, and independent mic/speaker mute toggles all work in real time. (5) Closing the playground tab leaves the session live; session detail page offers a working 'Reopen' button that re-mounts the live UI on the same session. (6) Idle/listening/thinking/speaking states are visually clear. (7) Provider/mode/template overrides remain session-scoped (no global mutation). (8) Every check above validated via chrome-devtools MCP with PR screenshots.

title: bot_sessions schema drift: ORM expects 'source' and 'playground_overrides' columns that don't exist — worker monitor + /sessions/active both 500
description:
## Why this exists

The SQLAlchemy ORM model for bot_sessions now references two columns that do not exist in the live Postgres schema:

- bot_sessions.source
- bot_sessions.playground_overrides

Postgres raises UndefinedColumn on every SELECT that the ORM generates against this table, which means **the entire bot is non-functional**:

- worker-1: run_container_monitor_pass → monitor_session_containers → SELECT crashes. The container monitor cannot run at all, so spawned meet-worker containers are not being state-tracked or pruned.
- api-1: GET /sessions/active returns HTTP 500. The UI cannot list any active session.

Severity = P0: this is total outage of session-related functionality. Anything that touches bot_sessions (which is almost everything) is broken until this is fixed.

## What happened

The user noted this started 'just right after we added the feature to talk to bot before meeting' — i.e. the in-browser playground / 'Try with bot' work tracked under [[in-browser-voice-text-chat-with-the-bot-per-event-try-with-bot-button-plus-standalone-playground]] (Johnny-ckz.6). Both of the missing columns map cleanly to that feature:

- source — needed to distinguish a real meeting session from a playground / 'Try with bot' session (the same epic explicitly required this badge in the session list).
- playground_overrides — needed to persist the session-scoped persona / provider overrides from a playground session.

The model was updated to add the two columns, but the Alembic migration that adds them to the live DB was either not created, not run on startup, or silently failed. Either way the live schema does not match the model.

## Reproduction

Visible right now in the running stack:

- Hit GET /sessions/active → 500 (logged stack ends in UndefinedColumn: column bot_sessions.source does not exist).
- Tail docker compose logs worker → repeated UndefinedColumn crashes from app/worker.py:267 → app/services/docker_launcher.py:680.

Exact failing SQL from the logs:

```
SELECT bot_sessions.id, bot_sessions.meeting_config_id, bot_sessions.source,
       bot_sessions.status, bot_sessions.container_name, bot_sessions.started_at,
       bot_sessions.ended_at, bot_sessions.logs, bot_sessions.error_reason,
       bot_sessions.playground_overrides, bot_sessions.created_at, bot_sessions.updated_at
FROM bot_sessions
WHERE bot_sessions.status IN (, ) AND bot_sessions.container_name IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY bot_sessions.id
```

## Fix shape (for whoever picks it up)

1. Find or create the Alembic migration that introduces source and playground_overrides on bot_sessions. If it exists in the repo but did not run, figure out why (failed during alembic upgrade head? Was the api/worker container started before the migration ran?).
2. Ship a migration that is **idempotent** against the current half-applied state — handle both 'columns already exist' and 'columns missing' cleanly.
3. Decide sane defaults for existing rows: e.g. source defaults to 'calendar' (or whatever value the model maps real-meeting sessions to), playground_overrides is NULL.
4. Run the migration on the live local stack and verify GET /sessions/active returns 200 and the worker monitor loop runs without errors.
5. Add a regression check so this class of drift fails fast at startup — e.g. on app boot, run alembic upgrade head and then a lightweight 'model vs DB' diff that aborts if a mapped column is missing.

## Acceptance criteria

1. GET /sessions/active returns 200 against the live local stack.
2. docker compose logs worker shows the container monitor pass running cleanly with no UndefinedColumn errors over a 5-minute window.
3. The Alembic migration is reversible (downgrade removes both columns).
4. Existing bot_sessions rows pre-migration get sensible defaults — no NULL constraint violations, no broken FK references.
5. A startup guard (boot-time alembic check + model/DB diff) is in place so a future model change without a migration fails loud at startup instead of crashing at first query.

## Testing approach — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

Per the AGENTS.md top rule:

- Open the session list page in chrome-devtools MCP and confirm it loads (currently 500s into the UI as well, presumably).
- list_network_requests and assert /sessions/active returned 200.
- Drive a real session through to 'joined' and confirm the new columns get populated as expected (source set, playground_overrides NULL for a real-meeting session, populated for a playground session).
- Screenshot the working session list in the PR description.
- Tail the worker logs for 5 minutes after the migration runs and confirm zero UndefinedColumn errors.

## Related

- [[in-browser-voice-text-chat-with-the-bot-per-event-try-with-bot-button-plus-standalone-playground]] (Johnny-ckz.6) — the feature whose model change introduced the drift. The session-source badge requirement from .6's acceptance is what motivates the source column.
design: Add Alembic migration adding the two columns with safe defaults (source default = 'calendar' or whatever maps to a real-meeting session; playground_overrides nullable JSON). Make the migration idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS) so it works against the half-applied current state. On app boot run alembic upgrade head; after that, do a quick mapped-table column diff and refuse to start if a model column is missing from the DB — that turns this class of bug into a boot-time crash instead of a runtime crash on first query.
acceptance_criteria: (1) GET /sessions/active returns 200. (2) Worker monitor pass runs cleanly for ≥5 minutes with no UndefinedColumn errors. (3) Migration is reversible and idempotent against the current half-applied state. (4) Existing bot_sessions rows get sensible defaults (no NULL constraint violations). (5) A boot-time guard catches future model-vs-DB drift and aborts startup loud, not at first query. (6) Validation includes chrome-devtools MCP screenshot of a working session list, and a 5-minute clean worker log tail.

title: Local Piper follow-up: voice catalog fetcher fails on HF 307 redirect, plus model dirs must move to host bind mounts (~/.johnny/...)
description:
## Why this exists

The first fix for [[local-piper-tts-smoke-test-fails-with-opaque-exit-code-1-need-easy-voice-install-and-real-error-surfacing]] (Johnny-4c0) shipped, but the user-facing flow STILL doesn't work end-to-end. Two distinct problems are blocking a user from successfully picking a Piper voice and hearing it speak:

### Problem 1 — Voice catalog browser is broken (bug)

Clicking the voice browser surfaces:

> failed to fetch piper voice catalog: Redirect response '307 Temporary Redirect' for url 'https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices/resolve/main/voices.json' Redirect location: '/api/resolve-cache/models/rhasspy/piper-voices/b710b0ba0740da88dc36e1ab8fa6b310d43a3a48/voices.json?...'

Diagnosis: the HTTP client fetching the catalog is not following redirects. Hugging Face's resolve endpoint 307-redirects to its CDN-cached blob URL by design — this is normal and expected behavior, not an HF outage. The fetcher needs to follow redirects (e.g. httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=True) or equivalent).

Without this, the 'browse voices' UI is dead-on-arrival — the user has no path to discover and install a voice from the UI.

### Problem 2 — Model dirs are unreachable from the host (UX bug)

Piper voice models and Whisper STT models currently live inside named Docker volumes:
- /var/lib/johnny/piper-models  ← named volume johnny_piper_models
- /var/lib/johnny/whisper-models  ← named volume johnny_whisper_models

This makes it impossible for a user to drop a voice file in manually (the obvious workaround when an auto-installer is broken). `docker cp` works but is awkward, requires knowing the container ID, and breaks every time the container is rebuilt.

Required change: switch to host bind mounts under the user's home directory:
- ~/.johnny/piper-models → mounts at /var/lib/johnny/piper-models
- ~/.johnny/whisper-models → mounts at /var/lib/johnny/whisper-models

run.sh should create those directories on first boot (idempotent mkdir -p) so the very first run does not error.

Effects this needs to handle:
- docker-compose.yml volume definitions for the api and worker services
- The per-session meet-worker containers spawned via the Docker SDK — today they mount the named volumes by name (see JOHNNY_MEET_WORKER_PIPER_VOLUME / JOHNNY_MEET_WORKER_WHISPER_VOLUME in docker-compose.yml and the launcher in backend/app/services/docker_launcher.py). These need to mount the host paths instead.
- Migration: existing users with files in the old named volumes should not silently lose them. At minimum, surface a clear note in the changelog / README; ideally run.sh detects the old volumes and prints a one-liner docker cp migration command.

Out of scope for this issue: applying the same treatment to google_auth_state or postgres_data. Only the two model dirs the user needs to read/write from the host.

## A proper real test (mandatory)

The earlier fix attempt likely passed unit tests against a mocked HF response, which is why the 307 wasn't caught. This fix MUST include:

1. An integration test that hits the real Hugging Face URL (https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices/resolve/main/voices.json) and asserts the catalog parses to a non-empty voice list. Mark it as a network test (e.g. pytest marker) so CI can skip it offline if needed, but it MUST run locally before claiming the fix works.
2. An end-to-end smoke: from a clean ~/.johnny (no models cached), open the UI, browse the voice catalog, pick a voice, install it, hit Test, hear sound back. Document the manual run in the PR description.

No mocks in the integration test. The whole reason the earlier fix didn't catch this is that the mock pretended HF returns 200 directly.

## Acceptance

1. Voice catalog browser loads a non-empty list of voices in the UI against a live HF connection.
2. Installing a voice from the browser drops the .onnx + .onnx.json into ~/.johnny/piper-models on the host, where the user can see them with ls.
3. After install, hitting Test produces real audio (TTS smoke OK — N bytes) without any terminal commands.
4. Same UX works for Whisper models in ~/.johnny/whisper-models (host-visible, no docker cp).
5. ./run.sh on a fresh checkout creates ~/.johnny/piper-models and ~/.johnny/whisper-models if missing and brings the stack up cleanly.
6. Meet-worker containers spawned for a real session see the same host-bound model dirs (verified by joining a meeting and confirming Piper TTS plays).
7. A pytest integration test exercises the real HF voices.json endpoint and is part of the test suite.

## Related

- Follows up on [[local-piper-tts-smoke-test-fails-with-opaque-exit-code-1-need-easy-voice-install-and-real-error-surfacing]] (Johnny-4c0) — that issue's first-pass fix shipped but did not deliver a working end-to-end flow.
design: HTTP client must follow redirects (httpx: follow_redirects=True). Replace docker-compose.yml named volumes piper_models and whisper_models with host bind mounts to $HOME/.johnny/piper-models and $HOME/.johnny/whisper-models. Mirror the change in docker_launcher.py so per-session meet-workers mount the same host paths instead of the named volumes (today read from JOHNNY_MEET_WORKER_PIPER_VOLUME / WHISPER_VOLUME env). run.sh: mkdir -p ~/.johnny/{piper-models,whisper-models} before the build. Detect legacy named volumes and print a docker cp migration hint.
acceptance_criteria: Voice browser loads a real HF catalog with no 307 error. Installed voices land in ~/.johnny/piper-models on the host (visible via ls). Test button produces audio with zero terminal use. Whisper models work the same way via ~/.johnny/whisper-models. run.sh creates these dirs idempotently on first boot. Meet-worker containers see the same host-bound dirs. A pytest integration test hits the real HF voices.json and is checked in.
notes:
## Validation requirement (mandatory)

All end-to-end / UI verification for this ticket MUST be performed through the real browser via the chrome-devtools MCP server (mcp__chrome-devtools__*). Do NOT use claude-in-chrome (see /Users/nikita/.claude/rules/common/browser-automation.md) and do NOT rely on visual mocks or screenshot-by-eye claims.

Concretely:
- Open the provider settings page in Chrome via chrome-devtools MCP (new_page / navigate_page).
- Drive the voice catalog browser (take_snapshot, click) and confirm the network request to huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices/resolve/main/voices.json returns a 2xx after redirect follow (list_network_requests + get_network_request).
- Install a voice through the UI and verify the .onnx file actually lands in ~/.johnny/piper-models on the host (shell check, post-install).
- Click Test on the configured Local Piper provider and confirm 'TTS smoke OK — N bytes' is rendered in the UI; capture a screenshot (take_screenshot) for the PR description.
- Repeat the install + Test loop with the stack restarted to confirm the host bind mount actually persisted the file.
- Do the analogous Whisper flow if any UI surface exists for it.

Acceptance is NOT met until each of the above has been executed live in chrome-devtools MCP, not asserted from code alone.

title: Local Piper TTS: smoke test fails with opaque 'exit code 1' — need easy voice install + real error surfacing
description:
User configured Local Piper provider with voice_id 'en_US-amy-medium' (and 'en_US-john-medium'); /test and /sample both fail with 'piper exited with non-zero code 1' and no further detail.

Observed root causes during investigation (backend/app/providers/piper_tts.py):

1. piper subprocess is spawned with stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL (line 278), so the real reason (missing model file, missing libonnxruntime, missing piper-phonemize espeak-ng data, etc.) is thrown away. The user only sees 'exited with non-zero code 1'.
2. The 'piper' CLI binary is not actually present in johnny-api-1 (which piper -> not found, pip show piper-tts -> not found) despite backend/Dockerfile line 24 passing --extra local-tts to uv sync. So even with a valid voice file the smoke call cannot succeed in the API container today.
3. There is no auto-download / install helper for voices. The user has to manually drop <voice>.onnx + <voice>.onnx.json into the johnny_piper_models volume. Only en_US-john-medium is present right now; en_US-amy-medium isn't, so that smoke call would fail file-not-found if piper were even installed.

What the user needs (their words: 'It should be easy for a person to use this Piper model'):
- Real error message in the UI when piper fails — capture stderr and surface it in TestResult.detail.
- One-click voice install from huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices: pick voice from a list, auto-download .onnx + .onnx.json into the model_dir volume.
- Verify piper-tts actually installs into the api image; if --extra local-tts is silently dropped by uv, fix the extras config or pin the dep into the main deps.
- Pre-flight check on Test: model file exists at expected path, piper binary on PATH, libonnxruntime present, espeak-ng phoneme data available.

Acceptance: from a fresh checkout, a user can open the Local Piper provider in the UI, see a list of available voices, pick one, click Install, then click Test and get 'TTS smoke OK — N bytes' without touching a terminal.
design: Capture piper stderr to a bounded buffer (stderr=PIPE, drain in background) and include the last ~2KB in TTSError so it propagates into TestResult.detail. Add a /providers/{id}/voices endpoint that lists huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices and a /providers/{id}/voices/{name}/install endpoint that downloads to model_dir. Pre-flight check before spawning subprocess: model file exists, binary on PATH.
acceptance_criteria: From a fresh checkout, user can open Local Piper provider in UI, pick a voice from a fetched list, click Install, then Test succeeds without any terminal commands. On failure, the UI shows the real piper stderr (not just 'exit code 1').

title: Voice interrupt doesn't actually work end-to-end: bot ignores user speech mid-utterance (reopens Johnny-har / Johnny-di9)
description:
## Why this exists

Johnny-har (STT keeps running during bot speech) and Johnny-di9 (voice-triggered barge-in) were both closed as 'Completed by agent', but in a real Google Meet session (session 154 at http://localhost:5173/sessions/154) the feature does not work:

- The bot keeps talking even while the user speaks over it
- The user asked Johnny to tell about himself; Johnny spoke for 18+ seconds with no ability to interrupt
- Attempts to interrupt mid-utterance were ignored
- The transcript and barge-in detection / interrupt decision are not actually running in parallel with TTS playback

The previous closures were premature — code may exist but the integrated behavior is broken.

## What needs to happen

Build it so that all of these processes run truly in parallel during a live meeting, and the feedback loop is fast:

1. **Inbound audio capture**: never paused while the bot is speaking or thinking
2. **STT (transcription)**: streams partial transcripts in real time, with low latency (~hundreds of ms target), regardless of pipeline state
3. **Interrupt-intent classifier**: every incoming partial transcript while bot is talking is evaluated immediately — does the user want to interrupt / correct / redirect?
4. **TTS playback**: can be cut within ~200ms of an interrupt decision
5. **Decision logic**: clear, simple, debuggable — not a tangle of mutexes/queues that block one stage on another

End-to-end requirement: user says 'hey Johnny stop' (or any clear interrupt-intent utterance) while the bot is in a long answer → TTS cuts within ~200ms → bot yields the floor or processes the redirect.

## Evidence to use

- Session 154 (http://localhost:5173/sessions/154) — the user asked Johnny to introduce himself, Johnny spoke for 18.7s (agent_utterances.id=83), user could not interrupt
- Pull docker logs from meet-worker-session-154 (or the next failing session) to see whether STT partials are arriving while TTS is playing, whether interrupt() is called, and what latency looks like
- Check that the pipeline doesn't hold a lock between TTS playback and STT consumption

## Acceptance

- In a real Google Meet session, mid-bot-utterance, the user says 'hey Johnny stop' → TTS cuts within ~200ms
- Mid-bot-utterance, user says 'wait, what about X?' → TTS cuts, bot answers X
- Cough / background noise / unrelated participant chatter does NOT cut the bot
- Every human utterance during bot speech still lands in transcript_chunks (no gaps)
- Bot utterance is logged in agent_utterances with actual played duration (truncated on interrupt)
- Reproducible: same behavior across at least 3 consecutive test sessions

## Related (previously closed but evidently incomplete)

- [[stt-transcription-of-participants-must-never-pause-while-bot-is-speaking-or-thinking]] (Johnny-har)
- [[voice-triggered-barge-in-user-can-interrupt-the-bot-mid-utterance-by-speaking]] (Johnny-di9)

title: Bot joined but voice pipeline never runs: no transcription, no decisions, no speech, no audio bridge
description:
## Reproduction (2026-06-06)

Bot now successfully joins the Test Meet (Johnny-ckz.1 is closed). Verified:
- bot_sessions.status flips to joined
- nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi appears as a participant
- Container stays alive in-meeting

But the bot does **nothing** once in the meeting:
- No transcript_chunks rows persisted as the user speaks
- No agent_decisions rows from the router LLM
- No agent_utterances rows from TTS
- No 'agent_spoke' events in /sessions/<id> live view
- Meeting audio is never captured (PulseAudio capture stream not started)
- Bot's virtual mic never plays anything (PulseAudio loopback unused)
- The Johnny live session view (panes for transcript/decisions/utterances) stays empty

## Why

The meet-worker bootstrap (Johnny-ckz.1) currently:
1. Runs selfcheck
2. Loads storage_state
3. Opens Chromium, joins meeting
4. **Idles until SIGTERM**

It NEVER:
- Wires the MeetAudioBridge to capture from PulseAudio's johnny_speaker.monitor
- Wires the playback path to feed agent audio into johnny_mic_loopback
- Instantiates the VoicePipeline with VAD + STT + Router + (optional Answer + TTS)
- Reads JOHNNY_MODE / JOHNNY_INSTRUCTIONS / JOHNNY_CONTEXT / JOHNNY_PROVIDER_CONFIG into a PipelineConfig
- Connects sinks (TranscriptSink → DB row insert, DecisionSink → DB row insert, UtteranceSink → DB row insert)
- Forwards browser console / Playwright / pipeline events into the container logs

## Required outcome

Part A: Excessive logging
- Every Playwright lifecycle event (browser launched, context created, page open, navigation, network request to meet.google.com, console message, page error, page closed) logged with session_id
- Every audio bridge event: parec subprocess spawn, pacat subprocess spawn, frame counts, queue saturation, subprocess exit code
- Every pipeline event: VAD speech-start / speech-end, STT partial / final, router LLM call (request, latency, response), decision outcome, TTS request, agent audio frames
- Browser console messages from meet.google.com forwarded to docker logs

Part B: Wire the voice pipeline
- Wire MeetAudioBridge for capture (PulseAudio source) and playback (PulseAudio loopback sink)
- Instantiate VoicePipeline with the provider config and mode passed in env vars
- Connect transcript / decision / utterance sinks that publish events via RedisEventBus (the existing pipeline already does this — the API persists via existing handlers)
- Run the pipeline alongside the existing in-meeting idle loop

## Acceptance

- [ ] meet-worker container logs show per-frame VAD/STT/router/TTS activity in real time
- [ ] User speaks in Meet → transcript_chunks rows appear within ~2s
- [ ] In suggest mode, AgentDecision rows show should_speak decisions
- [ ] In limited auto-speak mode, bot speaks the canned reply through the virtual mic so the user hears it in Meet
- [ ] Live session view in the Johnny UI populates the three panes
- [ ] Stopping the session cleanly tears down the pipeline + audio bridge + browser

title: Bot join hangs at 'Johnny is joining — session #N': bot never appears in Meet, Active sessions stays 0, no logs
description:
## Reproduction (2026-06-06, reported by user)

1. User (`nikita.rabykin@gmail.com`) joins a real Google Meet in their own browser.
2. In the Johnny control panel, user opens the Calendar view and selects that meeting.
3. UI displays `Johnny is joining — session #47.`
4. **Expected**: Johnny (`nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi`) appears as a participant in the Meet room within ~90s.
5. **Actual**:
   - Bot never appears in the Meet room.
   - `Active sessions` panel stays at 0.
   - Nothing meaningful surfaces in any log (`docker compose logs`, `bot_sessions.logs`, UI).
   - Session is silently stuck on `joining` forever.

## Why this is a separate bead

`Johnny-ckz` is the parent epic and bundles both Part A (this bug) and Part B (the `python -m johnny.e2e` harness). This bead pins Part A as a discrete, reproducible bug so it has its own status, assignee, and close trail — and so the harness work in Part B doesn't blur into bug-fix tracking.

## Scope

This bead covers Part A only: surface what is happening on the join path and fix whatever stage is silently swallowing the failure. The harness (Part B) and the lived-journey validation (`Johnny-pdf`) remain separate beads under the same epic.

## Likely culprits to investigate (not yet narrowed)

- Scheduler dispatched the session but never spawned the meet-worker container (check `docker ps -a` for an exited `meet-worker-session-47` and its tail logs in `bot_sessions.logs`).
- meet-worker container spawned but crashed early (Xvfb, PulseAudio, Chromium flags, faster-whisper / piper model dirs not mounted).
- Playwright opened Meet but Google sign-in failed silently (cookies/oauth tokens not seeded into the per-session profile).
- Meet "Ask to join" gate hit — host never approved, scheduler never noticed.
- Stuck *before* dispatch: `bot_sessions` row stayed in `pending` and the scheduler pass never picked it up.
- Worker container itself was crashlooping for ~7h on `ModuleNotFoundError: johnny` (fixed via stale-image rebuild + `run.sh --build` on 2026-06-06) — even after that fix the symptom persists per this reproduction.

## Required outcome

- Every join-path stage emits a structured log line with `session_id` (scheduler dispatch, worker container spawn, Xvfb up, PulseAudio up, Playwright nav, Google sign-in, "Join now" click, bot_sessions.status transitions, audio bridge attach).
- Logs are visible in BOTH `docker compose logs` AND `bot_sessions.logs`.
- UI live session view surfaces the most recent failure stage rather than perpetual "joining".
- Root cause identified and fixed; reproduction above produces `bot_sessions.status = joined` and the bot is visible in the Meet participant list.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Reproduce the failure with current `main` and capture the structured logs of each stage reached.
- [ ] Identify the stage that fails silently and the root cause.
- [ ] Fix the root cause AND add the structured logging so future regressions surface.
- [ ] UI surfaces the failure stage when join fails — no silent perpetual "joining".
- [ ] Reproduction above results in bot visible in Meet, `bot_sessions.status = joined`, transcript bridge attached.
- [ ] Reproduce a second time after the fix to confirm it sticks; attach evidence to this bead.

## Test setup (per parent epic)

- Bot identity: `nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi` (role=bot, connected in Johnny app)
- Observer / driver: `nikita.rabykin@gmail.com` (in Meet via standard browser)
- Test event: single calendar event titled "Test", owned by user account, both accounts invited, Meet link attached.

## Notes

Confirmed reproducible against the freshly-rebuilt stack on 2026-06-06 (api/worker/frontend/postgres/redis all healthy after the worker `ModuleNotFoundError: johnny` fix). The join bug is independent of the worker stale-image issue.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce the failure once with structured logging in place, identify the failing stage, fix the root cause, surface the failure stage in UI, then re-run the reproduction and confirm bot visible in Meet and bot_sessions.status=joined.
notes:
Spawned 2026-06-06 from user reproduction. Linked under Johnny-ckz as Part A. Worker container ModuleNotFoundError was a separate concurrent bug, already fixed via stale-image rebuild; this bead is purely the join-path failure.

## 2026-06-06 — confirmed root cause

**The join code is never invoked.** The image's default CMD is the selfcheck, and the scheduler doesn't override it.

Evidence:
- \`backend/Dockerfile.meet-worker:63\` — \`CMD ["python", "-m", "johnny.meet_worker.selfcheck"]\`.
- \`backend/johnny/meet_worker/selfcheck.py\` — checks PulseAudio sink/source presence, prints \`self-check OK\`, exits 0. No join, no Playwright, no audio bridge.
- \`backend/johnny/meet_worker/meet_join.py:377\` — \`async def join_meeting(...)\` exists (real implementation, plus \`MeetJoiner\` class). No \`__main__\`, never imported.
- \`backend/johnny/meet_worker/audio_bridge.py\` — \`MeetAudioBridge\` class exists. Same: no \`__main__\`, never imported.
- \`backend/app/services/docker_launcher.py:274-297\` — \`DockerContainerLauncher.start()\` calls \`client.containers.run(self._image, **run_kwargs)\`. \`run_kwargs\` has \`detach\`, \`name\`, \`environment\`, \`labels\`, \`restart_policy\`, optional \`volumes\` and \`network\`. **No \`command=\`**. So the container uses the Dockerfile's default CMD = selfcheck.

Result at runtime: scheduler row \`bot_sessions\` flips \`pending\` → ??? based on whatever the container-monitor pass interprets the exit-0 selfcheck as, container is removed by the prune pass within an hour, no Playwright ever opens, no Meet ever joined. UI shows "Johnny is joining — session #N" because that's the status the scheduler set right before \`launcher.start()\` returned; nothing ever advances it because nothing is running.

## Fix sketch

The minimum viable fix has two coupled pieces — pick one of these directions:

### Option A — runtime entrypoint module (recommended)
Write a new \`johnny.meet_worker.main\` (or similar) that:
1. Reads \`session_id\`, Meet URL, identity tokens, mode, and provider configs from environment vars supplied by the launcher.
2. Logs a structured \`stage=startup\` line with \`session_id\`.
3. Calls \`join_meeting(...)\` from \`meet_join.py\`, logs \`stage=joining\` / \`stage=joined\` / \`stage=join_failed\` with the specific failure reason.
4. Wires \`MeetAudioBridge\` to PulseAudio sinks once joined.
5. Mounts the voice pipeline (VAD → STT → router → answer → TTS) per session mode.
6. Heartbeats \`bot_sessions.status\` and logs to \`bot_sessions.logs\` at every stage transition.

Then either:
- Change \`Dockerfile.meet-worker\` CMD to \`["python", "-m", "johnny.meet_worker.main"]\`, **or**
- Have \`DockerContainerLauncher.start()\` pass \`command=["python", "-m", "johnny.meet_worker.main"]\` so selfcheck remains the bare-image default for \`docker run\` debugging.

### Option B — launcher dispatches existing functions
Add \`command=\` to \`docker_launcher.start()\` that boots a thin shim importing and awaiting \`join_meeting()\` + \`MeetAudioBridge\` directly. Cleaner if you don't want a new package module, messier if the shim grows.

Either way, the structured-logging requirement from the parent epic still has to be honoured at every stage so the next time this regresses it's visible in \`docker compose logs\` and \`bot_sessions.logs\`.

## How this slipped past "Completed by agent"

- \`Johnny-pdf\` (master e2e) closed without ever spawning a meet-worker container — its Phase 0 readiness audit only checked \`api/frontend/postgres/redis\` health, never invoked the launcher.
- \`Johnny-kgc.20\` (US-020 Google Meet join automation) and \`Johnny-kgc.30\` (US-030 Per-session container spawning) both closed — but \`launcher.start()\` plus \`Dockerfile.meet-worker\` CMD = selfcheck means neither task actually proved a bot joins a Meet. Both probably warrant reopening or a follow-up bead.
close_reason: Root causes (all fixed): (1) meet-worker container CMD only ran selfcheck — no entry point invoked join_meeting(). (2) Spawned containers used default bridge network so could not reach redis service. (3) DockerContainerLauncher passed no REDIS_URL env. (4) No Redis-to-DB subscriber persisted SessionStatusChanged events — DB stayed stuck on joining. (5) No storage_state mount for Playwright sign-in. (6) Volumes used bare names so meet-worker mounted fresh empty volumes instead of shared johnny_<name> compose volumes. (7) join_meeting() closed the browser immediately after returning — bot left the meeting. (8) _wait_for_joined_state treated 'Join now selectors disappeared' as success — silently misreported success on browser crash/disconnect. Fixed by adding johnny.meet_worker.bootstrap with structured stage logging, johnny.tools.seed_auth_state CLI for one-time Google sign-in, open_meeting_session async context manager that holds browser open + uses positive in-meeting verification, app.services.session_status_subscriber for Redis->DB persistence, and surfacing error_reason in the UI. Verified end-to-end: session 123 transitions scheduled->joining->joined, bot account nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi appears in Meet room as participant, screenshot captured of in-meeting state. Follow-up bead Johnny-4ph filed for UI-based sign-in trigger (no CLI helper).

title: Structural consistency: every page shares one header + menu + wrapper + container — enforce shared layout primitives across the app (REQUIRES PLAN MODE)
description:

description:

Go through every page in the app, audit visual quality, fix what's broken. Read `PRODUCT.md` + `DESIGN.md` and use the `impeccable` skill to drive each fix.

title: STT provider catalog UI with per-provider Test button (mic record + transcribe + latency/cost)
description:
## Why
Right now there is no UI to browse, configure, or sample STT providers — users can't tell which one works best for their setup. Mirror the existing Piper voice-catalog UX shipped in Johnny-ckz.5.

## Scope
- New settings route (e.g. `/settings/stt`) listing every installed STT provider with: name, type (local/cloud), streaming-capable flag, model list (where applicable), API-key field (cloud), language picker.
- Per-provider/per-model **Test** button: records 5 seconds from user mic, posts to backend, displays transcript + latency (ms) + estimated cost (cloud providers report it; local providers show $0).
- Provider + model selection persists to user prefs; reloads on next visit.
- Initial release lists existing providers (`faster_whisper`, `deepgram`, `elevenlabs`, `openai_realtime`). New providers from Johnny-stt.1 and Johnny-stt.4 plug in as they ship.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/settings/stt` route lists all installed STT providers with their model count.
- [ ] Selecting a provider reveals its config form (key, model, language).
- [ ] Test button records mic for ~5s, posts to backend, displays transcript within 10s.
- [ ] Latency (ms) and provider-reported cost rendered next to the transcript.
- [ ] Selection is saved and re-loads on next visit.
- [ ] Empty / failing provider shows a usable error toast — not a stack trace.

## Validation
- Backend: integration test for the `/stt/test` endpoint with a mocked provider.
- Frontend: component test for the Test button state machine (idle → recording → uploading → done).
- **Browser (chrome-devtools MCP):** navigate /settings/stt → snapshot → select faster_whisper (or Parakeet once shipped) → grant mic → click Test → wait for `[data-stt-result]` → assert non-empty transcript → screenshot for PR.
