title: Barge-in classifier LLM ReadTimeouts against Ollama Qwen 35B — every timeout is a missed interrupt + log noise
description:
## Why this exists

Validation under [[validate-in-browser-live-chat-live-talking-johnny-ckz-6-end-to-end-via-chrome-devtools-mcp-pure-verification-file-follow-up-bugs-for-any-gap]] (Johnny-ckz.10) found repeated `httpx.ReadTimeout` errors from the **barge-in classifier** during a normal playground session:

```
barge-in classifier failed for session=224 — leaving current response running
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File "/workspace/johnny/voice_pipeline/pipeline.py", line 819, in _maybe_barge_in
    decision = await self._classify_barge_in_intent(transcript)
  File "/workspace/johnny/voice_pipeline/pipeline.py", line 854, in _classify_barge_in_intent
    response = await self.router_llm.chat(...)
  File "/workspace/app/providers/openai_compatible_llm.py", line 274, in chat
    response = await self._client.post(url, json=body, headers=headers)
  ...
httpx.ReadTimeout
```

5+ occurrences over a single ~3-minute session. The configured LLM is "Ollama Qwen No Reason Uncensored" (fredrezones55/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Aggressive:latest, a 35B-parameter Q4_K_M model). On this hardware that model can easily take longer than the default `httpx` read timeout per turn.

When the barge-in classifier ReadTimeouts, the pipeline logs the error and **suppresses the barge-in decision** ("leaving current response running"). This is the right safe fallback when the bot IS actually speaking — but it doesn't fix the underlying latency problem and would still mask real barge-in attempts under [[run-the-two-bot-voice-interrupt-harness-end-to-end-against-real-models-fix-any-bugs-it-surfaces]] (Johnny-ckz.4)'s 500 ms p95 budget.

## Symptoms

1. Real user barge-in (saying "stop") will be missed when the classifier times out — every classifier ReadTimeout is a missed interrupt opportunity.
2. Worker logs are flooded with stacktraces, hiding other issues.
3. May contribute to the broader "bot never replies" symptom in [[playground-audio-path-never-opens-websocket-no-voice-no-bot-replies-johnny-ckz-6-regression]] if the same LLM is used for the conversation reply path.

## Fix shape (do not over-fit)

- The barge-in classifier is meant to be a low-latency router — it should NOT be using the main 35B reply model. Route it to a cheap small model (Llama 3.2 3B / Qwen 2.5 3B / a small distilled classifier) regardless of the user's "active" LLM choice.
- Or: keep the same model but use logit-bias/few-tokens-only sampling with a very short max-tokens to bound classifier latency.
- Independent of the model choice, set an explicit `httpx` timeout for the classifier call that's tighter than today's default — and if it times out, log at WARN (single line) instead of dumping a full traceback every time.

## Acceptance

1. Under load (mic active, free auto-speak mode), no `httpx.ReadTimeout` from the barge-in classifier appears in worker logs over a 5-minute playground session.
2. Worker log noise drops to a single WARN line on classifier-timeout, not a 30-line traceback.
3. Real "stop" barge-in test (drive via chrome-devtools MCP per Johnny-ckz.10 acceptance #4) is recognized and stops the bot within Johnny-ckz.4's p95 budget.

## Source

`johnny/voice_pipeline/pipeline.py:819` (`_maybe_barge_in`) and `_classify_barge_in_intent` at line 854.

title: Playground transcripts label every speaker=null row as 'You' — including STT hallucinations and any non-user rows
description:
## Why this exists

Validation under [[validate-in-browser-live-chat-live-talking-johnny-ckz-6-end-to-end-via-chrome-devtools-mcp-pure-verification-file-follow-up-bugs-for-any-gap]] (Johnny-ckz.10) found that the `/playground` page renders **every** `transcripts` row with `speaker = NULL` as "You", while the `/sessions/{id}` session-detail page correctly renders the same rows as "Speaker".

Concretely, for session 224 the `/playground` UI showed:
```
You — Hello can you hear me?
You — Does Olam A.P.I.
You — amwch ran i'n clo canwys.
You — . . . . . .
You — . . . .
```
…but on `/sessions/224` the same rows render as:
```
user      — Hello can you hear me?
Speaker   — Does Olam A.P.I.
Speaker   — amwch ran i'n clo canwys.
Speaker   — . . . . . .
Speaker   — . . . .
```

Only the first one ("Hello…") has `speaker = "user"` in the DB; the rest have `speaker = NULL` (mostly STT hallucinations and any future bot-side rows that don't carry a `speaker`). Labeling them all as "You" makes the playground conversation nonsensical.

## Fix shape

- Mirror the session-detail UI's labelling logic on the playground:
  - `speaker == "user"` → "You"
  - `speaker == NULL` and not "user" → "Speaker" (or "Bot" if we can disambiguate downstream)
- Consider rejecting any new transcript rows with `speaker = NULL` once the STT silence-hallucination bug is fixed; until then, at minimum do not label them as "You".

## Acceptance

1. On `/playground`, only `speaker = "user"` transcript rows render as "You".
2. All other speakers (`NULL`, `bot`, anything else) render with their correct label, matching `/sessions/{id}`.
3. Verified via chrome-devtools MCP `take_snapshot` showing the conversation feed after the linked STT bug fix.

## Source location

`frontend/src/routes/playground/+page.svelte` — the transcript rendering block defaulting `speaker` to "You".

title: STT hallucinations from silence: faster-whisper produces 'Does Olam A.P.I.', '. . . .', etc. on quiet mic and persists them as transcripts
description:
## Why this exists

Validation under [[validate-in-browser-live-chat-live-talking-johnny-ckz-6-end-to-end-via-chrome-devtools-mcp-pure-verification-file-follow-up-bugs-for-any-gap]] (Johnny-ckz.10) saw the playground accumulate STT garbage transcripts whenever there was no real speech:

- `Does Olam A.P.I.`
- `amwch ran i'n clo canwys.` (Welsh-shaped nonsense)
- `. . . . . .`
- `. . . .`

These are classic faster-whisper hallucinations on silence / low-energy audio frames. They are saved into `transcripts` with `speaker = NULL`, which both (a) pollutes the conversation feed and (b) feeds the decision LLM noise that it then has to suppress (the one decision row produced for session 226 was `should_speak=false` on `. . . .`).

## Reproduction (chrome-devtools MCP trace)

1. `new_page` against `/playground`, click Start (mic gets activated).
2. Type **nothing** — leave the browser tab in a quiet room for ~60 s.
3. `curl /sessions/{id}` shows new rows in `transcripts` every few seconds with `speaker=null` and silence-derived text.
4. On `/playground` these all render as "You" — actively misleading (see linked bug for the labelling half).
5. On `/sessions/{id}` they correctly render as "Speaker" but they still pollute the transcript and waste the decision LLM's tokens.

## Fix shape (do not over-fit)

- Apply a voice activity detection / energy gate before pushing a frame batch through faster-whisper, so pure silence never reaches the model.
- And/or post-filter: faster-whisper has a known set of hallucination phrases ("Thanks for watching", "Subtitles by the Amara.org community", `"...". "..."` patterns, the silence-dot pattern `". . . ."`). Drop transcripts whose text matches the hallucination filter, and/or whose `avg_logprob` / `no_speech_prob` indicates low confidence.
- Use the `condition_on_previous_text=False` and/or `no_speech_threshold` tuning that faster-whisper exposes.
- Whatever the gate is, it should also keep the silence rows out of the `bot_sessions.transcripts` table — even if they slip past the model, do not persist `.....`-shaped rows.

## Acceptance

1. Quiet room, mic on, 60 s of silence → **zero** new transcript rows for the session.
2. Real speech still produces transcripts (verified by typing into the text input or by speaking near the host mic).
3. Decision LLM no longer makes "should_speak=false because the transcript is empty/dots" decisions — the noise never reaches it.
4. Verified via chrome-devtools MCP (start session, wait silently for 60 s, screenshot the empty transcript).

## Evidence artifacts

- DB rows from session 224 and 226 (`/sessions/{id}` REST) showing the dot/Welsh/`Does Olam A.P.I.` transcripts.
- Screenshot `.validation-ckz10-artifacts/04-session-detail-page.png` (12 such rows on session 224).
- Same artifact for session 226 (2 dot rows).

title: Validate in-browser live chat / live talking (Johnny-ckz.6) end-to-end via chrome-devtools MCP — pure verification, file follow-up bugs for any gap
description:
## Why this exists

Johnny-ckz.6 (in-browser voice/text chat with the bot — per-event 'Try with bot' button + standalone playground) was implemented by an agent that **ignored the AGENTS.md top rule** requiring chrome-devtools MCP validation. The feature was marked done without anyone driving it in a real browser. The first visible symptom of that skipped step is already on file as the P0 schema drift in [[bot-sessions-schema-drift-orm-expects-source-and-playground-overrides-columns-that-don-t-exist-worker-monitor-plus-sessions-active-both-500]] (Johnny-ckz.9) — but that is almost certainly not the only thing the implementation skipped past.

This task exists to restore the validation that should have been done in-line, and to surface every other gap so each gap becomes its own follow-up bug. **No implementation work happens here.** Validation-only. If something doesn't work, file a new bug under Johnny-ckz and move on.

## Blocked by

[[bot-sessions-schema-drift-orm-expects-source-and-playground-overrides-columns-that-don-t-exist-worker-monitor-plus-sessions-active-both-500]] (Johnny-ckz.9) — until the schema drift is fixed, /sessions/active returns 500 and validation cannot proceed.

## What to validate (one-to-one with Johnny-ckz.6 acceptance)

Each item below must be exercised in a real browser via chrome-devtools MCP tools (loaded via ToolSearch first). For each, capture the noted artifacts.

### 1. Per-event 'Try with bot' button — opens session in <3s with audible greeting

- mcp__chrome-devtools__new_page against the calendar event detail page.
- mcp__chrome-devtools__take_snapshot — confirm 'Try with bot' button exists and is reachable.
- mcp__chrome-devtools__click the button. Start a wall-clock timer.
- mcp__chrome-devtools__wait_for the session UI to mount. Stop the timer. Must be < 3 s.
- mcp__chrome-devtools__evaluate_script on an audio element to confirm playback started (e.g. audio.currentTime > 0 within a few seconds of session start).
- mcp__chrome-devtools__take_screenshot of the active session.

### 2. Standalone /playground — persona pick, session-scoped overrides, voice + text

- Navigate to /playground.
- take_snapshot and assert the persona picker, override controls, and Start button exist.
- Pick a persona, override the active TTS provider (e.g. Local Piper if not currently active), click Start.
- Drive a voice turn (or text-fallback turn).
- After ending the session, navigate to the providers page and evaluate_script to confirm the **global** active TTS is unchanged.

### 3. Real bot_sessions rows with transcripts and utterances

- After exercising 1 + 2, hit /sessions/<id> for the just-created sessions in chrome-devtools MCP.
- take_snapshot and assert the transcript + utterance panels are populated.

### 4. Interrupts work within Johnny-ckz.4's latency budget

- Drive a user turn that triggers a long bot reply.
- Mid-reply, drive an interrupt ('stop'). Use the Speaker harness from [[run-the-two-bot-voice-interrupt-harness-end-to-end-against-real-models-fix-any-bugs-it-surfaces]] (Johnny-ckz.4) if it is available; otherwise type or play 'stop' manually with timestamps captured.
- evaluate_script on the audio element to confirm playback stopped.
- list_network_requests to capture the timing of the cut.
- Assert the interrupt latency is within the Johnny-ckz.4 budget (500 ms p95).

### 5. Playground sessions are visually distinct in the session list

- Navigate to the session list page.
- take_snapshot and assert there is a visible badge / tag separating playground sessions from real-meeting sessions.
- Screenshot.

### 6. Mic-denied falls back to text-only with no JS errors

- mcp__chrome-devtools__emulate or otherwise simulate a denied microphone permission (or use the browser's permissions UI directly).
- Start a playground session.
- take_snapshot — assert the UI offers a text input and a visible explanation.
- list_console_messages — confirm zero JS errors.
- Complete one text-turn round-trip end-to-end.

### 7. End-session tears down audio cleanly

- After a live playground session, click End.
- evaluate_script: assert no live RTCPeerConnection instances and that navigator.mediaDevices shows the mic is released.
- list_network_requests: confirm no lingering WebSocket / SSE.
- From the host shell, run docker ps --filter name=meet-worker-session and confirm **no** meet-worker container was spawned for this session at any point.

### 8. No meet-worker container for either surface

- During the live runs above, periodically run docker ps on the host and confirm no meet-worker container appears tied to these sessions.

## What to do when something fails

- File a new bug issue under epic Johnny-ckz with: which acceptance bullet failed, the chrome-devtools MCP command sequence that reproduced it, console + network artifacts, and a screenshot.
- Set the new bug's priority based on user-visible impact (P0 if blocking core flow, P1 otherwise).
- **Do not fix anything in this task.** Filing the bug is the whole deliverable per failure.

## Acceptance

1. Every numbered check above is executed via chrome-devtools MCP and the noted artifacts are captured (snapshots, screenshots, console / network captures, timing numbers).
2. A trace log of the validation run — command sequence + per-check verdict (pass / fail / blocked) — is recorded in this issue's notes when validation finishes.
3. Every failure has a corresponding follow-up bug filed under Johnny-ckz, with chrome-devtools MCP-captured evidence.
4. If every check passes, Johnny-ckz.6 is signed off as truly done and this task is closed clean.
5. No code in the application was modified as part of this task — verification only.

## Why this is a separate task and not a re-open of Johnny-ckz.6

The verification needs its own line-item with its own acceptance so it can be audited. It also has to be re-runnable: when Johnny-ckz.6's follow-up bugs land fixes, this validation is the gate they pass through.

## Process note

Going forward, any task that touches a UI must include browser validation IN-LINE during the implementation per the AGENTS.md top rule — not as a separate ticket. This task exists to clean up after a rule that was skipped, not to normalize the pattern of validating later.
design: Validation only — no implementation. Drive each Johnny-ckz.6 acceptance bullet through chrome-devtools MCP tools (loaded via ToolSearch as a first step): new_page, navigate_page, take_snapshot, click, evaluate_script, list_network_requests, list_console_messages, take_screenshot, wait_for, emulate. For each failure, file a new bug under Johnny-ckz with the reproduction sequence and captured artifacts. Blocked until Johnny-ckz.9 fixes the schema drift.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Every numbered acceptance bullet from Johnny-ckz.6 is exercised via chrome-devtools MCP and the captured artifacts (snapshots, screenshots, console/network captures, timing numbers) live in this issue's notes. (2) A pass/fail/blocked verdict per check is recorded. (3) Every failure has a follow-up bug filed under Johnny-ckz with chrome-devtools-MCP-captured evidence. (4) Zero application code is modified as part of this task. (5) If everything passes, Johnny-ckz.6 is signed off and this task closes clean.

title: In-browser voice/text chat with the bot — per-event 'Try with bot' button + standalone playground (no Meet required)
description:
## Why this exists

Right now the only way to talk to Johnny is to schedule a calendar event, let the meet-worker spawn, have it join a real Google Meet, and join the Meet ourselves. That loop is slow, fragile, requires a real meeting room, and is the main reason interrupt / prompt / provider bugs are hard to reproduce.

We need a way for a logged-in user to **talk to the bot directly from the browser, voice-to-voice (and text), without Google Meet in the loop at all**. Two surfaces, sharing the same underlying transport:

### Surface 1 — Per-event 'Try with bot' button

On each calendar event detail page, add a button (e.g. 'Try with bot now' or 'Rehearse'). Clicking it:
- Spins up a real bot_sessions row scoped to that event.
- The bot is loaded with the **exact same context** it would use for the real meeting: event title/description, attendees, linked Google Docs/Sheets (see Johnny-4da once that's done), prior-session continuity (Johnny-dsy), active providers, system prompt.
- The user's microphone + speaker are connected to the bot's voice pipeline directly in-browser. No Google Meet, no meet-worker container needed.
- The session appears in the session list and history exactly like a 'real' session, so transcripts / utterances / decisions persist the same way.

### Surface 2 — Standalone playground

A new /playground page (or similarly named) that lets a user just start a casual conversation with the bot without any calendar event at all:
- Pick a persona / instruction set (saved or ad-hoc).
- Optionally **override the active providers for this session only** (e.g. 'use Piper instead of ElevenLabs for this run', 'try GPT-4o instead of the configured default'). Overrides do NOT mutate the global active-provider selection.
- Optionally paste in a custom system prompt that takes precedence.
- Choose voice or text input; receive voice + transcript output.
- Session is logged the same way — visible in history with a 'playground' tag so it's distinguishable from real meetings.

## Value

- **Testing**: this is the primary use case the user called out. Testing every new provider, every prompt change, every fix to the interrupt / VAD / barge-in path becomes a 5-second loop instead of a 5-minute Meet round-trip. Directly replaces a chunk of what Johnny-ckz.4 needs to cover manually.
- **Demoing**: lets the user show the bot to someone in 10 seconds, on any machine, without provisioning a Meet.
- **Rehearsing**: lets the user practice an upcoming meeting with the bot using the real pre-meeting context.
- **Reproducing bugs interactively**: especially the voice-interrupt bugs (Johnny-ze3, Johnny-har) which are nearly impossible to repro reliably in a Meet.

## Required behavior

1. Voice-to-voice loop works end-to-end: user speaks → STT → router LLM → TTS → user hears it. No Google Meet in the path. Latency budget: time-to-first-audio comparable to or better than the meet-worker path.
2. Interrupts work: user can talk over the bot and the bot yields the floor (same contract as a real session). This surface should be a first-class venue for verifying the interrupt fix.
3. Text input as a fallback when mic isn't available or muted — same pipeline, just bypassing STT for that turn.
4. The session is a real bot_sessions row, with real transcript_chunks / agent_utterances / agent_decisions, viewable in the existing session detail page.
5. Per-event variant: bot context matches what the real meeting would get (verifiable by comparing the system prompt / context dump against the real meeting's).
6. Playground variant: provider/prompt overrides are scoped to that session only. Closing the session restores everything. Active-provider settings in the DB are untouched.
7. UI clearly distinguishes a playground/rehearsal session from a real one in the session list (badge or tag), so analytics / reports aren't polluted.
8. Mic permission is requested cleanly with a clear explanation; gracefully degrades to text-only if denied.
9. Leaving the page or clicking 'End session' actually ends the session and tears down the audio transport (cf. Johnny-ajc — do not repeat the leave-button bug here).

## Out of scope

- Multi-user playground (inviting a teammate into the same playground session).
- Video / screen-share.
- Persisting playground overrides as new saved provider configs (use the existing provider settings page for that).
- A standalone CLI or non-browser entrypoint.

## Acceptance criteria

1. From a calendar event page, clicking 'Try with bot' opens an in-browser voice session in under 3 seconds and the bot greets the user (audible).
2. From /playground with no event, the user can pick a persona, override the active TTS provider for that session only, click Start, and have a voice conversation. After ending, the global active-TTS selection is unchanged in the providers page.
3. Both surfaces produce a bot_sessions row with non-empty transcript_chunks and agent_utterances after a short exchange.
4. User can interrupt the bot mid-reply and the TTS cuts within the same latency budget Johnny-ckz.4 enforces.
5. Playground sessions appear in the session list with a clear visual badge separating them from real-meeting sessions.
6. Mic permission denial falls back to text-only chat with no JS errors and a visible explanation.
7. Ending the session tears down audio (no orphan WebRTC connections, no stuck mic indicator) — verified by inspecting browser state after End.
8. No meet-worker container is spawned for either surface (verified by docker ps while a playground session is live).

## Testing approach — MANDATORY via chrome-devtools MCP

Per the top rule in AGENTS.md, every user-visible behavior here must be validated through the real browser using the mcp__chrome-devtools__* tools. The verification trace for this feature must include at minimum:

- **Permission flow**: open the playground page; capture the mic permission prompt; grant it; assert audio capture starts (evaluate_script against navigator.mediaDevices state).
- **Voice round-trip**: drive a synthetic audio input (or use a prerecorded sample via the Speaker harness from Johnny-2bw / Johnny-ckz.4); confirm an audio element starts playing back the bot's reply; capture a screenshot of the live session.
- **Transcript rendering**: take_snapshot mid-conversation and assert user + bot turns are rendering with correct attribution.
- **Interrupt**: play 'stop' while the bot is replying; assert the bot's audio element stops within the latency budget; assert the user's 'stop' lands in transcript_chunks.
- **Per-event context parity**: open a calendar event in chrome-devtools MCP; click 'Try with bot'; in a separate tab open the system-prompt / context debug view; diff against the prompt that a real-meeting session for that event would receive. They must match (modulo session-id-style fields).
- **Override scoping**: in the playground, override the active LLM; run a turn; end the session; reload providers page; confirm the global active LLM is unchanged.
- **End-session cleanup**: end the session; evaluate_script to assert no live RTCPeerConnection instances; list_network_requests to confirm no lingering WebSocket; docker ps from the host to confirm no meet-worker container was spawned for this session.
- **Mic-denied fallback**: emulate a denied permission; assert the UI offers text input and no console errors; complete a text-only turn round-trip.

Unit/integration tests are necessary but **not** sufficient. The PR description must include screenshots from a real chrome-devtools MCP run covering each of the above checks.

## Related

- [[run-the-two-bot-voice-interrupt-harness-end-to-end-against-real-models-fix-any-bugs-it-surfaces]] (Johnny-ckz.4) — this playground is the natural interactive companion to that automated harness.
- [[active-session-leave-now-button-ui-marks-session-ended-but-bot-stays-in-the-google-meet]] (Johnny-ajc) — same end-session contract; do not repeat that leak.
- [[cross-session-continuity-rehydrate-prior-session-summary-for-recurring-events]] (Johnny-dsy) — per-event rehearsals should respect rehydrated context once that ships.
design: Reuse the existing voice pipeline (STT / router / TTS) as a transport-agnostic core. Run it under a browser-direct transport — likely WebRTC (LiveKit env already present in docker-compose) — so the meet-worker container is bypassed. Session-scoped provider overrides should be a per-session override layer on top of the registry, not a mutation of the active selection. Per-event surface reuses the same context-assembly that the meet-worker uses today, so prompts match. End-of-session teardown must be authoritative (kill peer connection, release mic, mark session ended in one transaction) — model after the contract Johnny-ajc requires.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Per-event 'Try with bot' button opens an in-browser voice session in <3s with audible greeting. (2) Standalone /playground supports persona pick, session-scoped provider/prompt overrides, voice + text. (3) Both produce real bot_sessions rows with transcripts and utterances. (4) Interrupts work within Johnny-ckz.4's latency budget. (5) Playground sessions are visually distinct in the session list. (6) Mic-denied falls back to text-only with no JS errors. (7) End-session cleanly tears down audio (no orphan WebRTC, no mic indicator stuck). (8) No meet-worker container is spawned for either surface. (9) All UI behavior validated via chrome-devtools MCP with screenshots in the PR.

title: Run the two-bot voice-interrupt harness end-to-end against real models, fix any bugs it surfaces
description:
Johnny-2bw built the automated two-bot harness (synthetic Speaker plays prerecorded prompts + 'stop' interrupts against the real Johnny meet-worker). The harness exists but has not been driven to a clean green run. This task is to actually run it, watch it fail, fix the bugs it surfaces, and re-run until it is reliably green.

Critical constraint: REAL MODELS ONLY
- No mocked STT, no mocked TTS, no mocked LLM. The whole point of the harness is to reproduce what fails in production, which only happens when the real STT/TTS/LLM pipeline is in the loop with its real latency / barge-in / VAD characteristics.
- Provider credentials to use: /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json. Import this as the provider config (the seeder at JOHNNY_PROVIDERS_FILE already supports this format — see Johnny-d3e and Johnny-k3z). This file holds API keys for the cloud STT/TTS/LLM providers the harness should exercise.

What 'works smoothly' means here:
- A single command (e.g. ./scripts/run-interrupt-harness.sh or pytest target) launches both participants, runs the scripted scenario, evaluates the assertions from Johnny-2bw, and prints a pass/fail summary.
- It can be re-run back-to-back without manual cleanup: no leftover meet-worker-session-* containers, no orphaned bot_sessions rows, no held Meet rooms.
- It does not require a human to be in the meet.
- Output (transcripts, audio captures, timing traces) is written to a known location so a failure can be debugged after the fact.

In-scope bug-fixing budget:
- Anything the harness surfaces that prevents it from reaching a deterministic verdict — flaky timing, race conditions on session start, transcript_chunks not arriving, agent_utterances not getting written, container teardown leaking — fix it. This includes underlying voice-interrupt bugs (Johnny-ze3, Johnny-har) if they are what the harness keeps catching.
- Out of scope: redesigning the harness; broadening it beyond the scenarios already specified in Johnny-2bw.

Depends on: Johnny-2bw (closed — built the harness)
design: Bring up the stack with the imported providers (JOHNNY_PROVIDERS_FILE pointing at the credentials JSON). Drive the harness from Johnny-2bw. When a run fails, capture the artifact bundle (meet-worker logs, transcript_chunks, agent_utterances, audio dump) and root-cause before re-running. Do not move to step 2 until the failure is understood — flaky-green is worse than red here.
acceptance_criteria: (1) The harness runs end-to-end with the providers from /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json — no mocks anywhere in the STT/TTS/LLM pipeline. (2) All Johnny-2bw assertions pass on three consecutive runs (no flakes): 'stop' lands in transcript within ~1s, TTS is actually cut, latency under 500ms, no follow-up after 'stop', follow-up after 'wait, what about X?', cough does not cut. (3) Re-running the harness does not require manual cleanup. (4) Any bugs the harness uncovers in the voice-interrupt path are fixed (not just bypassed).
notes: Existing Johnny-2bw harness uses scripted providers. Johnny-ckz.4 needs to add a --real mode that uses providers from JSON, pre-renders speaker audio via real TTS so real STT can transcribe, runs scenarios with real STT/LLM/TTS, and captures artifacts. Doing this now.

title: Active session 'Leave now' button: UI marks session ended but bot stays in the Google Meet
description:
User clicked the 'Leave now' button on an active session in the UI. The UI transitioned the session to its terminal/ended state, but the bot remained connected to the Google Meet — still online, still in the call, still presumably capturing audio.

Observed:
- UI: session shown as over after clicking 'Leave now'.
- Meet: bot participant still present in the meeting room; did not leave.
- Bot's meet-worker container apparently still running (connection not terminated).

Expected:
- 'Leave now' should both (a) end the session record in the DB and (b) cause the bot to gracefully exit the Google Meet (release media, hang up) and (c) stop / terminate the meet-worker container so the bot is no longer consuming resources or listening.
- After the click, the bot should be visibly gone from the Meet within a few seconds, and the corresponding meet-worker-session-<id> container should be stopped.

Severity rationale (P1): a bot that stays in a meeting after the operator explicitly told it to leave is a trust / privacy problem — the user reasonably believes the bot is gone, but it is still able to hear the conversation.

Out of scope for this issue: redesigning the leave flow. Just make 'Leave now' actually leave.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking 'Leave now' on an active session results in: (1) session marked ended in the UI/DB, (2) bot participant visibly leaves the Google Meet within a few seconds, (3) the meet-worker-session-<id> container is stopped (not just orphaned). All three must happen on every click, not just sometimes.

title: Active LLM provider sometimes gets unselected (TTS and STT are not affected)
description:
## Why this exists

The active-provider selection for LLM is unstable. The user had OpenAI configured as the active LLM provider, and after some operation (possibly a stack restart), the active LLM selection was empty — no provider marked active.

This is specific to LLM. The active TTS and active STT providers persist correctly through the same conditions; only LLM loses its selection.

Impact: when there is no active LLM, the bot can't think — every router decision and every utterance generation fails or no-ops. Meetings become useless without anyone noticing until the bot stays silent.

## What's broken

- Active LLM provider stored somewhere (DB row, settings table, provider.is_active column) is being reset/cleared under some condition
- TTS / STT use the same persistence pattern but are unaffected — so the bug is specifically in the LLM-active code path

## Investigation hints

- Check whether LLM providers have a different is_active / active_for_kind persistence pattern than STT/TTS
- Check stack startup code: does anything reset or recompute the active LLM on bootup (migration, seed, validator)?
- Check provider-update API path: does saving an LLM provider clear another's active flag without setting the new one?
- Check whether there's a uniqueness constraint that fails silently and leaves the active flag NULL on conflict
- Search backend/app/api/providers.py and any provider service module for asymmetric handling of kind=llm vs kind=stt/tts

## Acceptance

- Configure OpenAI as the active LLM
- Restart the stack
- Active LLM is still OpenAI
- Add/edit/delete other providers
- Active LLM remains as set, never silently NULLed
- Behavior matches TTS and STT for the same operations
- Add automated test that exercises 'set active LLM → restart → assert active LLM unchanged'

title: Add ElevenLabs as an STT provider (missing from Add Provider dropdown when kind=stt)
description:

title: Bot speaks over user mid-sentence: partial transcripts trigger responses before user finishes
description:
## Why this exists

When the user says something long, the system feeds partial transcripts to the LLM as they arrive, and the bot starts responding before the user has finished speaking. The result: the bot talks over the user, interrupting the user's own sentence — the opposite of polite turn-taking.

This is an endpointing / turn-detection bug. The system is treating every incoming partial transcript chunk as a complete user turn instead of waiting for the user to actually finish.

## What needs to happen

The voice pipeline must distinguish 'user is still talking' from 'user has finished their turn' before invoking the LLM:

### Possible approaches (the right answer is probably a combination)

1. **Endpointing via silence detection**: only treat the user as 'done' after N ms of silence (~600-1000ms target). Tunable per profile.
2. **Sentence-completion heuristics**: don't trigger a response if the transcript ends mid-sentence (no terminal punctuation, ends on a filler word, etc.)
3. **STT-provider endpointing signals**: many STT services emit an 'is_final' flag — only respond on is_final, not on partials
4. **Cancellable LLM dispatch**: if a new partial arrives while an LLM call is in flight for the previous partial, cancel the in-flight call and re-issue with the updated transcript
5. **Don't speak while user is speaking**: even if the LLM has a response ready, suppress TTS playback if STT is currently receiving voiced audio from the user

### Behavior we want

- User pauses to think mid-sentence → bot waits, doesn't jump in
- User says a long multi-clause sentence → bot waits for it to actually end before responding
- User finishes and falls silent for ~800ms → bot responds
- If the user resumes talking before that silence threshold, the LLM dispatch is cancelled and the bot stays silent

## Investigation hints

- Check how the pipeline decides 'turn ended': look for endpointing logic in backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/
- Check whether partial transcripts are flowing into the router / LLM, or only finals
- Verify VAD (SileroVAD or other) is actually configured — there's been a 'SileroVAD unavailable' warning in worker logs before, which would cause naive endpointing
- The fix may need a tunable parameter on meeting_config for silence threshold

## Acceptance

- User starts a long sentence, pauses for ~300ms mid-clause → bot does NOT respond yet
- User finishes, falls silent for ~800ms → bot responds
- User restarts speaking before the 800ms threshold → bot stays silent and the previous LLM dispatch is cancelled
- Multi-sentence user turns (the user explains something over 30 seconds with normal pauses) → bot does not jump in until the user actually stops
- No regression to interrupt behavior — barge-in (when bot IS speaking) still works per [[voice-interrupt-doesn-t-actually-work-end-to-end-bot-ignores-user-speech-mid-utterance-reopens-johnny-har-johnny-di9]] (Johnny-ze3)

## Related

- [[voice-interrupt-doesn-t-actually-work-end-to-end-bot-ignores-user-speech-mid-utterance-reopens-johnny-har-johnny-di9]] (Johnny-ze3) — opposite direction (user interrupts bot); this one is bot interrupting user
- [[build-automated-two-bot-test-harness-to-reproduce-voice-interrupt-failure-simulated-speaker-vs-johnny]] (Johnny-2bw) — the same harness should also assert 'bot does not speak while user's mic has voiced audio'

title: Build automated two-bot test harness to reproduce voice-interrupt failure (simulated speaker vs Johnny)
description:
## Why this exists

The voice-interrupt feature keeps being marked 'done' but in real sessions it doesn't work. Manual testing in real Google Meets is slow, non-reproducible, and depends on a human being available and patient. We need an automated harness that proves whether interrupt works — runnable any time, headless, with deterministic results.

### Latest failure evidence

Session 160 (http://localhost:5173/sessions/160):
- User: 'Can you say something a little bit more, Johnny?'
- Bot launched into a long monologue about the Anglo-Zanzibar War of August 27, 1896
- User repeatedly said 'stop' — bot ignored every attempt
- The 'stop' utterances do not appear in the session transcript at all — STT is dropping or never receiving the user's audio while the bot is speaking
- Confirms that [[voice-interrupt-doesn-t-actually-work-end-to-end-bot-ignores-user-speech-mid-utterance-reopens-johnny-har-johnny-di9]] (Johnny-ze3) is still broken AND that [[stt-transcription-of-participants-must-never-pause-while-bot-is-speaking-or-thinking]] (Johnny-har) is still broken — the user's words don't even land in transcript_chunks

## What to build

An automated end-to-end test harness with two synthetic participants in a real or simulated meeting:

### Synthetic 'Speaker' participant
- Joins a Meet (or simulated audio room) as a separate Playwright participant
- Plays prerecorded audio: an opening prompt that triggers Johnny to give a long answer ('tell me about yourself for 2 minutes'), then after N seconds plays a clear 'stop' interrupt phrase
- Optionally plays additional probes: 'wait, what about X?', cough, side-conversation chatter (to verify intent classifier ignores non-interrupts)

### Johnny under test
- Real meet-worker container running the actual stack (not a mock)

### Assertions the harness must verify
- Speaker's 'stop' utterance lands in transcript_chunks within ~1s of being played (proves STT runs during bot speech)
- agent_utterances row for the bot's long answer has audio_duration_ms < the full TTS length (proves TTS was actually cut)
- Time delta between speaker's 'stop' end and TTS cut is < 500ms (latency budget)
- Bot does not emit a follow-up utterance after a 'stop' signal (yields the floor)
- Bot DOES emit a follow-up addressing X after a 'wait, what about X?' signal
- Cough / unrelated chatter does NOT cut the bot

### Implementation hints
- Use Playwright to spawn the second Meet participant with mic input piped from a wav file
- Or, if Meet-in-the-loop is too fragile for CI, build a simulated audio bridge that feeds wav frames directly into Johnny's STT input and captures TTS output frames
- The test runs as 'uv run python -m johnny.e2e.interrupt' or 'make e2e-interrupt' and produces a pass/fail report
- Run it 10x in a row — flakiness > 0% is a failure

## Acceptance

- Single command runs the harness against a fresh stack
- Harness completes in < 5 minutes
- Pass/fail clearly reported with per-assertion detail
- Captured artifacts on failure: transcript_chunks rows, agent_utterances rows, meet-worker docker log, TTS waveform showing exactly where it was cut
- 10/10 successful runs against a working stack
- Successfully reproduces the failure today against the current broken stack (proves the harness catches real bugs)

## Related (all in the same broken family)

- [[voice-interrupt-doesn-t-actually-work-end-to-end-bot-ignores-user-speech-mid-utterance-reopens-johnny-har-johnny-di9]] (Johnny-ze3)
- [[stt-transcription-of-participants-must-never-pause-while-bot-is-speaking-or-thinking]] (Johnny-har)
- [[voice-triggered-barge-in-user-can-interrupt-the-bot-mid-utterance-by-speaking]] (Johnny-di9)
- [[bot-loses-conversation-context-mid-session-can-t-recall-its-own-prior-utterances]] (Johnny-7qp) — same kind of 'manual testing missed it' pattern

title: Bot loses conversation context mid-session: can't recall its own prior utterances
description:
## Why this exists

In session 155 (http://localhost:5173/sessions/155) the bot demonstrably forgets its own conversation history within a single meeting:

1. The bot delivered a substantive statement about upgrading infrastructure and making servers more reliable
2. The user asked the bot to repeat what it just said
3. The bot had no memory of its own prior utterance — could not recall even basic content it had spoken seconds earlier

The bot must follow the WHOLE context of the conversation within a session — every participant utterance AND every bot utterance — not a short rolling window. Losing track of its own statements makes the bot unusable for any real conversation.

## What needs to happen

- The LLM prompt that drives router decisions and bot answers must include the full conversation history of the active session
- 'Full' means: every transcript_chunk (human speech) and every agent_utterance (bot speech) since session start, in chronological order
- No 6-turn / N-turn rolling window cap — use token-budget management instead (summarize older turns if the window blows past the model limit, but never silently drop recent turns)
- The bot must specifically be able to answer 'what did you just say?' or 'repeat that' with the actual prior utterance content, verbatim or paraphrased

## Investigation hints

- Pull docker logs from meet-worker-session-155 to see what context is being passed into the LLM
- Check whether agent_utterances are being fed back into the LLM prompt at all (currently the focus may only be inbound transcripts)
- Cross-check with [[bot-carries-the-whole-meeting-s-context-not-a-6-turn-rolling-window-when-routing-and-answering]] (Johnny-ckz.3) — same family of bug, this one has fresh repro evidence

## Acceptance

- Bot says something substantive in a real session
- User asks 'repeat what you just said' or 'what did you just say about X?'
- Bot accurately recalls and reproduces the substance of its own prior utterance
- Works across at least 10 turns of conversation, including bot turns
- Conversation context survives an 18+ second bot utterance plus several user turns

title: Voice-triggered barge-in: user can interrupt the bot mid-utterance by speaking
description:
## Why this exists

When talking to the bot in a meeting, the user needs to interrupt it by speaking — exactly like interrupting a human. The bot can ramble or head the wrong direction; the natural fix is to say 'hey Johnny stop' or just start talking, and the bot stops.

This is voice-only. The user is in a Google Meet conversation; they are not going to open a UI or type anything.

But naive 'any sound interrupts the bot' is wrong: coughs, side-conversation between other participants, background noise, or off-topic mumbling shouldn't cut the bot off. The system must understand *intent*.

## What needs to happen

While the bot is speaking (TTS playing) or thinking (LLM in flight):
- Inbound STT keeps capturing every participant's audio (prerequisite: [[stt-transcription-of-participants-must-never-pause-while-bot-is-speaking-or-thinking]] / Johnny-har)
- As partial transcripts arrive, route them through a fast intent classifier (lightweight LLM call or rule + LLM) that decides whether this speech is:
  1. Direct interruption of the bot ('hey Johnny stop', 'wait', 'hold on')
  2. Correction / redirection of the bot ('no, focus on X', 'that's not right, it's actually Y')
  3. A new question to the bot ('actually, what about Z?')
  4. Side conversation between other humans, unrelated to the bot
  5. Background noise, mumbling, cough, etc.
- Only categories 1, 2, 3 trigger pipeline.interrupt() (backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/pipeline.py:371)
- Categories 4, 5 are transcribed (still go into history) but the bot keeps going

## Behavior after interrupt

- Category 1 (stop): TTS cuts within ~200ms, bot stays silent, yields the floor
- Category 2 (correct/redirect): TTS cuts, bot processes the correction and answers based on the new direction
- Category 3 (new question): TTS cuts, bot abandons current answer and addresses the new question

## Where the intelligence lives

The LLM (or router layer) is the decision-maker. It already has conversational context. Adding an 'interrupt intent' decision to each incoming partial transcript while the bot is talking is the natural place for this — not a hard-coded VAD trigger, not a keyword spotter.

## Prerequisites

- Johnny-har (STT continuity during bot speech) — without this, no inbound audio is available to classify

## Acceptance

- Bot starts a long answer in a real Google Meet
- Another participant coughs → bot keeps going
- Two participants quietly chat to each other off-topic → bot keeps going
- User says 'hey Johnny stop' → bot cuts within ~200ms and stays silent
- User says 'wait, no, talk about X instead' → bot cuts and switches to X
- User says 'actually, what's the status of Y?' → bot cuts and answers about Y
- All five cases produce transcript entries in the meeting history

title: STT transcription of participants must never pause while bot is speaking or thinking
description:
## Why this exists

The meeting transcript is the source of truth for what was said in the room. Right now, if the bot is speaking or thinking (LLM in flight, TTS playing), inbound STT for human participants can be suppressed or paused — meaning we lose context exactly when conversation is most active.

This is unacceptable: we must ALWAYS transcribe every human participant in the meeting, regardless of what the bot is doing. The bot is a participant, not an exclusive owner of the audio channel.

## What needs to happen

- Decouple inbound STT (participant audio → transcript_chunks) from the bot's speak/think pipeline state
- While the bot is generating an LLM response: keep transcribing
- While the bot is playing TTS into the room: keep transcribing
- While the bot is in any other 'busy' state: keep transcribing
- Verify there is no shared mutex / state machine forcing STT to wait on the bot

## Acceptance

- Run a session where the bot is intentionally made to speak for a long time
- Have a human participant speak over the bot mid-utterance
- Every word the human said is captured in transcript_chunks with correct timing
- No gaps in the transcript correlated with bot-speaking windows

## Related

- [[persist-bot-utterances-to-meeting-history-everything-the-bot-says]] (Johnny-awh) — interleaved log of bot speech vs. participant transcript chunks makes this verifiable
- [[user-can-interrupt-or-redirect-the-bot-mid-utterance-barge-in]] (sibling) — barge-in needs to detect human speech, which requires this fix

title: Approving a pending suggestion doesn't make the bot actually speak it
description:
## What's broken

When the user clicks 'Approve' on a pending bot suggestion in the UI, the bot does not appear to actually speak the approved text in the Google Meet session. The approval round-trips at the API level but the TTS/audio output to the meeting room never happens (or fails silently).

## Symptom

- Bot generates suggestion → appears in approval queue
- User clicks Approve
- UI shows the suggestion as approved
- No audio is heard in the Meet session
- Other participants do not hear the bot speak the approved text

## Investigation hints

- Verify the approval API path actually publishes the approved utterance to the TTS sink / voice pipeline
- Check backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/utterance_sink.py and the bot's audio bridge to the Meet room
- Check whether the bot's microphone in the Meet session is actually unmuted at the moment of speaking
- Cross-check with [[persist-bot-utterances-to-meeting-history-everything-the-bot-says]] (Johnny-awh) — once utterances are logged, we can see whether the approved text ever reached the TTS layer
- Related to [[review-and-standardize-bot-free-mode-speech-decision-logic]] (Johnny-vgl) — same underlying 'bot doesn't actually speak' family of symptoms, different trigger

## Acceptance

- User approves a pending suggestion
- Within ~2 seconds the approved text is heard in the Meet session
- The spoken utterance is logged in the meeting history (depends on Johnny-awh)

title: Pending approvals don't appear in UI until page is refreshed
description:
## What's broken

When the bot generates a suggestion that requires user approval, the pending approval does not appear in the UI in real time. The user has to manually refresh the page to see new pending approvals.

## Expected behavior

Pending approvals should appear automatically as soon as the bot routes a suggestion to the approval queue — within ~1 second, without any user action.

## Likely root cause

The UI is not subscribed to a real-time channel for approval events (no WebSocket / Server-Sent Events / polling). The approval queue is fetched once on page load and never refreshed.

## Acceptance

- Open the meeting/approval view
- Trigger the bot to generate a suggestion (e.g., speak something the router will defer for approval)
- New pending approval appears in the UI within ~1 second, no refresh needed
- Resolved approvals (approved/rejected) also update in real time
- Works across multiple browser tabs simultaneously

title: Persist bot utterances to meeting history (everything the bot says)
description:
## Why this exists

Currently the bot's transcriptions/utterances (everything it says into the meeting) are not consistently persisted to the meeting history. Without this, the user cannot review what the bot actually said after the meeting, audit autonomous-mode behavior, or debug why a suggestion did/did not get spoken.

The history must be the single source of truth for both:
- What participants said (already partially captured in transcript_chunks)
- What the bot said (currently missing or inconsistent)

## What needs to happen

- Every bot utterance — whether triggered by free mode, suggested-and-approved mode, autonomous mode, or any other path — must be persisted to the meeting history with:
  - session_id
  - timestamp
  - utterance text
  - source/mode that triggered it (suggestion-approved / autonomous / scripted / etc.)
  - linkage to the originating router decision or LLM response if applicable
- Existing sinks (see backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/transcript_sink.py and utterance_sink.py) should be reviewed to ensure they capture bot output, not only inbound STT
- UI: the meeting/session view must show bot utterances inline with participant transcripts so the timeline is complete
- Backfill: confirm historical sessions either get utterances backfilled where data exists or are clearly marked as incomplete

## Acceptance

- After a real Google Meet session, the history view shows every phrase the bot spoke, in order, distinguishable from participant transcript chunks
- Records survive container restart and are queryable in PostgreSQL
- Free-mode suggestions that were NOT spoken are also recorded (as suggestions) so the decision audit trail is complete

Related: [[review-and-standardize-bot-free-mode-speech-decision-logic]] (Johnny-vgl) — the free-mode decision logic must surface its outcome here.

title: Review and standardize bot free mode speech decision logic
description:
In free mode, the bot generates suggested responses (shown in UI like 'Suggested: ...') but does not actually speak them in the meeting. The decision-making process for when/whether the bot speaks is unclear and inconsistent.

This functionality needs to be reviewed and standardized:
- How is the decision made for the bot to speak vs. just suggest?
- What triggers actual speech output in free mode?
- How does free mode differ from other modes (guided, scripted, etc.)?
- Standardize the behavior so suggestions and actual speech are aligned with mode semantics

Context: Observed during a live meeting test where the bot showed a confident suggested response ('Yes I am! Nice to meet you all...') but never spoke it aloud in the Google Meet session.

title: Install piper-tts in api/worker (and meet-worker) image and mount piper_models volume
description: Same shape as Johnny-1gl but for the Piper TTS provider. The api container has no piper binary on PATH so the /providers/{id}/test smoke call fails. The meet-worker image also does not install piper despite SETUP_LOCAL.md claiming it ships pre-installed — fix both. Use the piper-tts PyPI wheel (provides the piper CLI). Also mount the piper_models named volume in api/worker so voice ONNX files downloaded by any service are visible everywhere.
close_reason: api/worker Dockerfile installs piper-tts via --extra local-tts; meet-worker Dockerfile pins piper-tts==1.4.2; api/worker compose services mount piper_models; verified POST /providers/172/test returns ok=true with 15604 bytes synthesized after downloading en_US-john-medium into the volume.

title: Install faster-whisper in api/worker image and mount whisper_models volume
description: The Test button in admin Providers UI calls POST /providers/{id}/test inside the api container, which runs a real transcribe_stream against the configured STT provider. For faster-whisper that requires the library to be importable in the api container; today only the meet-worker image ships it. Also api/worker need read access to the whisper_models named volume so cached CTranslate2 weights are shared with the meet-worker.
close_reason: api/worker Dockerfile now installs faster-whisper via uv sync --extra local-stt; api/worker compose services mount the whisper_models volume; verified by hitting POST /providers/136/test which returns ok=true after pre-warming the base model into the volume.

title: Verify ElevenLabs TTS provider works end-to-end with updated API key
description:
The ELEVENLABS_API_KEY value in .env has been replaced with a real ElevenLabs key (previously it contained a Google API key starting with AIzaSy... which caused HTTP 401 Invalid API key responses).

Now verify the ElevenLabs TTS adapter actually works end-to-end against the live ElevenLabs API:

1. Re-run `uv run python -m tests.e2e.providers_ui` and confirm the tts-elevenlabs row PASSes (no more 401).
2. Hit `POST /providers/{id}/test` directly against the seeded elevenlabs provider row and confirm it returns success with synthesized audio bytes (non-empty payload, valid audio content-type).
3. Exercise the provider in a real meeting context: trigger an agent_utterance in auto_speak_limited mode and confirm the resulting audio is generated via ElevenLabs and surfaces in the meeting audio bridge.
4. Capture the voice ID / model used in the request and persist a short note in the provider config so the working values are reproducible.
5. Close this issue only after a real Meet session has played back an ElevenLabs-synthesized utterance audibly to the user account.
close_reason: ElevenLabs TTS confirmed working — no further verification needed

title: Execute comprehensive end-to-end validation: bot joins real Google Meet and exercises every product feature across all modes
description:
## Why this exists

The lived product journey: Johnny (bot account, nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi) joins a real Google Meet via the Test calendar event, and every feature exposed by the app is exercised against the live session. The user observes/drives the meeting from nikita.rabykin@gmail.com.

This is the **master functional validation** for the Johnny product:
- Johnny-f7k smoke-tests infrastructure (`.env`, services, models).
- Johnny-upg drives the provider management UI.
- Johnny-ckz Part B builds an automated harness command.
- **This task is the full coverage run** that proves the actual product (join → listen → decide → speak → audit) works against a real Google Meet, in every mode, with every UI surface verified.

## Testing identities (do not confuse)

- **Bot identity (Johnny in the app)**: `nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi`, role=bot
- **Observer / driver (Meet participant)**: `nikita.rabykin@gmail.com`
- **Test calendar event**: single event titled "Test", owner=`nikita.rabykin@gmail.com`, both accounts invited, Meet link attached, freely modifiable between runs

## When to run

- After Johnny-ckz Part A (join-stuck bug fix) lands — without it, every phase past Phase 3 will fail.
- Re-run whenever any of the following changes: join path (Playwright, Xvfb, PulseAudio, Google sign-in), audio bridge, Pipecat pipeline, VAD, router LLM, answer LLM, TTS, persistence layer (transcript_chunks / agent_decisions / agent_utterances), live session UI, history view, identity switching, scheduler.

## How to run

- **Preferred**: via Johnny-ckz Part B harness — `uv run python -m johnny.e2e --mode=<mode>` for each of the four modes — once it is built.
- **Fallback (works today)**: execute the phases below manually with chrome-devtools-mcp driving every UI verification and the observer account driving Meet audio.

Either path must produce the same evidence package (screenshots + JSON report under `tests/e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>/`) and the same PASS/FAIL roll-up.

## Scope: every product surface

- **Calendar surface**: fetch, refresh, select event, configure bot
- **Profile templates**: applied via meeting_config with overrides
- **Identity switching**: bot account vs user account
- **Scheduler**: detects upcoming meeting, spawns worker, stops on time
- **Meet worker**: Playwright joins, Xvfb + PulseAudio configured, mic muted / camera off by default
- **Audio bridge**: capture meeting audio, playback synthesized audio into virtual mic
- **Pipecat pipeline**: VAD → STT → router LLM → answer LLM → TTS
- **All four modes**: listen / suggest / approval / auto_speak_limited
- **Browser push notifications + in-UI approvals**
- **Persistence**: transcript_chunks, agent_decisions, agent_utterances
- **Live session UI**: transcript pane, decision feed, pending approvals
- **History view**: list, detail, pgvector transcript search, export, delete

## Out of scope

- Performance benchmarking and latency budgets
- Multi-tenant / multi-user fixtures (single Test event, single bot, single observer)
- Concurrent meetings / load tests
- CI integration (follow-up task)
- AWS / cloud deployment paths
design:

- Observer / driver: nikita.rabykin@gmail.com (in Meet via standard browser; optionally connected in Johnny app)

title: End-to-end UI test of provider management via chrome-devtools-mcp
description:
## Why this exists

The user has populated `.env` with real API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Deepgram, and ElevenLabs (cloud), plus Ollama (local LLM via OpenAI-compatible endpoint). The provider settings UI at `/providers` (US-018, Johnny-kgc.18) is the only path real users will use to add, test, switch, and remove providers — but right now no automation exercises that path. A regression in the form, the registry endpoint, the encryption pipeline, or the active-row selector would ship undetected because the existing tests cover the API in isolation, not the UI flow.

Johnny-f7k handles the backend `.env` smoke (cheap API probes against each provider key) but never touches the browser. This task closes the gap: drive the real SvelteKit UI with chrome-devtools-mcp, exercise every provider end-to-end, assert both UI state and database state at every step, and produce a PASS/SKIP/FAIL report plus screenshot artifacts.

## Goal

Build a re-runnable E2E harness that proves the provider management UI works for every supported backend against the keys already present in `.env`. The harness:

- Runs against a live Docker Compose stack
- Drives a real browser via chrome-devtools-mcp
- Adds, tests, sets-active, switches, and removes every provider for every kind (STT / LLM / TTS)
- Skips any provider whose `.env` key is blank (no false failures)
- Captures screenshots and a JSON report into `tests/e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>/`
- Exits non-zero on any FAIL so it can gate CI

## Scope: per-kind x per-provider matrix

**STT**
- Deepgram (cloud) — `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`
- OpenAI Realtime STT (cloud) — `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- FasterWhisper (local) — model file in `whisper_models` volume; SKIP if not present

**LLM**
- OpenAI (cloud) — `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- Anthropic (cloud) — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
- Gemini (cloud) — `GEMINI_API_KEY` / `GOOGLE_API_KEY`
- OpenAI-compatible / Ollama (local) — `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` reachable; SKIP otherwise

**TTS**
- ElevenLabs (cloud) — `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`
- OpenAI TTS (cloud) — `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- Piper (local) — voice file in `piper_voices` volume; SKIP if not present

## Per-provider flow

For each provider with a configured key:

1. Navigate to `/providers`
2. Click "Add provider" for the right kind
3. Select the backend from the dropdown
4. Fill the form (credentials + config). The harness is **schema-aware**: it calls `GET /providers/schemas` if available (post-Johnny-mma) and renders field-by-field; otherwise it falls back to filling the current generic `Credentials` and `Options` textareas with the right `key=value` lines.
5. Submit
6. Assert row visible in the list with the expected name and kind
7. Assert row present in `GET /providers` API response
8. Click "Test" on the row
9. Assert test result rendered as success in UI within 10s
10. Assert success surfaced via `POST /providers/{id}/test` response code
11. Set the row as active for its kind
12. Assert active indicator visible in UI
13. Assert exactly one provider per kind has `is_active=true` in DB
14. Screenshot

After all providers of a kind are added:

15. Switch active between two providers of the same kind; assert UI and DB switch
16. Delete each provider one at a time
17. Assert row removed from UI and DB after each delete
18. Verify behavior when deleting the active provider — auto-promote another or require explicit unset, whichever matches the implemented contract

## Error and edge cases

- **Invalid API key** — fill with `sk-invalid-deadbeef`; Test button must report failure with HTTP status and readable UI error
- **Missing required field** — submit with a required field blank; form must reject with field-level error and make no API call
- **Duplicate name** — adding a second provider with the same `name` must be rejected with a clear UI message
- **Provider with no `.env` key** — SKIP gracefully with `reason` in the report, never FAIL
- **Network failure during Test** — `/providers/{id}/test` should surface a transient error and the UI must not get stuck in a loading state
- **Backend down mid-flow** — clean error toast, no UI crash

## chrome-devtools-mcp usage (REQUIRED — do NOT use claude-in-chrome)

Tools to load first via `ToolSearch`:

- `mcp__chrome-devtools__new_page` / `list_pages` / `select_page`
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__navigate_page`
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__take_snapshot` (accessibility tree — primary assertion handle)
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__take_screenshot` (visual artifacts)
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__fill` / `fill_form`
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__click`
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__wait_for`
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__list_console_messages` (capture browser errors)
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__list_network_requests` (verify API traffic)
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__evaluate_script` (last resort for state assertions)

Snapshot-based assertions (role + name) are preferred over XPath/CSS — they survive markup churn.

## Implementation

- Location: `tests/e2e/providers_ui/`
- Entrypoint: `uv run python -m tests.e2e.providers_ui` and `pytest -m e2e_ui` both work
- One Python module per kind: `test_stt.py`, `test_llm.py`, `test_tts.py`
- Shared fixtures: stack health check, schema fetcher, artifact directory factory, screenshot helper
- Final summary table (kind x backend x outcome) printed to stdout
- JSON report at `tests/e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>/report.json` for CI consumption
- Exit 0 only when no FAIL; SKIP does not block exit success
- Idempotent: harness deletes all provider rows at the start with a confirm prompt or `--force` for unattended runs
- Docs: `docs/E2E_TESTING.md` explains how to run, what is tested, and how to add a new provider

## Out of scope

- Provider performance benchmarking
- Cost tracking
- Long-form generation tests (verify connectivity, not depth)
- Mobile viewport testing
- A11y audit (separate task)
- Joining a real Meet — that is Johnny-ckz Part B
design:
- chrome-devtools-mcp ONLY (per CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude/rules/common/browser-automation.md). Never claude-in-chrome.
- Schema-aware form filler: prefer `GET /providers/schemas`; fall back to the current generic Credentials/Options textareas if endpoint is 404. Lets the harness run today and survive Johnny-mma landing.
- DB assertions via `GET /providers` (and `GET /providers/{id}`) — never direct DB queries. Keeps the test honest about what the API exposes.
- Idempotent setup: harness deletes all provider rows at start with explicit `--force` for unattended runs. Avoids cross-run state bleed.
- Artifact dir per run (`tests/e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>/`) so historical comparison and CI upload are easy.
- Test isolation: each provider exercise is independent and tagged so `pytest -k` can run a single backend.
- Secrets handling: harness reads keys from `os.environ` only, never logs key values, and scrubs password-type fields from screenshots.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Harness runs end-to-end against `docker compose up -d` and produces a PASS row for every provider whose `.env` key is set
- [ ] Each provider x {add, test, set-active, switch-active, delete} combination is exercised and asserted
- [ ] All browser automation goes through chrome-devtools-mcp; claude-in-chrome is never used
- [ ] Schema-aware form filling works in both pre-Johnny-mma (generic Credentials/Options textareas) and post-Johnny-mma (structured fields) states
- [ ] Screenshots captured at every major step and saved to `tests/e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>/`
- [ ] JSON report written to `tests/e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>/report.json` with PASS/SKIP/FAIL per provider x action
- [ ] Error/edge cases (invalid key, missing field, duplicate name, missing .env key, network failure) are exercised with expected-failure assertions
- [ ] Exit code is 0 only when no FAIL; SKIP does not fail the run
- [ ] `docs/E2E_TESTING.md` explains how to run and how to add a new provider
- [ ] Quality gates pass: `uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check`, `uv run mypy`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`
notes:
Related issues:
- Johnny-ckz — parent epic (validation harnesses)
- Johnny-f7k — backend .env smoke (complementary; non-UI)
- Johnny-mma — structured provider forms (this harness should adapt)
- Johnny-kgc.18 — US-018 the provider settings UI under test

Operational notes:
- API keys live in `.env`; harness reads via `os.environ` (do not hardcode anywhere in the repo)
- When chrome-devtools MCP server is not running, the harness should print a clear "start with: ..." message rather than fail with a cryptic socket error
- Common pattern: take_snapshot -> assert by role + name -> click by aria handle -> wait_for new node -> screenshot
- Run command (preview): `uv run python -m tests.e2e.providers_ui --force` (interactive: omit `--force`)

title: Smoke-test populated .env: bring stack up and verify end-to-end
description:
The user has populated .env with real keys (Google OAuth, Fernet, provider API keys). The setup guide (Johnny-mxx) and its bugfix (Johnny-i1d) made the documented commands runnable. The next concrete step is a repeatable smoke test that takes a populated .env and answers: "is this configuration actually usable, and where does it break?"

This task delivers a single command (or short script) the user can run after filling .env that verifies the whole stack stands up and the configured providers respond. It must produce a clear PASS/FAIL report per check so the user knows exactly what needs attention.

## What "smoke test" means here

The test is not a unit test — it is an integration probe that exercises real services with the real .env:

1. **Compose bring-up** — `docker compose up -d` succeeds, every service is healthy within a timeout (api, worker, frontend, postgres, redis).
2. **Migrations** — `alembic upgrade head` runs cleanly inside the api container against the live postgres.
3. **Fernet** — backend reads FERNET_KEY from env, encrypts and decrypts a sample value round-trip without error.
4. **Google OAuth config** — GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET / GOOGLE_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI are present and the consent URL builds without error (do not require a live user consent).
5. **Provider credentials sanity** — for each non-empty provider key in .env (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, DEEPGRAM_API_KEY, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY), perform a 1-line cheap call (e.g. list models / list voices / `hi` completion of <= 5 tokens) and report the HTTP status. Skip providers whose keys are blank.
6. **Local model dirs** — JOHNNY_WHISPER_MODEL_DIR and JOHNNY_PIPER_MODEL_DIR resolve to writable mounts inside the meet-worker image; report whether expected model files are present and, if not, what to download.
7. **Ollama reachability** — if Ollama is the configured local LLM backend, hit `/api/tags` on the host and report the available models.
8. **Container launcher** — if JOHNNY_USE_DOCKER_LAUNCHER=true, verify the api/worker can talk to the Docker daemon and the meet-worker image is built/pulled.
9. **WebSocket** — `/ws/global` accepts a connection and immediately closes cleanly (no auth in MVP).
10. **Frontend** — `http://localhost:5173` returns 200 and the SvelteKit shell loads (chrome-devtools MCP screenshot for visual confirmation).

## How to deliver it

Pick one of these (whichever fits the codebase best — leave the choice to the implementer):

- A new make target / script: `scripts/smoke.sh` or `make smoke` that runs the checks and prints a colored PASS/FAIL table at the end.
- A backend CLI: `uv run python -m johnny.smoketest` that performs the in-process checks (Fernet, OAuth URL build, provider calls, model dirs) and shells out for the Compose/health checks.
- A pytest marker `@pytest.mark.smoke` plus `uv run pytest -m smoke` that uses the real .env (skip-if-blank for optional providers).

The chosen entrypoint should be documented in docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md as the very last step of "You finished — now verify".

## Output the user sees

The test must print one row per check with a status icon (PASS / SKIP / FAIL) and a one-line reason on failure. Example:

```
[PASS] docker compose services healthy (api, worker, frontend, postgres, redis)
[PASS] alembic upgrade head
[PASS] FERNET_KEY round-trip
[PASS] Google OAuth consent URL builds
[PASS] OPENAI_API_KEY        — models.list returned 200, 47 models
[SKIP] ANTHROPIC_API_KEY     — not set
[PASS] DEEPGRAM_API_KEY      — projects.list returned 200
[PASS] ELEVENLABS_API_KEY    — voices returned 200, 23 voices
[SKIP] GOOGLE_API_KEY        — not set
[PASS] Ollama reachable      — http://localhost:11434, 2 models (llama3.1, qwen2.5)
[PASS] Whisper models dir    — base.en present
[FAIL] Piper voices dir      — empty; download from https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices
[PASS] Docker launcher       — meet-worker:latest image found
[PASS] WS /ws/global         — connect+close ok
[PASS] Frontend              — 200, shell rendered (screenshot: tmp/smoke/frontend.png)

12 PASS · 2 SKIP · 1 FAIL
```

Exit code is 0 if every non-SKIP check passed, 1 otherwise. SKIP is for optional providers with blank keys, never a failure.

## Out of scope
- Performing a real Google OAuth consent flow (would require a browser session and a real user).
- Joining a real Google Meet meeting end-to-end (that is a separate manual verification).
- Performance benchmarking (latency, throughput).
- Multi-account or LiveKit transport smoke (LiveKit-specific checks can be added once Johnny-kgc.25 is exercised in practice — for now JOHNNY_TRANSPORT=local is enough).
acceptance_criteria: A single documented entrypoint (script, make target, or pytest marker) runs the full smoke flow against a populated .env. The output prints one PASS/SKIP/FAIL row per check with a one-line reason on failure, and a final summary line. Skipped providers (blank keys) never cause a FAIL. Exit code is 0 only when every non-SKIP check passed. Checks include: docker compose healthy services, alembic upgrade, Fernet round-trip, Google OAuth URL build, per-provider live credential probes (cheap calls), Ollama reachability if configured, model directories, Docker launcher reachability if enabled, WebSocket connect, frontend HTTP 200 with screenshot. The smoke entrypoint is added as the final step of docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md. All quality gates pass: uv run pytest, uv run ruff check, uv run mypy, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint. Visual verification via chrome-devtools MCP captures the frontend shell.

Either the smoke flow was not run against the post-US-027 image or its 'compose healthy services' check did not include the worker. Needs a rerun + a fix that asserts every default-profile compose service is healthy (not just the ones that happen to be Up).

title: Fix broken commands in docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md
description:
The setup guide created under Johnny-mxx has commands that fail for a fresh user:

1. python3 -c 'from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())' fails with ModuleNotFoundError because the user has no global cryptography install yet.
2. uv install is not a valid subcommand (uv uses 'uv sync' for installing project deps, or 'uv pip install' for ad-hoc installs).
3. The guide doesn't make clear when to install backend deps (uv sync) vs frontend deps (pnpm install) before doing other steps.

Fixes required:
- Replace the cryptography-based Fernet key generation with a stdlib-only one-liner: python3 -c 'import base64,secrets; print(base64.urlsafe_b64encode(secrets.token_bytes(32)).decode())'
- Or use 'uv run --with cryptography python -c ...' so deps are auto-fetched
- Add a clear 'Install dependencies' step using 'uv sync' (backend) and 'pnpm install' (frontend) before any commands that require them
- Verify every copy-paste block in the guide actually works on a clean macOS/Linux machine
- Ensure ordering: clone -> install deps -> generate keys -> .env -> docker compose up
close_reason: Replaced Fernet command with stdlib base64+secrets one-liner (no cryptography install needed), added openssl fallback, fixed prereqs to clarify Python/Node are only required for non-Docker dev. Same fix applied to .env.example comment. Verified both commands produce a valid Fernet-decodable 32-byte key.

title: Persistent piper subprocess — kill the ~200-400 ms per-utterance ONNX spawn tax
description:
## Why
The dominant local-stack TTS latency, surfaced by Johnny-ckz.8 profiling and codified in the Piper in-UI tip 'Persistent piper process is the next big win', is the cold spawn + ONNX runtime startup that runs on every synthesize call. ~200-400 ms of pure overhead per turn.

## What
Hold one (or one-per-voice) long-lived piper subprocess. Reuse stdin/stdout across synthesize calls. Handle:
- voice swap (current implementation picks model_path per call)
- subprocess crash with auto-respawn
- graceful shutdown on adapter teardown
- chunk delivery still streaming (not buffered until end of utterance)

Alternative: piper HTTP server variant fronted by a thin adapter. Same goal, different mechanism.

## Acceptance
1. Local Piper time-to-first-audio drops below 100 ms p50 on the test machine (vs the current ~300 ms p50 driven by spawn).
2. Behaviour unchanged for the existing tests in tests/providers/test_piper_tts.py.
3. UI tip on the Piper settings card is updated to reflect the new floor.
4. Chrome-devtools MCP validation of the playground showing the new latency in real use.

## Refs

- docs/LATENCY.md — current targets + methodology.
- Johnny-ckz.8 — parent profile/tune task. This is the headline optimisation it called out.

These rules are non-negotiable. A PR that skipped any of them gets rejected and the ticket reopens.

### 1. Read BOTH `PRODUCT.md` AND `DESIGN.md` at the project root, FIRST.

You may not enter plan mode for this ticket until you have read both files in full. They establish the brand voice (*"composed, deliberate, signal"*), the Signal Yellow discipline (`oklch(0.927 0.176 103)` ≈ `rgb(249, 233, 78)`, 5–10% of any surface, primary-CTA / focus-ring / live-indicator only), the OKLCH token system, the component spec for Button / Card / Alert / Badge / Input / Label / Separator, and the 8 verification gates that must pass before close.

Modal layout, form-field grouping, the "preview without save" affordance, the dynamic model-list dropdown, the Piper download CTA placement, error / empty / loading states — drive each through impeccable. After implementation, re-run `/impeccable document`.

### 3. From-scratch reimagining. The previous /providers UX is reference material ONLY.

The current state is not a starting point. Start from PRODUCT.md + DESIGN.md + impeccable + the operator tasks below, and design the page **fresh**.

### 4. BANNED patterns (PRODUCT.md anti-references)

Generic shadcn default · AI-startup landing energy · glitchy / pastiche cyberpunk · SaaS marketing tropes · friendly cartoon warmth · enterprise admin clutter. See PRODUCT.md for the full list.

### 5. Signal Yellow discipline

Yellow ONLY on: primary CTA (≤1 per screen state), focus ring, live-now indicator, selected nav, brand mark, diagnostic highlight in playground. NEVER on body text, hyperlinks, card/panel borders, decorative icons, or non-"live" status indicators.

### 6. Hard verification gates from DESIGN.md (must all pass before close)

- [ ] Placeholder contrast ≥ 4.5:1.
- [ ] Primary button label contrast ≥ 4.5:1.
