---

## 🚨 PLAN MODE + RESEARCH IS MANDATORY 🚨

Before writing any production code, the assignee MUST:

1. **Read the full current `/providers` page implementation** — every component, every store / API call, every state machine. Document file paths in this ticket's notes.
2. **Map the current providers page operator flows** — how does the operator add a provider today? Edit one? Rename one? Delete one? Download a Piper voice? Test a configuration? Each flow gets a one-paragraph "current state" entry in the notes.
3. **Identify the provider plugin schemas** — `backend/app/providers/schema.py` and individual provider definitions — so the modal renders fields dynamically per kind, not via per-kind hardcoded form components.
4. **Identify how dynamic model lists work** for providers that have them (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, etc.) — what endpoint do we call to enumerate models at runtime? Document.
5. **Identify the Piper voice download mechanism** — where does it live today, why does the download button only appear after a provider is added, how do we make it reachable from a clean state?
6. **Enter plan mode** (`EnterPlanMode` / `/plan`) and produce a concrete plan covering: modal component tree, kind-picker, dynamic field rendering, preview/test flow (no save required), dynamic model fetching per provider, rename/delete affordances, Piper download trigger, migration of existing UX (what gets deleted), chrome-devtools MCP validation steps.
7. **Get the plan approved before exiting plan mode and implementing.**

A PR shipping without evidence of phases 1–6 in the ticket notes will be rejected.

---

## Symptoms — the current /providers page UX is broken

User's verbatim frame:

> *"when we're selecting or adding new Piper voices, there is no way to download the model actually because the download opens only after we add the first item. There is just simply no this button."*
>
> *"In 'available adapters' it looks messy."*
>
> *"We just have to click only one plus button, 'add the new provider', then we should select it from the select list, just standard select, and then it should show all the configuration like it was previously, but for some reason it was refactored to a very inconvenient state right now, which doesn't follow any UI guidelines."*
>
> *"Make the modal interface for all of this and ensure that we can play and preview even without saving the things."*
>
> *"Cover all the cases such as previewing, adding new providers, deleting old ones, renaming providers — which is completely missing right now — deleting, selecting from the list, especially when OpenAI it should load all the providers [models]."*

Specific broken behaviours:

- **Piper download is unreachable from a clean state.** The "download voice model" CTA only appears AFTER a Piper provider has been added. A new operator has no way to download a voice model before configuring a provider that needs one.
- **"Available adapters" layout is incoherent.** Multiple inline lists / dropdowns scattered across the page instead of a single normalized entry point.
- **No `+ Add provider` button.** Add affordance is fragmented across provider categories.
- **No rename.** Provider instances cannot be renamed once created.
- **Delete is missing or hidden.** No clear affordance to remove a provider instance.
- **No preview / test before save.** Operator must commit configuration to disk before they can hear / see if it works.
- **Static model lists.** Providers like OpenAI have a huge model catalog that changes over time; the UI doesn't fetch the live model list — operator must guess / paste model IDs.

## Expected UX — single modal CRUD pattern, every operator task through it

ONE **`+ Add provider`** button at the top of the providers page (regardless of category — the modal handles the kind).

Clicking it opens a single modal:

1. **Kind picker** — standard `<select>` (or shadcn-svelte Combobox) listing every available provider plugin. Optionally grouped by category (LLM / TTS / STT). Selecting a kind renders that kind's required fields below.
2. **Configuration fields** — driven by the plugin's schema. Display name (always present), API key / base URL / model / voice / language / etc. as the schema requires.
3. **Dynamic model list** — for providers that publish a model catalog at runtime (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, others), the model field is a Combobox that calls the provider's `list_models` endpoint on demand. Stale catalogs are refreshable via a small refresh icon.
4. **Preview / Test (no save required)** — a Test button runs the configuration against the provider with the current modal state. Returns transcript (STT), generated audio (TTS), text completion (LLM) inline in the modal. Operator can iterate on config without persisting until they're happy.
5. **Piper download (and any other "download model first" provider)** — a `Download voice model` CTA inside the modal when Piper is selected, reachable from a clean modal state. Shows download progress; the modal stays open during the download; on completion the model becomes selectable in the model picker.
6. **Save** — persists the instance with the display name. Modal closes; row appears in the providers list.

The **same modal handles Edit, Rename, and Delete**:

- Clicking an existing row opens the modal pre-filled with that instance's values.
- The display-name field IS the rename affordance — edit it and save.
- Modal footer has a Delete button (with confirmation) that removes the instance.

The providers list view becomes a plain list / table of instances: display name, kind label, primary key field (e.g. model), edit affordance (row click).

## Scope

- Replace the current `/providers` page with the redesigned UX described above.
- Implement the single modal that handles ALL CRUD operations + preview + Piper download.
- Implement dynamic model list fetching for providers that support it.
- Standardize so EVERY provider goes through this single modal — no exceptions.
- Delete the existing scattered inline add UI / per-category dropdowns / out-of-modal download buttons.

## Acceptance criteria — what "done" looks like

- [ ] A single `+ Add provider` button is present at the top of /providers. No inline per-category add controls remain.
- [ ] Clicking the button opens a single modal with a kind-picker `<select>` listing every available provider (LLM + TTS + STT plugins).
- [ ] Selecting a kind dynamically renders the fields required for that kind from the plugin schema (NOT a hardcoded per-kind form).
- [ ] For OpenAI and other providers with a runtime model catalog, the model field fetches live and refreshes on demand.
- [ ] **Preview / Test button works WITHOUT saving** — operator iterates on config inside the modal and gets real results before committing.
- [ ] **Piper voice download is reachable from a clean modal state** — operator can download a voice model before any Piper provider is configured. Download progress visible in the modal.
- [ ] Clicking an existing provider row opens the SAME modal pre-filled — edit / rename / delete all happen inside it.
- [ ] Multi-instance per kind still works (Johnny-stt.7 regression check) — two Ollama instances with different models save independently via the modal.
- [ ] Provider settings persistence layer is unchanged or migrated cleanly — no lost configs.
- [ ] The previous fragmented add / edit / delete UI components are deleted, not just hidden.
- [ ] Every CRUD operation (Add / Edit / Rename / Delete / Preview / Download) works for at least one provider in each category: Anthropic (LLM), Ollama (LLM), Piper (TTS), ElevenLabs (TTS), faster-whisper (STT), Deepgram (STT).
- [ ] No regressions on existing configured providers — they keep working after the redesign.

## Anti-patterns — do not close prematurely

- ❌ *"I produced a plan — closing."* → Reject. Plan is a prerequisite, not the deliverable.
- ❌ *"I read PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md and wrote findings — closing."* → Reject. No code shipped.
- ❌ *"I added the modal but the Piper download is still out-of-modal — closing."* → Reject. Piper download must live inside the modal per the operator flow.
- ❌ *"Preview works but requires save — closing."* → Reject. Preview-without-save is acceptance criterion.
- ❌ *"Unit tests pass — closing."* → Reject. Unit tests do not prove the modal works for users.
- ✅ *"All acceptance checkboxes ticked; chrome-devtools MCP screenshot tour attached covering Add / Edit / Rename / Delete / Preview / Piper-download flows; no console warnings; no 4xx/5xx on save / delete / list-models; closing."* → Accept.

## Validation — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

For each of the following flows, capture: navigate → snapshot → drive → assert → screenshot. Attach all screenshots to the PR.

1. **Empty state**: fresh /providers page with zero providers configured. Assert `+ Add provider` button is visible and reachable.
2. **Piper voice download from clean state**: open modal → pick Piper → download a voice model → assert progress UI → assert model appears in voice selector after completion.
3. **Add Anthropic (static config)**: open modal → pick Anthropic → enter API key + display name → click Test → assert valid response → save → assert row appears.
4. **Add OpenAI (dynamic model list)**: open modal → pick OpenAI → enter API key → assert model dropdown auto-populates with live catalog → pick a model → Test → save.
5. **Add Ollama (multi-instance regression check on Johnny-stt.7)**: add Ollama instance #1 with model A, save. Add Ollama instance #2 with model B, save. Assert both rows appear, both pickable in the playground.
6. **Edit + Rename**: click an existing row → modal opens pre-filled → change display name → save → assert row title updates.
7. **Delete**: click an existing row → modal opens → click Delete → confirm → assert row disappears, no orphan in playground picker.
8. **Preview-without-save**: open modal → pick a TTS provider → enter config → click Test → assert audio plays → close modal WITHOUT saving → assert no new row in providers list.
9. `list_console_messages` clean on every step.
10. `list_network_requests` clean (no 4xx/5xx on save / delete / list-models / download).

## Related

- [[Johnny-fe.2]] — broader /providers page reimagine + shadcn-svelte migration. This ticket lives inside that surface; coordinate so the redesign and migration ship together.
- [[Johnny-stt.8]] — earlier-filed Add/Edit/Delete modal pattern ticket. THIS ticket is the comprehensive version (preview / dynamic models / Piper download / rename / delete all in scope). Johnny-stt.8 should be closed and forwarded here once this is claimed.
- [[Johnny-stt.7]] — multi-instance per-kind regression. Acceptance criterion #5 above is the regression check.
- DESIGN.md component spec (Button / Card / Alert / Badge / Input / Label) — the modal is built from these primitives.

## Priority

P2 — matches the rest of the Johnny-fe epic. Not blocking, but operator-painful right now and the longer it sits the more user goodwill is burned on every interaction with /providers.

## History

Filed 2026-06-07 in response to user direction. Bundles every providers-page UX concern (Piper download reachability, modal-based CRUD, preview-without-save, dynamic model lists, rename, delete, standardized per-kind flow) into one comprehensive redesign ticket, gated on plan-mode research, with mandatory PRODUCT.md / DESIGN.md / impeccable header.

title: REIMAGINE + migrate: Final shadcn-svelte migration audit + cleanup (delete old CSS, ensure parity, full screenshot tour)
description:
## 🚨 MANDATORY before any design or code work 🚨

These rules are non-negotiable. A PR that skipped any of them gets rejected and the ticket reopens.

### 1. Read BOTH `PRODUCT.md` AND `DESIGN.md` at the project root, FIRST.

You may not enter plan mode for this ticket until you have read both files in full. They establish:

- **`PRODUCT.md`** — brand identity, voice, anti-references, design principles. Three-word brand: *composed, deliberate, signal.* Cyberpunk-yellow signal on near-black neutrals. Dark is the primary identity; light is engineered to match but isn't the front cover. Voice: *"confident, technical, terse. Sentences carry information, not enthusiasm. Labels say what will happen (`Stop session`, `Approve reply`), not how the user might feel about it."*
- **`DESIGN.md`** — full design system: OKLCH color tokens, Inter + JetBrains Mono type scale (body at 14px, console density), 8-pt spacing, 6px workhorse radius, Linear/Vercel-precise motion (no bounce / no elastic), the full component spec for Button / Card / Alert / Badge / Input / Label / Separator, layout rules (240px sidebar, no top bar, max-widths per surface type), 8 verification gates.

The current `frontend/src/app.css` ships the stock shadcn-svelte neutral baseline. That is **what this work REPLACES**, not what it preserves.

### 2. Use the `impeccable` skill for every design decision.

Layout, hierarchy, typography, spacing, color, motion, error states, empty states, copy, micro-interactions, accessibility, responsive behaviour — drive every choice through impeccable. After implementation, re-run `/impeccable document` per DESIGN.md's instruction to capture the shipped state and supersede the seed values in the doc.

### 3. From-scratch reimagining. The previous design is reference material ONLY.

Do not start from the existing layout and tweak. Start from PRODUCT.md + DESIGN.md + impeccable + the operator task this surface supports, and design the page **fresh**. Steal nothing reflexively; question every panel, every modal, every button placement.

### 4. BANNED patterns — do not ship these (PRODUCT.md anti-references)

- ❌ **Generic shadcn-svelte default.** Black-and-white neutral, indigo accent, identical card stacks. The "I generated this in five minutes" look. The stock baseline is the START of the migration, not its destination.
- ❌ **AI-startup landing-page energy on app screens.** Gradient hero, hero metrics, "Trusted by" logos, identical icon+heading+text card grids.
- ❌ **Glitchy / pastiche cyberpunk.** Scanlines, chromatic aberration, glitch text effects, all-monospace body, neon outlines on every box, `FUTURE`/`2077`/`SYS://` all-caps labels. The yellow is for *color commitment*, NOT a costume.
- ❌ **SaaS marketing tropes on the dashboard.** Glassmorphism, big tracked uppercase eyebrows above every section, `01 / 02 / 03` numbered markers, gradient text, side-stripe alert borders.
- ❌ **Friendly cartoon / mascot warmth.** No robot illustrations, no emoji-heavy empty states, no "Hi! 👋" copy. Johnny is NAMED but does not anthropomorphize.
- ❌ **Enterprise admin clutter.** Three-pane shells, ribbon toolbars, every-row-has-an-icon density. Density yes, decoration no.

### 5. The Signal Yellow discipline — the single most important rule from DESIGN.md

Signal Yellow (`oklch(0.927 0.176 103)` ≈ `rgb(249, 233, 78)`) appears ON, and ONLY on:

- The **primary CTA** of any given surface — at most **one per screen state**.
- The **focused state** of any interactive element — 2px outline, 2px offset.
- The **live-now indicator** — active-session dot, recording badge, "Johnny is speaking" pulse.
- The **selected / active state in navigation** — sidebar nav `aria-current="page"` gets a 1.5px yellow left-edge accent plus elevated text color.
- The **brand mark / logo** when it appears against a dark surface.
- **Diagnostic highlight** in the playground (in-flight streaming token).

Yellow does **NOT** appear on: body text (ever), hyperlinks in long-form prose, card/panel/separator borders, decorative icons, status indicators that aren't the brand-defined "live" state.

**The test:** if you covered the yellow with a gray of the same value, would the surface still be readable and the hierarchy still legible? Yes → yellow is doing real work. No → the structure needs fixing first.

### 6. Hard verification gates from DESIGN.md (must all pass before close)

- [ ] Body text (`--ink` on `--background`) hits ≥4.5:1 in BOTH dark and light modes.
- [ ] Placeholder text (`--ink-subtle` on `--surface-3`) hits ≥4.5:1.
- [ ] Primary button label (black on yellow) hits ≥4.5:1.
- [ ] Yellow appears on ≤ 3 elements per visible viewport at any moment.
- [ ] No card sits inside another card.
- [ ] No section uses an uppercase tracked eyebrow.
- [ ] Reduced motion honored; active-session pulse degrades to a static state.
- [ ] Screenshot of this surface (dark mode) is unambiguously NOT stock shadcn.

---


## ⚠️ REIMAGINE, not a 1:1 port ⚠️

Do NOT port the existing layout to shadcn-svelte primitives. The goal is to actively reimagine the UX of this surface using shadcn-svelte as a TOOLKIT for BETTER design — not a stylistic re-skin.

For this page:

1. **Audit the current UX critically.** What is awkward? Overcrowded? Hard to find? What does the user struggle with? Inspect the current page via chrome-devtools MCP and review existing user feedback in beads history.
2. **Redesign the information architecture.** Group related controls. Surface the primary action prominently. Defer secondary/tertiary actions to drawers / dialogs / dropdowns. Use shadcn-svelte layout primitives (Card, Tabs, Sheet, ScrollArea, Sidebar) as composition units — not just as replacement components.
3. **Improve interaction patterns.** Replace one-off custom widgets with shadcn-svelte primitives that are familiar and accessible (keyboard nav, focus states, ARIA). Empty / loading / error states get explicit handling via Empty / Skeleton / Alert.
4. **Prove the new UX is materially better via chrome-devtools MCP before/after screenshots in the PR description.** Same task should take fewer clicks / less cognitive load / less scrolling than the previous design.

A pure shadcn-svelte port that preserves the exact information architecture and layout is NOT acceptable. The "after" should look like a thoughtful redesign that happens to use shadcn-svelte primitives.

### Anti-patterns — do not close prematurely

- ❌ *"I produced an approved plan — closing."* → Reject. Plan is a prerequisite, not the deliverable.
- ❌ *"I swapped Button and Input components — closing."* → Reject. No reimagined UX shipped.
- ❌ *"Unit tests pass — closing."* → Reject. Unit tests do not prove the redesign works for users.
- ✅ *"All acceptance criteria checked; chrome-devtools MCP before/after screenshots attached; user flow demonstrably improved (fewer clicks / less scrolling / clearer hierarchy); closing."* → Accept.

---

## Original migration guidance (preserved verbatim from previous ticket)

After all per-page sub-tickets close: (1) remove dead bespoke CSS, unreferenced utilities, hardcoded color values; (2) audit each page in chrome-devtools MCP — full a11y snapshot, console-message log, network-request log (no 404 on stale assets); (3) capture the full screenshot tour required by the parent acceptance criteria — light + dark for every page; (4) confirm no mixed UX (no bespoke Button/Input/Dialog/Select/Modal/Tabs/Card next to a shadcn one). Only after this passes can [[Johnny-fe]] be closed.

## 2026-06-06 — Foundation tokens shipped; final audit BLOCKED on .1–.8

### What shipped

- frontend/src/app.css: replaced the stock shadcn neutral baseline with the DESIGN.md OKLCH token set in both :root (light) and .dark (primary identity). Added every new token DESIGN.md introduces beyond shadcn — --surface-1/2/3, --ink, --ink-muted, --ink-subtle, --ink-on-yellow, --border-strong, --separator, --primary-hover, --primary-pressed, --success, --warning, --info, --glow-primary, motion vars, z-index vars. Added 2px Signal-Yellow focus ring (focus-visible only), prefers-reduced-motion fallback, and the .live-pulse keyframe with reduced-motion degrade.
- frontend/src/app.html: Inter + JetBrains Mono via Google Fonts (display=swap). Production self-host migration is a separate concern (CLAUDE.md font rule applies before README screenshot).

### Verification gates status

PASS — gate 1 (--ink on --background: 17.91 dark, 18.86 light); gate 2 (--ink-subtle on --surface-3: 4.64 dark, 7.49 light — lifted from L=0.55/0.60 to 0.62/0.40 to clear AA per DESIGN.md §Input verify-after-implementation note); gate 3 (--primary-foreground on --primary: 16.09); gate 7 (reduced motion: CSS gate + .live-pulse degrade); gate 8 (NOT stock shadcn — dark + Signal Yellow scheme is unambiguously not the indigo neutral baseline).

FAIL/BLOCKED on .1–.8 — gate 4 (yellow on > 3 elements; providers chips are undisciplined); gate 5 (card-in-card; providers content card holds a list of provider cards); gate 6 (uppercase tracked eyebrows: ADD A NEW STT (SPEECH-TO-TEXT) PROVIDER, AUTHENTICATION, MODEL, ADVANCED — all .2 page).

### Audit screenshots

- .ralph-tui/iterations/fe9_home_default.png — light; header still hardcoded bg-slate-900 (= .1 work)
- .ralph-tui/iterations/fe9_home_dark.png — dark; main content adopts tokens, shell does not
- .ralph-tui/iterations/fe9_providers_dark.png — providers in dark; all .2 audit failures visible

### Why this is open, not closed

The acceptance criteria for the final audit include 'no card-in-card', 'no uppercase tracked eyebrow', and 'yellow on ≤ 3 elements per viewport'. The current providers page (and every page under .1–.8) violates these because the per-page reimagining has not happened. Closing on foundation-only would be the documented close-discipline anti-pattern ('I swapped Button and Input — closing'). Reopens when .1–.8 are properly closed.

### Quality gates

- pnpm build: PASS (2.42s)
- pnpm lint: 1 pre-existing error in providers/+page.svelte:235 — unused configuredRowsFor; unrelated to this work. Should be fixed in .2 / Johnny-stt.7 follow-up.

### Deps added

Johnny-fe.9 now blocks on Johnny-fe.1..8 in bd. The final audit can only run after every per-page redesign closes.

These rules are non-negotiable. A PR that skipped any of them gets rejected and the ticket reopens.

### 1. Read BOTH `PRODUCT.md` AND `DESIGN.md` at the project root, FIRST.

You may not enter plan mode for this ticket until you have read both files in full. They establish:

- **`PRODUCT.md`** — brand identity, voice, anti-references, design principles. Three-word brand: *composed, deliberate, signal.* Cyberpunk-yellow signal on near-black neutrals. Dark is the primary identity; light is engineered to match but isn't the front cover. Voice: *"confident, technical, terse. Sentences carry information, not enthusiasm. Labels say what will happen (`Stop session`, `Approve reply`), not how the user might feel about it."*
- **`DESIGN.md`** — full design system: OKLCH color tokens, Inter + JetBrains Mono type scale (body at 14px, console density), 8-pt spacing, 6px workhorse radius, Linear/Vercel-precise motion (no bounce / no elastic), the full component spec for Button / Card / Alert / Badge / Input / Label / Separator, layout rules (240px sidebar, no top bar, max-widths per surface type), 8 verification gates.

The current `frontend/src/app.css` ships the stock shadcn-svelte neutral baseline. That is **what this work REPLACES**, not what it preserves.

### 2. Use the `impeccable` skill for every design decision.

Layout, hierarchy, typography, spacing, color, motion, error states, empty states, copy, micro-interactions, accessibility, responsive behaviour — drive every choice through impeccable. After implementation, re-run `/impeccable document` per DESIGN.md's instruction to capture the shipped state and supersede the seed values in the doc.

### 3. From-scratch reimagining. The previous design is reference material ONLY.

Do not start from the existing layout and tweak. Start from PRODUCT.md + DESIGN.md + impeccable + the operator task this surface supports, and design the page **fresh**. Steal nothing reflexively; question every panel, every modal, every button placement.

### 4. BANNED patterns — do not ship these (PRODUCT.md anti-references)

- ❌ **Generic shadcn-svelte default.** Black-and-white neutral, indigo accent, identical card stacks. The "I generated this in five minutes" look. The stock baseline is the START of the migration, not its destination.
- ❌ **AI-startup landing-page energy on app screens.** Gradient hero, hero metrics, "Trusted by" logos, identical icon+heading+text card grids.
- ❌ **Glitchy / pastiche cyberpunk.** Scanlines, chromatic aberration, glitch text effects, all-monospace body, neon outlines on every box, `FUTURE`/`2077`/`SYS://` all-caps labels. The yellow is for *color commitment*, NOT a costume.
- ❌ **SaaS marketing tropes on the dashboard.** Glassmorphism, big tracked uppercase eyebrows above every section, `01 / 02 / 03` numbered markers, gradient text, side-stripe alert borders.
- ❌ **Friendly cartoon / mascot warmth.** No robot illustrations, no emoji-heavy empty states, no "Hi! 👋" copy. Johnny is NAMED but does not anthropomorphize.
- ❌ **Enterprise admin clutter.** Three-pane shells, ribbon toolbars, every-row-has-an-icon density. Density yes, decoration no.

### 5. The Signal Yellow discipline — the single most important rule from DESIGN.md

Signal Yellow (`oklch(0.927 0.176 103)` ≈ `rgb(249, 233, 78)`) appears ON, and ONLY on:

- The **primary CTA** of any given surface — at most **one per screen state**.
- The **focused state** of any interactive element — 2px outline, 2px offset.
- The **live-now indicator** — active-session dot, recording badge, "Johnny is speaking" pulse.
- The **selected / active state in navigation** — sidebar nav `aria-current="page"` gets a 1.5px yellow left-edge accent plus elevated text color.
- The **brand mark / logo** when it appears against a dark surface.
- **Diagnostic highlight** in the playground (in-flight streaming token).

Yellow does **NOT** appear on: body text (ever), hyperlinks in long-form prose, card/panel/separator borders, decorative icons, status indicators that aren't the brand-defined "live" state.

**The test:** if you covered the yellow with a gray of the same value, would the surface still be readable and the hierarchy still legible? Yes → yellow is doing real work. No → the structure needs fixing first.

### 6. Hard verification gates from DESIGN.md (must all pass before close)

- [ ] Body text (`--ink` on `--background`) hits ≥4.5:1 in BOTH dark and light modes.
- [ ] Placeholder text (`--ink-subtle` on `--surface-3`) hits ≥4.5:1.
- [ ] Primary button label (black on yellow) hits ≥4.5:1.
- [ ] Yellow appears on ≤ 3 elements per visible viewport at any moment.
- [ ] No card sits inside another card.
- [ ] No section uses an uppercase tracked eyebrow.
- [ ] Reduced motion honored; active-session pulse degrades to a static state.
- [ ] Screenshot of this surface (dark mode) is unambiguously NOT stock shadcn.

---


## ⚠️ REIMAGINE, not a 1:1 port ⚠️

Do NOT port the existing layout to shadcn-svelte primitives. The goal is to actively reimagine the UX of this surface using shadcn-svelte as a TOOLKIT for BETTER design — not a stylistic re-skin.

For this page:

1. **Audit the current UX critically.** What is awkward? Overcrowded? Hard to find? What does the user struggle with? Inspect the current page via chrome-devtools MCP and review existing user feedback in beads history.
2. **Redesign the information architecture.** Group related controls. Surface the primary action prominently. Defer secondary/tertiary actions to drawers / dialogs / dropdowns. Use shadcn-svelte layout primitives (Card, Tabs, Sheet, ScrollArea, Sidebar) as composition units — not just as replacement components.
3. **Improve interaction patterns.** Replace one-off custom widgets with shadcn-svelte primitives that are familiar and accessible (keyboard nav, focus states, ARIA). Empty / loading / error states get explicit handling via Empty / Skeleton / Alert.
4. **Prove the new UX is materially better via chrome-devtools MCP before/after screenshots in the PR description.** Same task should take fewer clicks / less cognitive load / less scrolling than the previous design.

A pure shadcn-svelte port that preserves the exact information architecture and layout is NOT acceptable. The "after" should look like a thoughtful redesign that happens to use shadcn-svelte primitives.

### Anti-patterns — do not close prematurely

- ❌ *"I produced an approved plan — closing."* → Reject. Plan is a prerequisite, not the deliverable.
- ❌ *"I swapped Button and Input components — closing."* → Reject. No reimagined UX shipped.
- ❌ *"Unit tests pass — closing."* → Reject. Unit tests do not prove the redesign works for users.
- ✅ *"All acceptance criteria checked; chrome-devtools MCP before/after screenshots attached; user flow demonstrably improved (fewer clicks / less scrolling / clearer hierarchy); closing."* → Accept.

---

## Original migration guidance (preserved verbatim from previous ticket)

Migrate the playground page to shadcn-svelte. Includes: Configure card (Select for decision mode/template, Input for persona, collapsible Advanced section), Start session Button, chat thread, mic input with live STT partials, voice playback controls. Replace with Card, Select, Input, Textarea, Button, Toggle (mic), and possibly Accordion for Advanced. Verify via chrome-devtools MCP: navigate to /playground, snapshot, start a free-playground session (mocked or real), send a chat message, click mic icon, screenshot light + dark. Child of [[Johnny-fe]].

- Root layout shell (sidebar, header, sessions panel, approvals panel)
- /providers
- /playground
- /calendar
- /settings
- /templates
- /history list + detail
- /sessions/[id] detail

title: REDO: Frontend migration to shadcn-svelte — ACTUALLY migrate components (Johnny-stt.9 was closed after research only, no code shipped); every step verified via chrome-devtools MCP
description:
## Why this ticket exists

[[Johnny-stt.9]] was filed to migrate the entire frontend to shadcn-svelte (https://www.shadcn-svelte.com, per https://www.shadcn-svelte.com/llms.txt). The assigned agent closed it with the reason *"Completed by agent"* — but **no migration actually shipped**. Only research happened. No components were swapped, no pages were converted, the app still renders with its previous bespoke component set.

User's verbatim frame:

> *"the migration task was closed but not [done]. You have to create another one with the context of the previous one. It did only research and it did not any migration nothing super stupid. Also ensure that everything is being tested in chrome-devtools MCP."*

So this ticket re-files the work with two hard rules:

1. **"Done" means actual component-by-component migration is shipped** — files swapped, old components deleted, dark theme working, every page rendered through shadcn-svelte primitives. Research alone does not close this ticket.
2. **Every migration step is verified in the real browser via chrome-devtools MCP** — not just at the end, but per surface as it lands. A surface without a chrome-devtools MCP screenshot tour is not considered migrated.

## Goal (unchanged from Johnny-stt.9)

Migrate the **entire** frontend to **shadcn-svelte** as the single component library. Every page, every component, every form, every modal, every list, every button uses shadcn-svelte primitives. No bespoke alternatives where a shadcn-svelte primitive exists.

Reference: **https://www.shadcn-svelte.com/llms.txt** — follow these instructions to the letter for setup, theming, and component patterns.

## What "done" means (precise — closes the loophole that sank Johnny-stt.9)

This ticket may NOT be closed unless ALL of the following are true:

- [ ] shadcn-svelte is installed AND configured (`components.json`, Tailwind config, CSS variables, theme tokens all in place per llms.txt).
- [ ] At least one shadcn-svelte primitive **replaces** its bespoke counterpart in the codebase — old component deleted, new one referenced in the app. (NOT just imported; actually rendered on a real page.)
- [ ] **Every page in the app** has been visited via chrome-devtools MCP and screenshotted. The screenshots are attached to the PR.
- [ ] **Every reusable component in `lib/components/`** (or wherever shared components live) has been migrated to shadcn-svelte or explicitly justified as out-of-library (e.g., domain-specific that has no shadcn equivalent).
- [ ] No mixed UX: nowhere in the app does a bespoke Button / Input / Dialog / Select / Modal / Tabs / Card / etc. sit next to a shadcn-svelte one. Either the surface is fully migrated or it's part of a documented phased rollout with a tracking sub-ticket.
- [ ] All existing user flows still work end-to-end: provider settings, playground (chat + voice), calendar import, session list, session detail, sign-in. **Each verified via chrome-devtools MCP**, not just unit tests.
- [ ] No console warnings in chrome-devtools MCP on any major surface.
- [ ] No 404s in chrome-devtools MCP network panel for stale CSS / removed assets.

The phrase "research is complete" or "package is installed" does NOT satisfy this ticket. Neither does "plan was written". Only the above checklist closes it.

## 🚨 PLAN MODE IS MANDATORY, BUT PLAN MODE IS NOT THE GOAL 🚨

Plan mode prevents repeating Johnny-stt.2's reckless build. But plan mode is also where the previous agent stopped — they planned, then closed. To prevent that:

1. **Plan mode produces a plan, not a deliverable.** The plan is reviewed and approved. Then implementation begins. Closing the ticket on the plan alone is incorrect.
2. **Implementation has its own definition of done** (the checklist above).
3. **Implementation is verified by browser screenshots from chrome-devtools MCP** — the screenshots are the proof. Without them, the ticket stays open.

### Required plan-mode pass

The assignee MUST:

1. **Read https://www.shadcn-svelte.com/llms.txt fully.**
2. **Inventory the current frontend** — every page, every reusable component, every form, every modal. Cross-reference each to its shadcn-svelte replacement.
3. **Identify in-flight UI surfaces** — coordinate with whoever is working on Johnny-stt.4, .8 so their UI work lands in shadcn-svelte primitives, not bespoke.
4. **Enter plan mode** and produce a concrete plan covering:
   - Installation + theming setup (Tailwind config, components.json, CSS variables).
   - Per-surface migration order (probably: shared shell → navigation → settings pages → playground → calendar → modals).
   - Cutover strategy — big-bang single PR or staged surface-by-surface PRs.
   - The chrome-devtools MCP validation tour: for each surface, navigate → take_snapshot → take_screenshot, and what state to verify.
   - Whether to split into sub-tickets per surface.
5. **Get the plan approved.**
6. **Then implement.**
7. **Then validate via chrome-devtools MCP per the tour above.**
8. **Then attach screenshots to the PR.**
9. **Then close.**

A close that happens before step 7 is invalid and will be reopened.

## Scope

Same as Johnny-stt.9:

- Install shadcn-svelte per llms.txt.
- Configure Tailwind, design tokens, theming (light + dark if applicable).
- Migrate every existing UI component to its shadcn-svelte equivalent.
- Delete the previous component implementations once their shadcn-svelte replacements are in place.
- Ensure no mixed UX.

## Out of scope

- Adding new features that don't exist today.
- Backend / provider plugin changes.
- The actual content / copy of any page.

## Acceptance criteria (the checklist that closes the ticket)

- [ ] shadcn-svelte installed, configured, and themed per llms.txt — repo follows the canonical structure (`components.json`, `lib/components/ui/`, etc.).
- [ ] Every existing page in the app renders using shadcn-svelte primitives.
- [ ] Theming (light + dark if applicable) works across every surface.
- [ ] All existing user flows still work end-to-end (playground, settings, calendar, sign-in, session management) — no functional regressions.
- [ ] No dead code: old bespoke components, unreferenced CSS, orphaned utilities are removed.
- [ ] Visual consistency: spacing, typography, color usage match shadcn-svelte conventions across every surface.
- [ ] **Chrome-devtools MCP screenshot tour attached to the PR** — at minimum: home / dashboard, provider settings (each tab if applicable), playground (idle + with chat), calendar import, session list, session detail, sign-in flow. Each screenshot taken via `mcp__chrome-devtools__take_screenshot`.
- [ ] **Chrome-devtools MCP console-message log attached** showing zero warnings on each surface.
- [ ] **Chrome-devtools MCP network-request log attached** showing no 404s on stale assets.

## Validation — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP, per surface, throughout the migration

Not just at the end — this is integrated into the workflow. For EACH surface being migrated:

1. `mcp__chrome-devtools__navigate_page` → the surface URL.
2. `mcp__chrome-devtools__take_snapshot` — assert the surface still renders with the migrated components.
3. Drive the key interaction on that surface (e.g. on provider settings: open the add-provider modal; on playground: send a chat message; on calendar: import an event).
4. `mcp__chrome-devtools__list_console_messages` — assert no errors / warnings.
5. `mcp__chrome-devtools__list_network_requests` — assert no 4xx/5xx on the surface's resources.
6. `mcp__chrome-devtools__take_screenshot` — capture for the PR.

Repeat per surface. A surface without this evidence is not migrated.

## Anti-patterns (do not repeat Johnny-stt.9's premature close)

- ❌ "I read llms.txt and the existing code — closing as research complete."  → Reject. Reopen the ticket.
- ❌ "I installed shadcn-svelte and configured Tailwind — closing."  → Reject. No components migrated.
- ❌ "I migrated the Button component — closing."  → Reject. Every primitive must be migrated AND verified per surface.
- ❌ "Unit tests pass — closing."  → Reject. Unit tests do not prove the UI works. Chrome-devtools MCP screenshots do.
- ✅ "All checklist items above marked true; chrome-devtools MCP screenshots attached; user-facing flows verified end-to-end in browser; closing."  → Accept.

## Open questions

- Does the existing Tailwind config conflict with shadcn-svelte's expected setup?
- Is there a dark-mode story today? How does it map to shadcn-svelte's theme tokens?
- Single big-bang PR or staged migration? Decide during plan mode.
- Should this be promoted to an epic and split into per-surface sub-tickets? Acceptable if the assignee deems necessary — but the parent ticket then tracks the overall closure.

## Related

- [[Johnny-stt.9]] — the previous attempt. Closed after research only, no code shipped. This ticket is the redo.
- [[Johnny-stt.8]] — Add/Edit/Delete modal pattern. Depends on this migration so its work lands in shadcn-svelte primitives.
- [[Johnny-stt.4]] — VoiceInk parity bundle. Will use whatever component primitives this migration produces.

## History

Filed 2026-06-06 because Johnny-stt.9 was closed prematurely by an agent after research only — no code shipped, no components migrated, no chrome-devtools MCP validation. This ticket re-files the work with strict definition-of-done and chrome-devtools MCP validation embedded per surface, not bolted on at the end.

- shadcn-svelte foundation per llms.txt: components.json, src/app.css (full theme tokens, light + dark, oklch), src/lib/utils.ts (cn helper), Tailwind v4 wired via @tailwindcss/vite.

**Why NOT closing the parent:** The acceptance criteria require EVERY page migrated, EVERY surface chrome-devtools MCP toured in light + dark, and dead bespoke CSS removed — ~10k lines of Svelte across 10 pages. The bead description explicitly permits sub-tickets and says the parent then tracks overall closure. Parent stays OPEN until .10.9 closes. title: Provider settings UX: replace embedded per-category 'Add new X provider' dropdowns with a single 'Add provider' button → modal → reusable Add/Edit/Delete pattern (REQUIRES PLAN MODE)
description:
## Symptom — current Add-provider UX is an anti-pattern

Adding a new provider in the current settings UX is structured in a deeply unusual way:

- The page has **separate inline "Add new LLM provider" / "Add new TTS provider" / etc. sections**, each with its own embedded dropdown list of provider kinds, each rendered directly into the page.
- There are multiple parallel dropdown lists scattered across the page (one per provider category) instead of a single normalized entry point.
- There is **no single "Add provider" affordance** that users expect from standard CRUD UX.
- Editing an existing provider is not a click-the-row-it-opens-a-form interaction; there is no consistent edit modal.

User's verbatim frame:

> *"yes now it supports adding multiple providers, but this is stupidly stupid... There's a super anti-pattern of user experience... Why the fuck we configure some providers and then we have 'add a new LLM provider' with the stupidest list with providers — why can't we just have a button 'add provider', we click on that, we use just the regular select, we select the provider which we want to add (Anthropic or Google Gemini, whatever we need), then it shows all the fields that we need to fill up, we put the name and click save. And then we reuse this modal to edit the provider — we just click on the provider, it opens the modal and we can edit. Or we can delete. What the fuck is wrong... Why don't it use the past and the popular user experience practices."*

The user is asking, with reason: this is a solved problem in standard UX. Why was it reinvented poorly?

## Expected UX — standard CRUD modal pattern

One **"+ Add provider" button** at the top of the provider settings surface (regardless of LLM / TTS / STT category — the modal handles the category choice).

Clicking it opens a **single modal** with this flow:

1. **Step 1 — pick the provider kind.** A single `<select>` (or equivalent dropdown / combobox / searchable list) listing every available provider: Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, openai-compatible, Piper, ElevenLabs (TTS), Deepgram (STT), faster-whisper, Parakeet, OpenAI Realtime, etc. Optionally grouped by category (LLM / TTS / STT) in the dropdown.
2. **Step 2 — fill in the fields.** Once a kind is selected, the modal renders the fields required for that kind (display name, API key, base URL, model, voice, language, etc. — exact fields driven by the provider's schema).
3. **Step 3 — name and save.** User gives the instance a display name (e.g. "Ollama — Qwen 35B") and clicks Save. Modal closes, the new instance appears in the list.

The **same modal is reused for Edit and Delete**:

- Clicking an existing provider row opens the modal pre-filled with the instance's current values.
- The user can edit any field and click Save → updates the row.
- The modal has a Delete button (with a small confirmation) that removes the instance.

The provider list view becomes a plain table / list of instances: name, kind, key fields, edit affordance (row click), no inline add controls.

## 🚨 PLAN MODE IS MANDATORY 🚨

Same rule as [[Johnny-stt.5]]: do not start coding. The previous provider-UX implementation was shipped without planning and produced the current anti-pattern. The fix must not repeat that mistake.

Before writing any production code on this ticket, the assignee MUST:

1. Read the current provider-settings UI — every per-category "Add new X provider" section, every embedded dropdown, every save handler. Document each in the ticket notes.
2. Read the existing modal / dialog component library in the frontend — is there a shared modal component? Is there an existing form abstraction (e.g. a JSON-schema-driven form)? If yes, reuse it. If no, document the decision to add one.
3. Read the provider plugin schemas (`backend/app/providers/schema.py` and individual provider definitions) — confirm the per-kind field set is discoverable so the modal can render fields dynamically.

title: Provider settings regression: cannot add multiple providers of the same kind (DB allows it, new UI/API blocks it) — Ollama save fails with 'conflicts with another provider with the same kind/name/display'
description:
## Symptom

Trying to save a second provider of the same kind (e.g. a second Ollama LLM provider with a different model) fails with the validation error:

> *conflicts with another provider with the same kind/name/display*

The database row is never persisted. The new provider-settings UX rework (shipped under [[Johnny-stt.2]]) silently changed the contract from **N providers per kind** to **1 provider per kind** — without migrating the DB and without telling users.

User's verbatim frame:

> *"previously we could add the same type of providers multiple times. But now it's limited only to one provider at a time. However, the database wasn't fixed. We still need to be able to add multiple providers, even the same one. For example, I can add multiple OLAMA providers, but I can choose different models just for plane."*

> *"add a new task. Highest priority."*

## What worked before (and must work again)

The previous UX let users add multiple instances of the same provider kind, each with their own display name and config:

- *Ollama (Qwen 35B)* — kind=ollama, base URL=..., model=qwen-35b
- *Ollama (Llama 3 8B)* — kind=ollama, base URL=..., model=llama-3-8b
- *Ollama (some-finetune)* — kind=ollama, base URL=..., model=some-finetune

The user could then pick any of these per session / event / playground action.

The same applies to every other provider kind: multiple OpenAI keys for different orgs/projects, multiple Anthropic, multiple Piper TTS voices grouped as instances, multiple ElevenLabs with different default voices, multiple Deepgram with different language defaults, etc.

## Current broken behaviour

- Add an Ollama provider (instance A). Save: ✅.
- Add a second Ollama provider with a different model (instance B). Save: ❌ `conflicts with another provider with the same kind/name/display`.
- The DB schema still allows multiple rows — only the API / save-validation layer blocks it.
- Net effect: users with multi-instance setups can no longer configure their app. Nothing works properly until this is fixed.

## Root cause (user's hypothesis)

> *"exactly the missed interface opportunity and skipping the logic of multiple providers"*

The new provider UX appears to enforce a uniqueness check at the API / validation layer on `(kind, name, display)` — but the underlying DB has no such constraint (and shouldn't). So the UX is **inconsistent with the schema**, and the UI was never built to model "N instances per kind" in the first place.

## Fix shape (investigation, not prescription)

The assignee will need to:

1. Find the save-validation rule that emits the *"conflicts with another provider with the same kind/name/display"* error. Remove or correct the bogus uniqueness check.
2. Confirm the DB schema allows multiple rows per kind (per user, it already does — verify).
3. Rework the provider-settings UI to model **provider instances** (each with its own ID, display name, and config) rather than **one config per kind**:
   - List view shows each instance as a row with name/display + kind label + edit/remove.
   - Add button creates a new instance, not "edit the existing kind".
   - Each kind can have arbitrarily many instances.
4. Every UX surface that picks a provider (session start, event config, playground, voice picker, model picker, etc.) must reference an **instance ID**, not a kind. Audit and update each call site.
5. Migrate any existing single-instance config rows so they show up as named instances in the new model (don't lose user data).

This overlaps heavily with [[Johnny-stt.5]] (the unified provider-UX refactor). The work should not be duplicated — either:
- This fix lands first (urgent), and Johnny-stt.5 builds on it; OR
- Johnny-stt.5 folds this scope in and we close this ticket as superseded.

The assignee should coordinate with whoever is working on Johnny-stt.5 before starting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User can add **multiple Ollama providers**, each with a distinct display name and a distinct model — both save successfully, both appear in the list.
- [ ] Same for **OpenAI, Anthropic, Piper, ElevenLabs, Deepgram, OpenAI Realtime, faster-whisper** — any provider kind, multiple instances allowed.
- [ ] The provider settings UI lists every instance separately with its own display name, kind label, edit, and remove affordances.
- [ ] The *"conflicts with another provider with the same kind/name/display"* error never fires for a legitimate new instance.
- [ ] Session / event / playground UX selects providers by **instance ID**, not by kind. Two Ollama instances can be picked independently for two different sessions.
- [ ] Existing single-instance user configs are migrated cleanly to the instance model — no user data lost.
- [ ] Regression test in `backend/tests/` covers: create 2 instances of the same kind, save both, list both, select each independently. Test fails today; passes after fix.
- [ ] No regression on the single-instance happy path (a user who only ever has one provider of a kind still works fine).

## Validation — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

1. `navigate_page` → provider settings (wherever the unified UX lives — see Johnny-stt.5 for the refactor target).
2. `take_snapshot`.
3. Add Ollama instance A (display: "Ollama Qwen 35B", model: qwen-35b). Save — assert success, assert it appears in the list.
4. Add Ollama instance B (display: "Ollama Llama 3 8B", model: llama-3-8b). Save — assert success (no "conflicts" error), assert both instances now in the list.
5. `list_console_messages` and `list_network_requests` — assert no 4xx/5xx on either save.
6. Open the playground, `take_snapshot` of the provider picker — assert both Ollama instances selectable independently.
7. Send a message picking instance A, assert qwen-35b responds. Repeat with instance B, assert llama-3-8b responds.
8. `take_screenshot` of: settings list with both instances visible, playground picker showing both, response from each.

## Related

- [[Johnny-stt.5]] — major refactor of unified provider-settings UX (LLM + TTS + STT). This ticket is one specific symptom that .5 addresses. Coordinate to avoid duplicate work; if .5 ships first, this can close as superseded.
- [[Johnny-stt.2]] — Catalog UI (CLOSED) that introduced the regression by modelling "one config per kind".
- Any existing per-session-provider picker code that references a provider by `kind` rather than `instance_id` is in scope to audit.

## Priority

**P0 — Highest.** User explicitly flagged this as highest priority because the app is functionally unusable for any setup with multiple providers of the same kind, which is the common case (multiple Ollama models, multiple OpenAI keys, multiple Piper voices grouped as instances, etc.).

title: Refactor and unify ALL provider settings UX (LLM + TTS + STT) into one cohesive provider page — explore existing code FIRST, integrate everything, REQUIRES PLAN MODE
description:
## Symptom — current state of provider settings is fragmented

The provider-settings UX in this app is incoherent:

- **STT catalog page** (shipped under [[Johnny-stt.2]]) was added as a **standalone page** that is **not reachable from the main menu / navigation** and does not share visual or interaction patterns with the rest of the app.
- **LLM provider settings** live somewhere else, with their own UX (TBD by code exploration — the assignee will map this).
- **TTS provider settings** live somewhere else again, with yet another UX (TBD by code exploration).

User's verbatim frame:

> *"this kind of like user experience and user interface that was added is absurdly stupid because we can't even open this page to our menu or UI"*

> *"we had this UI catalogue for providers but it ... is not being integrated with the functionality that we had. We had special tab provider but for some reason ... everything like should be unified"*

> *"create a super huge refactor and rework of the provider's page including all our LLM TTS and STT things"*

> *"Everything inside of that epic"* — the refactor must cover everything in the Johnny-stt epic, alongside the existing LLM + TTS provider surfaces.

## Expected end state

**One unified Provider Settings surface in the app**, with:

1. A **single entry** in the main menu / app navigation (e.g. "Settings → Providers" — exact naming determined during plan).
2. **LLM, TTS, and STT each live as a tab (or sibling section)** inside that one surface — no separate isolated pages for any of them.

6. **No regressions** on any existing LLM, TTS, or STT functionality.

This ticket exists because the previous attempt ([[Johnny-stt.2]]) shipped without planning and produced a disconnected page. That will not happen again.

The assignee **must** complete the following BEFORE writing any production code:

### Phase 1 — codebase exploration

   - Persistence layer — same backend endpoint pattern, or different?
3. Identify the main menu / navigation file(s) and where provider-settings entries live (or don't).
4. Document findings inline in this ticket's `--notes`.

### Phase 2 — plan mode
5. **Enter plan mode** (`EnterPlanMode` / `/plan`) and produce a concrete plan that covers:
   - The unified component tree (which shell, which tabs, which shared sub-components).
   - File-level migration: which files get added, which get edited, which get **deleted** (the standalone STT page from .2 should go away; duplicated form components should be consolidated).
   - Menu / navigation change: where the single Provider Settings entry lives and what label it carries.
   - Persistence-layer change (if any): unified config API vs. per-category endpoints.
   - The chrome-devtools MCP validation steps for the final UX.
   - Explicit list of regressions to verify against (existing LLM / TTS provider flows must keep working).
6. **Get the plan approved before exiting plan mode.**

### Phase 3 — implement
7. Only after sign-off, implement and validate.

A PR that lacks evidence of phases 1 + 2 (exploration findings in `--notes`, an approved plan) will be rejected.

## Scope

This is a **major refactor**, not a small add-on. Touches:
- LLM provider settings UI (refactor to fit the unified shell).
- TTS provider settings UI (refactor to fit the unified shell).
- STT catalog UI (move from standalone page to a tab inside the unified shell — the page shipped under Johnny-stt.2 gets deleted as part of this).
- Main menu / app navigation (single entry).
- Any shared form / field / button / state components needed to make the three tabs visually + interactionally consistent.
- Backend persistence layer (if needed to unify per-category save endpoints).

## Out of scope

- Adding **new** providers (that's Johnny-stt.4 and any future provider tickets).
- Changing provider **plugin** code under `backend/app/providers/` — only the UI / settings layer.
- Streaming-input UX in the chat (that's Johnny-stt.3).
- Replacing the playground or any non-settings surface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Single menu entry** for Provider Settings in the main navigation, reachable from app entry in ≤ 2 clicks.

- [ ] The standalone STT catalog page from Johnny-stt.2 (route + component) is **deleted**, not just hidden.
- [ ] Existing LLM provider flows still work end-to-end (regression: pick provider, edit config, save, test → unchanged behaviour).
- [ ] Existing TTS provider flows still work end-to-end (same regression check).
- [ ] STT provider flows (including the Johnny-stt.2 Test button) work inside the new unified tab.
- [ ] No dead code: orphaned components, unreferenced routes, duplicated form widgets are removed.
- [ ] Exploration findings + approved plan are documented in this ticket before any production code lands.

## Validation — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

1. `navigate_page` → app root.
2. `take_snapshot` of the main menu / navigation — assert exactly one Provider Settings entry is visible.
3. `click` the Provider Settings entry.
4. `take_snapshot` — assert LLM, TTS, STT tabs (or sibling sections) all visible.
5. For each tab:
   - `click` the tab.
   - `take_snapshot` — assert the provider list renders.
   - `click` a provider in that tab; verify the config form renders with consistent layout vs. the other tabs.
   - For LLM / TTS / STT — run an end-to-end smoke (save a setting, verify it persists; for STT, also exercise the Test button → transcript flow from Johnny-stt.2's acceptance).
6. `take_screenshot` of each of the three tabs side-by-side comparison for the PR description.

title: Live streaming STT in playground chat input (mic icon + partial transcripts as user speaks)
description:
## Why
User wants to see the speech-recognition output appear instantly in the chat as they speak — explicitly asked to keep this as a separate ticket from the Parakeet integration.

## Scope
- Mic icon in the playground chat input.
- While held (or toggled), audio streams from browser → backend WebSocket → selected streaming-capable STT provider.
- Partial transcripts render in-place in the chat input as the user speaks.
- On stop/release, the final transcript becomes the message body and is sendable.
- Provider switch lives in the catalog (Johnny-stt.2). Default: Parakeet local (Johnny-stt.1). Fallback: Deepgram / AssemblyAI / ElevenLabs streaming.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Mic toggle visible in the playground chat input.
- [ ] First partial transcript visible ≤ 500ms after start of speech (Parakeet local target; cloud providers may be higher).
- [ ] Partials update at ≥ 2 Hz.
- [ ] On stop, the final transcript replaces partials and the message becomes sendable.
- [ ] Changing the selected STT provider in the catalog changes the streaming source on the next session.
- [ ] Mic-permission denial shows a usable error, not a silent failure.

## Validation
- Backend: WebSocket frame test with synthetic PCM stream and an assertion that partials are emitted ≥ N times.
- Frontend: component test for the mic toggle state machine.
- **Browser (chrome-devtools MCP):** navigate to /playground → grant mic → press mic button → assert `[data-partial-transcript]` updates ≥ 3 times → release → assert chat input contains final transcript → screenshot for PR.

## Depends on
- Johnny-stt.1 (Parakeet, default streaming provider)
- Johnny-stt.2 (catalog UI exposes the provider switch)

title: Profile + tune end-to-end voice latency on real local STT/TTS/LLM, and add in-UI optimization tips on each provider settings page
description:
## Why this exists

Even when Local Piper is working, time-to-first-audio feels long. The user explicitly wants to (a) measure where the time goes on real models, (b) actually adjust settings to reduce it, and (c) capture the resulting know-how directly inside the provider settings UI so the next person tuning a model is not flying blind.

Sibling task [[per-session-activity-timing-log-surfaced-in-chat-history-per-turn-pipeline-events-with-durations]] (Johnny-ckz.7) ships the activity-log surface that this work feeds and that this work also exercises as its own measurement instrument.

## Constraints

- **Real models only.** No mocks. Use the providers exported in /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json (seed via JOHNNY_PROVIDERS_FILE per Johnny-d3e / Johnny-k3z).
- Cover Local Piper TTS, Local Whisper STT, and at least one local LLM (the JSON should have one configured; if not, document the gap and proceed with what is configured).
- Profile the **full path the user feels**: VAD-detected user-speech-end → first audible byte out. Not just synthesis time.

## Investigation deliverables

1. **Latency map** per provider on real models: VAD end → STT first-partial → STT final → LLM first-token → LLM total → TTS first-byte → first audio chunk delivered to the transport. Capture p50 + p95 from at least 20 turns of varied length.
2. **Bottleneck attribution** with evidence (logs / traces / activity-log entries from Johnny-ckz.7).
3. **Concrete optimizations applied** to the codebase / configs, not just recommendations. Likely candidates:
   - Persistent piper process per voice (vs spawn-per-utterance) — the docstring on backend/app/providers/piper_tts.py already names this.
   - Piper HTTP server variant if process-keep-alive isn't enough.
   - Verify the audio bridge to Meet / WebRTC actually forwards chunks as they arrive (suspect: buffers until end-of-utterance).
   - Tune chunk_bytes, native_sample_rate defaults if profiling shows mis-set values.
   - Whisper: model size vs latency trade-off; check whether faster-whisper is using GPU when available, CPU thread count, beam size.
   - Local LLM: context window trimming, prompt-cache reuse, lower-latency decode params.
4. **Documented target**: time-to-first-audio target on file (proposed: 300 ms p50 / 500 ms p95 for local stack); state whether the optimizations hit it, and if not, what would.

## In-UI optimization tips on every provider settings page (mandatory, not optional)

The provider settings window is where a user actually changes these knobs. After profiling, surface what was learned directly in that UI:

- A help section on each provider's settings card explaining what each option does and how it affects latency / quality / cost. Plain language, with rules of thumb (e.g. 'medium voices are ~2× slower than low voices but noticeably more natural; on CPU expect ~XX ms time-to-first-audio with default settings').
- Specifically for Local Piper: explain voice-tier trade-off (low / medium / high), native_sample_rate (which voices output 16k vs 22k), chunk_bytes, and call out the persistent-process optimization if it ships.
- Specifically for Local Whisper: explain model-size trade-off (tiny / base / small / medium), CPU vs GPU, beam size, real measured latencies on the test machine.
- Specifically for Local LLM(s): context window, decode settings, expected first-token latency.
- A small 'Measured on this machine' block per provider showing the most recent profile numbers (if cheap; otherwise just the static guidance).
- Each settings page should also link to the relevant section of any docs that this task produces.

Content style: short, useful, no marketing fluff. Imagine the reader is the operator at 11pm trying to make the bot snappier before tomorrow's demo.

## Out of scope

- The activity-log UI itself (Johnny-ckz.7).
- Cloud TTS / LLM provider tuning (separate ticket if interesting later).
- Aggregating latency analytics across many sessions (dashboard).
- Hyper-optimizations behind feature flags / experiments framework.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A written latency map of the local stack is on file with p50 / p95 numbers from ≥20 turns using real models seeded from /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json.
2. The dominant bottleneck is identified with evidence.
3. At least one concrete optimization is implemented and re-measured; before/after numbers are on file.
4. Each provider's settings page in the UI has a help / tips section explaining its options and their latency/quality trade-offs, including measured rules-of-thumb from this work.
5. The 'Measured on this machine' block (if shipped) reflects the latest profile numbers.
6. All UI additions (the in-settings help sections) are validated via chrome-devtools MCP per the AGENTS.md top rule, with screenshots in the PR.

## Testing approach — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

- Profile from the playground (Johnny-ckz.6) once it lands, OR a real Meet, using chrome-devtools MCP to capture browser-side timings via performance_start_trace / performance_stop_trace / list_network_requests.
- For every provider settings page that gets a new tips section, drive the UI in chrome-devtools MCP: navigate, snapshot, expand the tips section, screenshot, assert the rules-of-thumb match what was measured.
- Re-measure after each optimization and capture the delta in the PR.

## Related

- [[per-session-activity-timing-log-surfaced-in-chat-history-per-turn-pipeline-events-with-durations]] (Johnny-ckz.7) — sibling; produces the events this work uses as its measurement instrument.
- [[local-piper-follow-up-voice-catalog-fetcher-fails-on-hf-307-redirect-plus-model-dirs-must-move-to-host-bind-mounts]] (Johnny-ckz.5) — must be unblocked before Piper end-to-end profiling can happen.
- [[in-browser-voice-text-chat-with-the-bot-per-event-try-with-bot-button-plus-standalone-playground]] (Johnny-ckz.6) — natural profiling surface.
- [[run-the-two-bot-voice-interrupt-harness-end-to-end-against-real-models-fix-any-bugs-it-surfaces]] (Johnny-ckz.4) — uses the same real-models constraint and credentials JSON.
design: Profile before changing — measure where time actually goes (model load vs subprocess fork vs bridge buffering vs resampling). Per piper_tts.py docstring, the named upgrade path is a persistent piper process (or Piper HTTP server) fronted by an adapter that reuses the long-lived process; evaluate first. For Whisper, check whether faster-whisper is using the CPU thread count and beam size we think it is. Surface findings in the settings UI as a help section per provider, written for the 11pm-before-demo operator audience. Use Johnny-ckz.7's session_timings as the measurement instrument once it lands; until then, instrument ad-hoc.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Latency map with p50/p95 from ≥20 real-model turns on file, seeded from /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json. (2) Dominant bottleneck identified with evidence. (3) At least one optimization implemented and re-measured with before/after numbers. (4) Each provider's settings page in the UI has a help/tips section covering its options and their latency/quality trade-offs, including measured rules-of-thumb. (5) All settings-page UI additions validated via chrome-devtools MCP with screenshots in the PR.

title: Per-session activity / timing log surfaced in chat history (per-turn pipeline events with durations)
description:
## Why this exists

The session detail view today shows transcripts and bot utterances, but nothing about the pipeline that produced them. When a turn feels slow, or the wrong provider was used, or an interrupt arrived but didn't cut, there's no on-page way to see what actually happened. The user asked for a 'super useful' activity log inside the chat history — so an operator can land on a session and immediately see, per turn, the timing and the events.

This task is **the log itself** — capture the events, persist them, render them. Profiling + tuning + in-UI optimization tips live in a separate task (filed alongside this one).

## What to log (per user-turn → bot-reply round-trip)

- User speech start / end (from VAD)
- STT: first-partial latency, final-transcript latency, model / provider used
- Router / LLM: time-to-first-token, total generation time, model used, finish reason, token counts if cheap to get
- TTS: time-to-first-audio-byte, total synth time, voice / provider used, output bytes / duration
- End-to-end: user-speech-end → first-audio-out-to-user (the single number users actually feel)
- Interrupts: when user interrupted, when TTS was cut, latency delta (ties into Johnny-ckz.4)
- Provider switches mid-session (the active provider changed between turns)
- Errors / retries / fallbacks (which provider failed, what we fell back to)

## Persistence

A thin session_timings table is the minimum viable shape — keyed by (session_id, turn_id, event_type, started_at, duration_ms) with a small JSON payload for the per-event detail (e.g. {'model': 'gpt-4o', 'tokens': 312}). If a session-events stream already exists, extend that instead of adding a new table — the investigation under Johnny-ckz.7's sibling profiling task can confirm the cleanest fit; this implementation task should pick one and stick with it.

## UI

A collapsible 'activity' panel per turn in the session detail page (or a single timeline at the top — designer's call), in plain log form with badges per provider. Not a full Gantt chart. Goal: a user scanning a session can see in one glance which turn was slow and which step in that turn was the cost.

Render contract:
- Collapsed by default; expanded shows the per-event list with absolute and relative timings.
- Provider name is visible per row (so 'TTS: 1.4s — Local Piper' is immediately legible).
- Errors are visually distinguished (red badge or icon).
- Works on a session that has only some of the events (older sessions without the new logging just show what they have, no crashes).

## Out of scope

- Optimizing latency (covered by the sibling profiling task).
- Cross-session analytics / dashboards aggregating timing across many sessions.
- Exporting the log to CSV / JSON — additive later if needed.
- Live streaming the log into the UI mid-session — initial version can render after the turn ends; mid-turn streaming is a nice-to-have.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A new session that goes through a full user-turn → bot-reply round-trip produces session_timings rows (or session-events entries) for every applicable event type listed above.
2. The session detail page shows a per-turn activity panel reflecting those events with absolute and relative timings.
3. Provider name is shown per event so it's obvious which TTS / STT / LLM was used.
4. Interrupts (when present) are visible in the panel with their measured latency delta.
5. Sessions that pre-date this change still load with no crashes and no empty-panel error (they just show fewer events).
6. The DB migration is reversible.

## Testing approach — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

Per the AGENTS.md top rule:

- Drive a real session (in the playground from Johnny-ckz.6 if it has shipped, otherwise a real Meet) using the credentials in /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json so the log includes real STT/TTS/LLM events.
- Open the session detail page in chrome-devtools MCP and take a screenshot of the rendered activity panel — collapsed and expanded.
- take_snapshot the per-turn panel and assert (in the test transcript) that every required event type is present and timed.
- Drive an interrupt turn and confirm the interrupt row + its latency delta show up.
- Load an old session (pre-migration) and confirm the panel degrades gracefully.

Unit tests are necessary but not sufficient. The PR description must include the chrome-devtools-MCP screenshots above.

## Related

- [[run-the-two-bot-voice-interrupt-harness-end-to-end-against-real-models-fix-any-bugs-it-surfaces]] (Johnny-ckz.4) — the harness will produce real timing data this log can render.
- [[in-browser-voice-text-chat-with-the-bot-per-event-try-with-bot-button-plus-standalone-playground]] (Johnny-ckz.6) — natural first surface to land the panel on.
design: Thin session_timings table keyed by (session_id, turn_id, event_type, started_at, duration_ms) with a small JSON detail blob; OR extend the existing session-events stream if one is in place. Emit events from the same spots that already log to logger — wrap them in a thin emitter so the writes are cheap. UI: collapsible per-turn panel, log style, badge per provider, red badge for errors. Mid-turn streaming is a nice-to-have; initial version may render after turn-end.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Per-turn session_timings entries are persisted for every applicable event type (STT, LLM, TTS, end-to-end, interrupts, provider switches, errors). (2) Session detail page renders a collapsible per-turn activity panel with absolute + relative timings and visible provider names. (3) Interrupts appear with their latency delta. (4) Pre-migration sessions render with no crashes. (5) DB migration is reversible. (6) Validation includes chrome-devtools-MCP screenshots of collapsed + expanded panel and an interrupt-turn capture, using real models seeded from /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json.

title: ElevenLabs TTS: handle 'exceeds quota' 401 gracefully in the response loop
description:
When ElevenLabs returns 401 with 'exceeds your quota of N, M credits required', the pipeline's _stream_answer_into_tts raises TTSError. The _respond_loop catches it via the broad 'except Exception' guard and logs — the session continues, transcription keeps working — but the user gets silence with no surface indication that TTS broke.

Found during the Johnny-ckz.4 real-provider harness work: the configured ElevenLabs key in /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json had ~2 credits remaining and every harness invocation tripped this.

What we should do:
- Emit a structured event when TTS fails (e.g. AgentTTSFailed with provider name + reason).
- Surface in the session UI so the user can see 'TTS provider out of credits' rather than 'bot just stopped speaking'.
- Probably: add a circuit breaker so we don't keep hammering a broken provider for the whole session.

Reproduction: configure ElevenLabs with an out-of-credits key, ask the bot to speak. Bot will fail silently.

Found by: Johnny-ckz.4 real-provider harness work.

title: Interrupt harness real-mode: clarification assertion shape doesn't match real behavior
description:
The Johnny-ckz.4 real-provider harness for clarification_redirects_long_answer expects TWO AgentSpoke events: the cut original answer + the follow-up. In real mode, the cut original answer publishes NO AgentSpoke because _answer_and_speak's 'if not text or not collected: return False' fires when the interrupt cuts in before any sentence has flushed to TTS. Only the follow-up answer (real bot saying 'Regarding the launch date, we are currently targeting...') emits AgentSpoke.

Observed (from artifacts/2026-06-06T11-40-53Z-interrupt/report.json):
- fast_barge_in_count=1 (interrupt fired correctly).
- transcripts_persisted=['Give me a summary...', 'Wait. What about the launch date?'] (real STT works).
- utterances_persisted=[{'output_text': 'Regarding the launch date, we are currently targeting...'}] (FOLLOW-UP answer was generated and persisted).
- agent_spoke_durations_ms=[17658] (one event, the follow-up).
- played_frame_count=208 — more audio than the follow-up alone (~9s of CUT answer also played).

Two possible fixes:
- Update real-mode assertions: 'success' is fast_barge_in_count>0 AND a follow-up utterance whose text mentions the new question keyword ('launch').
- Or: change _answer_and_speak to emit AgentSpoke even for cut answers with at least N played frames so the cut path stays observable.

Probably both — the second is the real fix (observability) and the first makes the assertion sensible.

Reproduction: uv run python -m johnny.e2e.interrupt --real --providers-file /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json --fallback-tts-openai --only clarification_redirects_long_answer

title: Interrupt harness real-mode: stop scenario flakes when LLM round-trip is slow
description:
The Johnny-ckz.4 real-provider harness for stop_interrupts_long_answer is flaky: 1-in-3 runs the bot fails to produce ANY AgentSpoke because the user starts saying 'stop please' before the answer LLM has streamed enough text to produce a first TTS frame. When this happens, the assertion 'first_agent_spoke_truncated' fails with 'no AgentSpoke published'.

Root cause: The scenario waits 8 s after the 'tell me about yourself' prompt before the 'stop please' interrupt. On slow LLM days (OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini occasionally takes 2.5-3 s to first token), the bot has not yet produced any audio when the interrupt fires.

Options:
- Bump REAL_MODE_EXTRA_SILENCE_MS to 10000+ (longer wait, slower test).
- Or: switch the bot to a faster LLM for the harness (e.g. gpt-4o-mini).
- Or: change the assertion to accept 'fast_barge_in_count > 0 AND no AgentSpoke' as a valid pass for the stop scenario.

Reproduction: uv run python -m johnny.e2e.interrupt --real --providers-file /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json --fallback-tts-openai --only stop_interrupts_long_answer

title: LLM providers: fetch model list dynamically from each provider's API instead of hardcoding
description:
Currently the model picker for LLM providers shows only a hardcoded short list (e.g. OpenAI shows 'GPT-4.1' and a couple more, not the full lineup). Users can't pick newer / less-common models without editing config.

Wanted: every LLM provider's model dropdown fetches the actual available models live from the provider's API, so the list stays current as providers ship new models.

Coverage needed (at minimum):
- OpenAI — GET /v1/models with the configured API key
- Anthropic — GET /v1/models
- Google (Gemini) — equivalent list endpoint
- Ollama — GET /api/tags against the configured base URL (this is local, so the list IS literally whatever models the user has pulled)
- Any other LLM provider already registered in backend/app/providers

Behavior:
- Fetch on demand when the user opens the provider config (or on a refresh button); cache briefly so we don't hammer the API.
- If credentials are missing/invalid, surface a clear 'enter API key to load models' message instead of falling back to the stale hardcoded list.
- Ollama in particular should ALWAYS fetch fresh — it reflects what's on disk and there is no static list to fall back to.

Out of scope: STT and TTS providers (those have separate model/voice taxonomies; see the Piper UX issue for the local-TTS analogue).
acceptance_criteria: Opening an LLM provider's config in the UI shows a model dropdown populated from the provider's live /models endpoint (or /api/tags for Ollama). New models the provider ships are visible without code changes. With no credentials, the UI shows a clear prompt to enter the key rather than a stale fallback list.

title: ElevenLabs e2e plan uses library voice incompatible with free tier
description:
