title: Bot carries the whole meeting's context (not a 6-turn rolling window) when routing and answering
description:
## Why this exists

Today the voice pipeline at \`backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/pipeline.py\` keeps the last **6** transcripts in memory and nothing else (\`DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_WINDOW_SIZE = 6\`, line 69; rolling delete at line 850-851; window assembly at line 853-874). Older parts of the meeting fall out of the prompt entirely.

The static \`config.context\` field on a \`MeetingConfig\` exists (line 130, used at lines 740 and 789) but only carries pre-meeting context the user typed in by hand. Nothing accumulates *during* the meeting.

Effect: ten minutes into a meeting, the bot has forgotten the first nine minutes. Ask "what did we decide about the staging deploy earlier?" and it has no idea. That defeats most of the value of a long-form meeting bot.

## What "whole context" means here

Three layers, all needed:

1. **Pre-meeting context** — already there (\`config.context\`), but should also pull from the Google Calendar event's description / attachments / linked docs if available.
2. **In-meeting accumulation** — every finalised transcript from this session, in order, available to both router and answer LLMs, not capped at 6.
3. **Cross-session continuity (optional, smaller scope)** — if the same calendar event recurs (same recurring_event_id), surface the most recent prior session's summary as additional context. File a follow-up bead if too much; can be deferred.

## What to build

### Storage is already there

\`transcript_chunks\` (\`backend/app/db/models.py\` and the persistence layer in \`app/services/transcripts.py\`) already persists every finalised STT chunk per session — that's the source of truth. The pipeline just doesn't read from it; it works from its in-memory window.

### Pipeline changes

- Drop the \`DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_WINDOW_SIZE = 6\` cap as the default. Replace with an unbounded list per session, capped by **token budget** instead of turn count.
- Make \`_build_input_window\` (line 853) emit the **full** session transcript when within budget, otherwise apply a rolling summarisation step: oldest N transcripts get collapsed into a short summary line ("Earlier: …"), recent transcripts kept verbatim.
- Token budget knobs configurable per provider (different LLMs have different windows). Default safe: 75 % of the provider's max context, reserving the rest for the answer.
- Summarisation can be a lightweight call to the same router/answer LLM with a "summarise the following meeting transcript in <= N sentences" prompt; cache the summary against the session so it's not recomputed every turn.

### Crash / resume

- On worker (re)start mid-session — e.g. container respawn — rehydrate \`_transcript_history\` from \`transcript_chunks WHERE session_id = ?\` so the bot doesn't reset to zero context.

### Calendar context

- Read the calendar event's \`description\` (already fetched per \`app/services/calendar_polling.py\`) and append it to the pipeline's system prompt as additional context, distinct from the user-typed \`config.context\` so both are visible to the LLM and persisted separately for audit.
- If the event has attached Google Docs / Sheets URLs in the description, **out of scope** for this bead — list as a follow-up.

### Persistence / audit

- The system prompt the LLM sees per turn (with full or summarised context) should be persisted on \`agent_decisions\` (or alongside it) so audits can reproduce why the bot answered the way it did. Today the snapshot in \`_build_input_window\` (line 858-873) captures \`transcript_window\` and \`instructions\` / \`context\` — extend with the summarised-history snapshot when summarisation kicks in.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In a 30+ minute session, asking the bot a question about something said in the first 5 minutes produces an answer that references that earlier context (not a "I don't know").
- [ ] No 6-turn cap on transcript history — capped by token budget instead.
- [ ] When over the token budget, oldest transcripts are summarised; the summary is cached per session and reused across turns.
- [ ] Pre-meeting context = \`config.context\` + calendar event description, both visible in the system prompt and persisted for audit.
- [ ] On worker container restart mid-session, the next turn picks up the full prior transcript from \`transcript_chunks\` (no context reset).
- [ ] The \`_build_input_window\` snapshot stored per decision includes whatever the LLM actually saw (full or summarised) so audits are reproducible.
- [ ] Token-budget knob is configurable per LLM provider; defaults to 75 % of the provider's max context.
- [ ] Tests cover: full session under budget, session over budget triggering summarisation, mid-session restart rehydration, calendar description merged into context.
- [ ] Quality gates pass: \`uv run pytest\`, \`uv run ruff check\`, \`uv run mypy\`, \`pnpm typecheck\`, \`pnpm lint\`.

## Out of scope

- Cross-session continuity for recurring events (file a follow-up under \`Johnny-ckz\` if you want it).
- Reading attached Google Docs / Sheets URLs from the event description (separate bead).
- Vector-search retrieval over transcripts (already a separate workstream — \`agent_decisions\` and \`transcript_chunks\` have embeddings via \`compute_pending_embeddings\`; this bead is about *in-session* context, not retrieval).
- Per-speaker memory / who-said-what diarisation upgrades.

## Notes

The current 6-turn cap was a scaffolding default, not a designed limit — \`config.transcript_window_size\` is already configurable. This bead is the natural next step: lift the cap, switch to token-budgeted, and persist what the LLM actually saw.

## Related

- \`Johnny-ckz\` — parent epic (join-stuck fix + e2e harness). This bead reinforces the value the harness needs to prove.
- \`Johnny-ckz.2\` — Autonomous mode. Autonomous benefits most from full context since it has no per-utterance approval gate.
- \`Johnny-pdf\` — master e2e validation. When this lands, \`Johnny-pdf\` Phase 5/6/7 scripts should include a question that requires context from earlier in the same session, otherwise the test never exercises this.
- \`Johnny-kgc.33\` — US-033: Transcript and audit persistence. The data layer this bead reads from.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline no longer caps transcript history at 6 turns; carries the full session transcript within a configurable token budget, summarising older content when over budget; merges calendar event description into pre-meeting context; rehydrates from transcript_chunks on worker restart; persists whatever the LLM actually saw per decision; tests cover under-budget, over-budget, restart, calendar merge; quality gates pass.
notes: Spawned 2026-06-06 from user request — explicitly wants the bot to hold the whole meeting's context. Lives under Johnny-ckz alongside Johnny-ckz.2 (Autonomous mode), which benefits most from real context.

title: Add 'Autonomous' mode: bot speaks freely per profile instructions, no whitelist, no approval gate
description:
## Why this exists

Today \`BotMode\` (\`backend/app/db/models.py:51-55\`) ships four values:

1. \`listen_only\` — STT only, bot never speaks.
2. \`suggest_only\` — pipeline runs, decisions logged, bot stays silent.
3. \`approval_required\` — pipeline proposes a reply, user must Approve/Reject in the UI before it speaks.
4. \`limited_auto_speak\` — bot speaks, but only verbatim from the profile template's \`allowed_replies\` whitelist (currently required for this mode at \`app/api/templates.py:52\` and \`app/api/meeting_configs.py:138\`).

There's no mode for "let Johnny act on its own, guided only by the profile template's instructions and context". The user wants exactly that: free-form generation, no approval round-trip, no allowed-reply whitelist — the bot self-governs against the profile instructions.

This is the natural fifth mode that the existing scaffolding was clearly designed to support but never delivered.

## What to build

### New enum value

- Add \`AUTONOMOUS = "autonomous"\` to \`BotMode\` in \`backend/app/db/models.py\`. Naming options considered: \`AUTO_SPEAK\` (parallel with \`LIMITED_AUTO_SPEAK\`), \`FREE_SPEAK\`, \`AUTONOMOUS\`, \`UNRESTRICTED\`. Recommendation: \`AUTONOMOUS\` — communicates the *intent* (operates on its own per instructions) rather than the surface behaviour. UI label: "Autonomous".
- Alembic migration in \`backend/alembic/versions/\` extending the PG enum type. Pattern to follow: \`0003_decision_outcome_suggested.py\` already adds a value to an enum and is the template to copy.

### Validation rules

- \`allowed_replies\` requirement at \`app/api/templates.py:52\` and \`app/api/meeting_configs.py:138\` is currently \`if mode is BotMode.LIMITED_AUTO_SPEAK\` — leave it as-is. For \`AUTONOMOUS\`, \`allowed_replies\` must be **empty or ignored** (the whole point is no whitelist).
- Profile template instructions and context **must be non-empty** for \`AUTONOMOUS\` — they are the only governance. Add a parallel validation that rejects an autonomous-mode template/meeting_config with blank instructions.

### Pipeline behaviour

- Reuse the existing router → answer → TTS path (same as approval/limited_auto_speak).
- Skip the approval gate entirely (no \`agent_decisions.status = pending\`, no browser push, no countdown).
- No whitelist match against \`allowed_replies\` — the answer LLM's free-form output goes straight to TTS.
- Decisions are still persisted to \`agent_decisions\` with \`outcome = spoken\` (or \`suppressed\` if the router declines, e.g. low confidence / non-question) so the audit trail stays intact.
- Honour the same per-session rate limit knobs the limited mode uses (cost + talking-over-others control), but default the cap a bit lower for autonomous since each utterance is free-form and longer. Make the cap overrideable per meeting_config.

### Frontend

- Add the new mode to \`frontend/src/lib/templates.ts\` — both the union type (line 10-13), the iteration list (16-19), and the human label map (23-26). Suggested label: \`'Autonomous'\`.
- Add the mode to \`frontend/src/lib/sessionDetail.ts\` (line 24-26 area) so the session detail view renders it.
- Surface a small "no approval, no whitelist — driven by profile instructions" note in the mode picker so a user picking Autonomous knows what's at stake.
- The template form should make \`instructions\` required when the mode is \`autonomous\` (mirror the backend validation).

### API

- Schemas at \`app/api/sessions.py:146\`, \`app/api/meeting_configs.py:65,89,128\`, \`app/api/templates.py:39,72\` already type as \`BotMode\` — they will accept the new value automatically once the enum lands, but verify with a unit test per endpoint.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] \`BotMode.AUTONOMOUS\` exists and is persisted via meeting_configs and templates.
- [ ] Alembic migration adds the value to the PG enum and \`alembic upgrade head\` is clean against a populated database.
- [ ] Autonomous-mode template / meeting_config rejects blank \`instructions\` with a clear validation error.
- [ ] Autonomous-mode template / meeting_config does **not** require \`allowed_replies\`.
- [ ] In an autonomous session, the router proposes a reply, the answer LLM produces free-form output, TTS speaks it within ~4s of the question — no approval round-trip.
- [ ] Decisions still land in \`agent_decisions\` with \`outcome=spoken\` (or \`suppressed\` for declined cases); \`agent_utterances\` rows persist as in other speaking modes.
- [ ] Per-session rate limit applies; over-cap requests log a \`suppressed\` decision with \`reason=rate_limited\`.
- [ ] Frontend renders 'Autonomous' as a fifth option in the mode picker and on the session detail view.
- [ ] Quality gates pass: \`uv run pytest\`, \`uv run ruff check\`, \`uv run mypy\`, \`pnpm typecheck\`, \`pnpm lint\`.

## Out of scope

- Per-template instruction templates / prompt library.
- Anti-jailbreak guardrails against malicious instructions — the bead assumes the user owns their template.
- Voice-tone / persona tuning (uses whatever the configured TTS provider produces).
- A "kill switch" UI button to immediately silence an autonomous bot mid-meeting — file a follow-up bead under \`Johnny-ckz\` if you want it; it's a different shape of work.

## Notes

This belongs under \`Johnny-ckz\` because the lived-journey validation in \`Johnny-pdf\` (Phases 4-7 explicitly enumerate all four modes) needs a fifth phase or an extension of Phase 7 to cover Autonomous. When that lands, update \`Johnny-pdf\` acceptance to include the new mode.

## Related

- \`Johnny-ckz\` — parent epic (join-stuck fix + e2e harness).
- \`Johnny-pdf\` — master e2e validation, currently enumerates Phases 4-7 across the four existing modes; will need extending.
- \`Johnny-kgc.26\` — US-026: Listen-only and Suggest-only modes (closed; precedent for adding modes).
- \`Johnny-kgc.27\` — US-027: Approval-required mode (closed; reference for pipeline behaviour without approval gate).
- \`Johnny-kgc.28\` — US-028: Limited auto-speak (closed; nearest neighbour — same speak path, different governance).
acceptance_criteria: BotMode.AUTONOMOUS lands with migration; validation enforces non-empty instructions and ignores allowed_replies; pipeline speaks free-form output without an approval gate; decisions and utterances persist as in other speaking modes; per-session rate limit honoured; frontend exposes 'Autonomous' as the fifth mode option and on session detail; quality gates pass.
notes: Spawned 2026-06-06 from user request — explicitly wants a mode that lets the bot act on instructions alone with free speech and no per-utterance confirmation. Lives under Johnny-ckz so the e2e harness picks it up.

title: openai-realtime STT adapter targets deprecated Realtime Beta API
description: The E2E harness (Johnny-upg) flagged that POST /providers/{id}/test against an openai-realtime row fails with: "The Realtime Beta API is no longer supported. Please use /v1/realtime for the GA API." The adapter at backend/app/providers/openai_realtime_stt.py still sends `OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1` and connects to the beta endpoint. Update it to the GA endpoint /v1/realtime and re-run `uv run python -m tests.e2e.providers_ui` until stt-openai-realtime PASSes.

title: Surface undecryptable Google account tokens with a clear reconnect path
description:
When a stored Google account row's refresh token cannot be decrypted (typically because FERNET_KEY was rotated since the OAuth flow, or postgres data outlived the host .env), the Calendar page surfaces the raw backend error 'google api client error: failed to decrypt refresh token for account N' and offers no recovery path. The user is stuck at a dead end even though Settings → Disconnect can already clean the row up.

## Repro

1. Connect a Google account via /settings (account row stored, refresh token encrypted with key K1).
2. Regenerate FERNET_KEY (e.g. user re-ran the setup guide §3) and restart the stack — postgres volume persists.
3. Open /calendar — Refresh attempt against /calendar/events?account_id=N raises GoogleApiClientError → 502 → top-of-page red error.

## Root cause

backend/app/services/google_client.py:96-102 — _decrypt_refresh_token() raises GoogleApiClientError with the literal account id. backend/app/api/calendar.py:117-121 maps it to HTTP 502 with the bare exception string. The frontend (frontend/src/routes/calendar/+page.svelte:104-111) just renders error.message.

## Fix (proposed scope)

Backend:
- Introduce a distinct error class (e.g. TokenUndecryptableError) or carry a structured code on the existing GoogleApiClientError so callers can tell 'tokens unreadable, needs reauth' apart from transport / quota / scope errors.
- Map this code to a dedicated HTTP status (409 Conflict with detail {code: 'account_needs_reauth', account_id, email}) on /calendar/events and any other endpoint that calls GoogleApiClient (calendar polling worker should mark the row dirty and skip rather than throwing).
- Add a 'token_health' field to the AccountRead response: 'ok' | 'needs_reauth'. Computed cheaply at list time by attempting a no-op decrypt of refresh_token_encrypted (do not fetch userinfo).

Frontend:
- Settings: badge accounts whose token_health=='needs_reauth' as 'Token unreadable — reconnect'. Reuse the existing Add-account OAuth flow with the same role / default-user tags; on success, the row is replaced in place because upsert is keyed by email (google_client.py:265).
- Calendar: when the selected account.token_health=='needs_reauth', skip the /calendar/events call entirely and render an empty state with a deep link to /settings#account-N and a 'Reconnect this account' inline action that initiates OAuth right there.

Docs:
- docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md §3 — move the 'if you lose the key, all encrypted rows must be deleted' warning to a callout at the top of the section. Add a copy-paste recovery snippet that disconnects all accounts via the API (which is already key-loss-safe per auth.py:474-479) instead of dropping postgres data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New typed error path distinguishes 'undecryptable token' from other GoogleApiClient failures
- [ ] /auth/google/accounts response includes token_health for every row, computed without a Google round-trip
- [ ] GET /calendar/events returns 409 with {code: 'account_needs_reauth'} (not 502) when the selected account's token cannot be decrypted
- [ ] Settings page shows a 'Reconnect' affordance for accounts in needs_reauth state; clicking it runs OAuth and the row is replaced after callback
- [ ] Calendar page detects needs_reauth before fetching and renders a non-error empty state with a Settings deep link
- [ ] Recovery callout added at the top of docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md §3 with the disconnect-via-Settings instruction
- [ ] Backend tests cover: undecryptable refresh token → typed error, /calendar/events 409 response, /auth/google/accounts token_health field
- [ ] Frontend tests cover: Settings reconnect button visibility, Calendar empty-state branch
- [ ] chrome-devtools screenshot of Calendar empty state and Settings reconnect badge attached

## Non-goals

- In-place key rotation (decrypt with old key, re-encrypt with new key) — out of scope; user is told to reconnect instead
- Multi-key support / key versioning on encrypted columns
- Detecting and auto-clearing meeting_configs whose identity_account is broken — Disconnect already cascades with force=true; document that path instead

## Notes

Current immediate workaround: /settings → Disconnect on the broken account (already handles undecryptable tokens — auth.py:474-479) → re-add via 'Add account'.

title: Refactor provider settings UI: per-provider structured forms instead of generic Credentials/Options textareas
description:
The current provider settings UI (US-018, Johnny-kgc.18) exposes only two generic textareas per provider — "Credentials" and "Options" — both accepting raw key=value lines. This is opaque: users must already know the exact env-var-style keys each provider expects (e.g. DEEPGRAM_API_KEY vs api_key vs token; OLLAMA base_url vs OPENAI_API_BASE; ElevenLabs voice_id vs voice). It causes silent typos, hides which fields are required, and makes provider switching painful.

This task replaces the two-textarea design with structured, row-based forms — one form schema per concrete provider adapter. Each provider type renders its own clearly labeled fields with inline guidance (placeholders, descriptions, links to where to get the value), required/optional markers, validation, and field grouping (auth vs config vs model selection).

The backend provider registry (US-011) already knows each provider's required/optional fields; this task surfaces that schema to the frontend rather than dumping a free-text textarea on the user.

## Scope

### Backend
- Extend the provider adapter base classes (STTProvider, LLMProvider, TTSProvider) with a class-level `field_schema()` classmethod that returns a list of field definitions: { name, label, type (text/password/url/number/select), required, placeholder, help_text, default, options? (for select), group? }
- Each concrete adapter (DeepgramSTT, OpenAIRealtimeSTT, FasterWhisperSTT, OpenAI LLM, Anthropic LLM, Gemini LLM, OpenAICompatibleLLM, ElevenLabsTTS, OpenAITTS, PiperTTS) declares its own field_schema with the right fields, labels, and help text
- New endpoint GET /providers/schemas returns all registered provider schemas grouped by kind so the frontend can render dynamic forms
- Persist values into the existing provider_credentials table — split fields into "credentials" (encrypted) and "config" (plain) buckets server-side based on the schema's type/sensitivity
- Validation: backend validates incoming payloads against the schema (required, type) before save; returns 422 with field-level errors
- Migration is not required if the underlying storage already uses JSONB; this is a UI/schema-presentation refactor, not a data-model rewrite

### Frontend
- New `/providers` UI replaces the two textareas with a per-provider form generated from the schema fetched from /providers/schemas
- Each provider card shows: provider name, kind badge, set of structured rows (label + input + help text + required marker), Test button, Save button, Delete button
- Field types render appropriately: password fields are masked, select fields use a dropdown, URL fields show a leading protocol hint, etc.
- Inline help text links to the provider's signup/docs page when relevant ("Get a key →")
- Validation surfaces both client-side (required, type) and server-side (422 field errors)
- The previous free-text textareas are removed entirely — no fallback raw mode

## Why this matters now
- The interactive wizard (Johnny-61y) will reuse the same schema source of truth, so a structured field_schema benefits both UI and CLI
- The setup guide (Johnny-mxx) can reference exact field names from the schema instead of pseudo-keys
acceptance_criteria: Backend: each provider adapter declares field_schema(); GET /providers/schemas returns schemas grouped by kind; payload validation returns field-level 422 errors. Frontend: /providers page renders a structured form per provider with labeled rows, help text, password masking, select dropdowns, URL hints, and required markers — no generic key=value textareas remain. Test button still works against the structured form. Setup wizard (Johnny-61y) consumes the same field_schema source of truth. All quality gates pass: uv run pytest, uv run ruff check, uv run mypy, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint. Visual verification via chrome-devtools MCP with screenshots of at least one cloud and one local provider form.

title: Build interactive CLI setup wizard for Johnny
description:
Build a Python CLI wizard that walks the user through Johnny's full local setup interactively. The wizard should be the friendlier alternative to docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md — instead of copy-pasting commands, the user answers prompts and the wizard does the work.

The wizard should:

- Run via 'uv run python -m johnny.wizard' or a script entrypoint like 'johnny setup'
- Use a rich TUI library (questionary, rich, or textual — pick one and stick to it)
- Detect prerequisites (Docker, uv, pnpm, available disk space, GPU presence) and report what is missing with direct install links
- Guide Google OAuth setup: open the Google Cloud Console URL in the default browser, prompt for client ID / client secret, write to .env
- For each provider kind (STT, LLM, TTS), ask: cloud or local?
  - If cloud: list options (Deepgram, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, ElevenLabs) with provider sign-up URLs and 'best for' notes; prompt for API key; write to .env and call backend API to register
  - If local: list recommended models per kind with size on disk and quality notes; let user pick; download automatically via huggingface-hub, ollama pull, or direct URL; place in correct volume path; call backend API to register
- Recommend best defaults per kind for local-first (e.g., faster-whisper small for STT, Llama 3.1 8B via Ollama for LLM, Piper en_US-amy-medium for TTS)
- Generate FERNET_KEY automatically and write to .env (only if missing)
- After provider setup, run the same smoke test the Providers UI offers ('Test' button) for each registered provider and report pass/fail
- Offer to start the Docker Compose stack at the end and open the UI
- Be re-runnable safely: detect already-completed steps and offer to skip or reconfigure
- Provide a '--non-interactive' mode that reads answers from a YAML file for CI / scripted setups

The wizard is a complement to docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md (Johnny-mxx), not a replacement — the docs should reference it as the recommended path.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard runs via a single 'uv run python -m johnny.wizard' command; detects missing prerequisites with install links; configures Google OAuth, all three provider kinds (cloud and local), and FERNET_KEY end-to-end; downloads local models automatically into the correct Docker volumes; runs provider smoke tests and reports pass/fail; safely re-runnable; supports --non-interactive YAML mode

title: Write local-first setup guide with copy-paste commands and direct download links
description:
Create a step-by-step setup guide for running Johnny entirely locally. The guide must be copy-paste ready, super simple, and include direct download links for every model and dependency.

The guide should cover:
- Prerequisites (Docker, uv, pnpm, Python version, disk space requirements)
- Cloning the repo and running 'docker compose up'
- Creating the dedicated johnny-bot Google account and registering OAuth desktop client (direct links to Google Cloud Console pages)
- Filling .env with all required variables (FERNET_KEY generation command, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)
- Local STT setup: which faster-whisper model size to pick (recommendation + size on disk), exact HuggingFace URL, where to place the file, config entry
- Local LLM setup: recommended model (e.g., Qwen2.5 7B or Llama 3.1 8B), Ollama vs vLLM choice, exact 'ollama pull' command or vLLM Docker command, base_url to put in provider config
- Local TTS setup: recommended Piper voice (e.g., en_US-amy-medium), direct download URL for .onnx and .json files, where to place them, config entry
- Silero VAD: confirm it ships in the image or list the download command
- LiveKit local dev server: docker run command for local LiveKit if needed
- Provider configuration via UI: screenshots or step-by-step of adding STT/LLM/TTS providers with the exact field values matching the downloaded models
- First-run smoke test: connect Google account, mark a test meeting, verify bot joins
- Troubleshooting section: PulseAudio not found, model file missing, OAuth redirect failure, container OOM

The output should be a single markdown file at docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md. Every command must be copy-pasteable. Every download must be a direct link. Assume the reader knows Docker basics but nothing about the AI stack.
acceptance_criteria: docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md exists and covers all sections above; every model has a direct download link; every command block is copy-pasteable; a fresh machine following the guide can run a Listen-only test session end-to-end without consulting other docs

title: US-033: Transcript and audit persistence
description:
As a user, I want full audit data persisted so that I can review what was said, what Johnny decided, and what Johnny spoke.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] transcript_chunks stores finalized chunks with session_id, start_offset, end_offset, speaker, text, embedding (pgvector)
- [ ] agent_decisions stores every router invocation with input window, raw output, and outcome
- [ ] agent_utterances stores every spoken reply with mode, prompt, output text, and audio duration
- [ ] All three tables are indexed by session_id and timestamp for fast retrieval
- [ ] A nightly job (Celery beat) computes and stores embeddings for transcripts that lack them

- [ ] uv run ruff check passes
- [ ] uv run mypy passes
- [ ] pnpm typecheck passes
- [ ] pnpm lint passes

title: US-032: Live transcript and approval UI
description:
As a user, I want a live view of an active session with transcript, decisions, and approval controls so that I can supervise Johnny in real time.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Session view shows three panes: rolling transcript, decision feed, pending approvals
- [ ] Transcript pane shows speaker labels when available, partial vs finalized styling, and auto-scrolls
- [ ] Decision feed shows each router decision with reason, confidence, and outcome (spoken / suppressed / pending)
- [ ] Pending approvals pane shows the suggested reply with approve/reject buttons and a countdown to auto-reject
- [ ] "End session" button appears at the top and triggers stop_session

title: US-031: WebSocket for live updates
description:
As a user, I want the UI to receive live events from active sessions so that I see transcripts, decisions, and approval prompts in real time.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Backend exposes WS /ws/sessions/{session_id} that streams events from a Redis pub/sub channel
- [ ] Frontend subscribes when viewing a session and renders events in a virtualized list
- [ ] Event types: transcript_partial, transcript_final, router_decision, approval_pending, agent_spoke, session_status_change
- [ ] Reconnect logic recovers gracefully without duplicating rendered events
- [ ] A separate WS /ws/global carries notifications about session lifecycle for the calendar view

title: US-030: Per-session container spawning
description:
As a developer, I want each meet session to run in its own isolated container so that one bad meeting cannot affect others.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] start_session task uses Docker SDK to launch a meet-worker container with env vars (session_id, meet_link, account_id, provider_config, instructions)
- [ ] Container is named meet-worker-session-<id> and labeled for easy filtering
- [ ] On container exit, logs are tail-copied to bot_sessions.logs and the row status updated
- [ ] Crashed containers are not auto-restarted; the session is marked failed with the exit reason
- [ ] A cleanup task prunes stopped containers older than 24 hours
- [ ] uv run pytest passes
- [ ] uv run ruff check passes
- [ ] uv run mypy passes
- [ ] pnpm typecheck passes
- [ ] pnpm lint passes

title: US-029: Bot session scheduler
description:
As a developer, I want a background scheduler that spawns and tears down bot sessions at the right time so that Johnny joins promptly and exits cleanly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Celery (or Dramatiq) beat checks every minute for meeting_configs whose event starts within the next 2 minutes and has no active bot_session
- [ ] For each due meeting, scheduler enqueues a start_session task that spawns the meet-worker container
- [ ] A stop_session task is scheduled for event.end_time + 60s and gracefully terminates the worker
- [ ] Manual "Join now" and "Leave now" buttons in the UI invoke the same tasks
- [ ] Scheduler state (active sessions, scheduled jobs) is visible in the UI status panel
- [ ] uv run pytest passes
- [ ] uv run ruff check passes
- [ ] uv run mypy passes
- [ ] pnpm typecheck passes
- [ ] pnpm lint passes

title: US-028: Limited auto-speak mode
description:
As a user, I want auto-speak mode to be constrained to my pre-approved phrase list so that Johnny can respond automatically without saying anything risky.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] When mode is "Limited auto-speak", the answer LLM is invoked with a tool/structured-output schema that forces selection from allowed_replies
- [ ] If no allowed reply fits, the bot stays silent and logs the skipped decision
- [ ] Spoken utterance must be a verbatim match for an allowed reply (no paraphrasing)
- [ ] Spoken count per meeting is rate-limited (configurable, default max 3 per 5 minutes)
- [ ] Each utterance is persisted with the matched allowed_reply_id for auditing
- [ ] uv run pytest passes
- [ ] uv run ruff check passes
- [ ] uv run mypy passes
- [ ] pnpm typecheck passes
- [ ] pnpm lint passes

title: US-027: Approval-required mode with browser push
description:
As a user, I want approval-required mode to push notifications to my browser so that I can approve replies without keeping the UI focused.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Service worker registered in SvelteKit requests notification permission once per session

title: Johnny — Google Meet AI Meeting Bot
description:
Johnny is a single-user AI assistant that joins Google Meet meetings on the user's behalf and can listen, transcribe, suggest replies, ask for approval, or speak autonomously within configured constraints.

Runs as a daemon stack (Docker Compose) with a SvelteKit web UI for calendar browsing, per-meeting configuration, and real-time approval/transcript visibility.

Built around three swappable layers:
1. Meeting connector — Playwright+Chromium driving a real Google Meet session
2. Voice-agent pipeline — Pipecat with LiveKit transport adapter
3. Provider-agnostic STT/LLM/TTS adapters — cloud and local from day one

All meeting data (transcripts, router decisions, agent utterances) persisted to PostgreSQL with pgvector for transcript search.

## Goals
- Mark calendar events for Johnny to attend, with per-meeting context and behavior mode
- Four bot modes: listen-only, suggest-only, approval-required, limited auto-speak
- Provider adapters from day one (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, faster-whisper, vLLM/Ollama, Piper)
- Local Docker Compose with PostgreSQL, Redis, FastAPI, SvelteKit, isolated meet-worker containers per active meeting
- Join as dedicated bot Google account or user's own account, configurable per meeting
- Persist full meeting audit log for post-meeting review

title: faster-whisper: auto-detect GPU + auto-tune compute_type and CPU threads
description:
## Why
The Whisper in-UI tip on the provider settings card promises 'On NVIDIA hardware CUDA shrinks transcription by 4-8x; on CPU-only boxes it harmlessly falls back. Pair with compute_type=float16 on GPU, int8 on CPU.' Right now the device field defaults to cpu and the operator has to manually pick the right combo. Auto-detect would give us the gain by default.

## What
On adapter init:
- if device='auto' (or default): probe for CUDA availability; if present, switch to cuda + float16; otherwise cpu + int8.
- consider OMP_NUM_THREADS / cpu_threads tuning on CPU (faster-whisper supports cpu_threads kwarg).
- log the picked combo at INFO so an operator can see what auto resolved to.

## Acceptance
1. New providers default to 'auto' and resolve to cuda+float16 on GPU hosts, cpu+int8 on CPU-only.
2. Existing rows with device='cpu' keep their behaviour (no implicit upgrade).
3. Tests cover both branches with a mock detector.
4. Whisper UI tip on /providers is updated to mention the auto behaviour.

## Refs
- backend/app/providers/faster_whisper_stt.py — adapter; fields already include 'auto'.
- Johnny-ckz.8 — parent; this is one of the named optimisation candidates.
- docs/LATENCY.md — current numbers.

title: Live model-catalog fetch for OpenAI / Anthropic / Ollama in /providers modal
description:
Deferred from Johnny-fe.10 (single-modal CRUD redesign).

The /providers modal currently shows a static `FieldType.SELECT` of known models for OpenAI, Anthropic, etc. Operators have to know which models exist; if Anthropic ships a new claude-haiku-4-5 they have to wait for a code update.

The bead description for Johnny-fe.10 included this in the original scope but it was deferred to keep the iteration shippable. Implementing this means:

1. Per-provider `list_models()` backend method on `LLMProvider` (and probably TTS too — OpenAI TTS has a voice catalog API). Optional return — providers without a live catalog continue to use the static SELECT options.
2. `POST /providers/preview/list_models` endpoint that takes `(kind, provider_name, values)` (the same payload shape as the other preview endpoints), instantiates a transient provider, calls list_models, and returns the catalog.
3. Frontend: `previewListModels` client + a Combobox-style field in the modal that fetches on focus + provides a refresh button. Falls back to the static SELECT when list_models is not implemented.
4. Cache the catalog per-(provider_name, api_key-hash) for some TTL (5 min?) so each character typed doesn't fire a network round-trip.

The 'Ollama / OpenAI-compatible' provider is the highest-value target — Ollama exposes /v1/models that lists every locally-pulled model. Right now operators have to type the exact model identifier by hand.

Related: Johnny-fe.10, Johnny-fe (epic).

title: Parakeet CUDA build variant — opt-in INSTALL_PARAKEET=cuda for NVIDIA GPU hosts
description:
## Why

[[Johnny-stt.1]] shipped the NeMo / Parakeet adapter and Johnny-stt-runsh-nemo-cpu (this follow-up filed during the CPU install fix) wired the install into backend/Dockerfile, backend/Dockerfile.meet-worker, docker-compose.yml, and run.sh — but only for **CPU-only torch** (via `--extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu`). On a host with an NVIDIA GPU the user has no way to get a CUDA-enabled torch + NeMo without manually editing the Dockerfiles.

## What to ship

Promote the `INSTALL_PARAKEET` build arg from a 0/1 toggle to a 3-way variant: `none` | `cpu` (default) | `cuda`. The `cuda` branch picks the matching CUDA torch wheel index (e.g. `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124`) and skips the CPU-only flag.

- backend/Dockerfile + backend/Dockerfile.meet-worker: read `ARG INSTALL_PARAKEET=cpu` and branch on its value.
- docker-compose.yml: thread `${INSTALL_PARAKEET:-cpu}` to build.args for api / worker / migrate / meet-worker.
- run.sh: comment + export. Add a sanity check that warns if INSTALL_PARAKEET=cuda but `nvidia-smi` isn't on $PATH (cuda host driver missing).
- Add `runtime: nvidia` or `deploy.resources.devices` to the api / meet-worker compose entries when the variant is cuda, so the spawned container actually sees the GPU. Behind a separate env so non-GPU hosts don't choke on the unknown runtime.
- Document in README / setup notes.

## Acceptance criteria

- `INSTALL_PARAKEET=cuda ./run.sh` on an NVIDIA-GPU host produces an api image where `python -c 'import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())'` prints `True`.
- The catalog Test button with `device=cuda` in the Parakeet config transcribes in <1 s for a 5 s utterance (vs ~3–5 s on CPU).
- `INSTALL_PARAKEET=cpu` (default) is unchanged — no regression for users without a GPU.
- `INSTALL_PARAKEET=none` keeps the image lean and the error message from `_load_model` still tells the user how to enable it.
- chrome-devtools MCP run on a GPU host: navigate to Provider settings → STT tab → pick Parakeet → click Test → assert transcript renders + latency line shows the speedup.

## Notes

- Default stays `cpu` because most contributors are on Apple Silicon / Linux laptops without an NVIDIA GPU. CUDA is opt-in.
- The CPU branch shipped under the same epic as [[Johnny-stt.1]] (Parakeet adapter) — see the commit that touches backend/Dockerfile + backend/Dockerfile.meet-worker + docker-compose.yml + run.sh.
close_reason: Not needed — user opted out. CUDA-specific build variant would only matter for NVIDIA GPU hosts and adds maintenance burden; revisit only if a concrete GPU host need emerges.

title: STT provider settings: 'Record sample' button to verify transcription end-to-end (symmetric to existing TTS demo)
description:
## Why this exists

TTS providers already have a Play button that smoke-tests the provider by synthesising a demo phrase the user can hear (see Johnny-6ij). STT providers have no equivalent — there's no way to verify that a configured STT provider actually transcribes correctly without spinning up a full meeting.

This task adds the missing symmetric control on the STT provider settings page: a Record button that captures a short voice sample from the user's mic, sends it through the configured STT provider, and renders the transcribed text back in the UI. Same spirit as the TTS demo — fast feedback that the provider is wired correctly with the credentials it has.

Low priority per user request — nothing depends on this; it's an ergonomic improvement to the provider configuration flow.

## What to build

On every STT provider's settings card / configuration view:

- A **'Record sample'** button. Clicking it requests microphone permission (if not already granted), then starts capturing audio.
- A **'Stop'** button (or 'Stop and transcribe') visible while recording. Hitting it ends capture immediately. A safety cap auto-stops at 10 seconds if the user forgets to click stop.
- A visible recording indicator while capturing: timer (mm:ss), mic-level meter so the user can see the signal, and a clear 'recording…' state.
- After Stop, the captured audio is sent to the backend, run through the same provider's transcribe function (mirroring the _smoke_test pattern in backend/app/api/providers.py:706), and the resulting transcript text is rendered in a box under the button.
- Show useful metadata next to the result: provider used, recording duration, transcription latency (ms), and any provider-specific signal (confidence if available, detected language if the provider returns it).
- A small Play-back button lets the user hear what was recorded, so a 'no transcription' result can be diagnosed as 'I was muted' vs 'STT failed'.

### Default recording length

User suggested 5-10 s. Pick a 10 s safety cap with the user free to Stop earlier — long enough to read a sentence, short enough to keep the round-trip fast.

### Mic permission denial

If the browser denies mic access, show a clear inline message ('Microphone access needed to record a sample — enable it in browser settings') instead of a console error. As an optional nice-to-have: allow uploading a pre-recorded short clip (.wav / .webm) as a fallback so users without a mic, and CI, can still smoke-test STT.

### Provider coverage

Works for every registered STT provider:
- Cloud (Deepgram, OpenAI, etc — whatever is registered).
- Local Whisper.

A provider that hasn't implemented the transcribe contract yet returns a clean 'Not supported' message instead of crashing.

## Out of scope

- Streaming / partial-transcript display during recording. Initial version transcribes after stop. Streaming is a separate later improvement.
- Speaker diarization, language picking, custom vocabulary. Use provider defaults.
- Saving samples server-side for later. The audio is transient — used once, discarded.
- Multi-clip A/B comparison across providers. (Nice idea, but separate ticket.)

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every registered STT provider's settings card has a 'Record sample' button.
2. Clicking Record requests mic permission cleanly; clicking Stop (or hitting the 10 s cap) ends the recording and triggers transcription.
3. The transcription text appears in the UI within a few seconds of Stop, along with: provider used, recording duration, transcription latency, optional confidence / language metadata if the provider returns them.
4. A Play-back control lets the user audit the recorded clip locally without leaving the page.
5. Mic-denied state shows a clear inline message and a documented fallback (upload clip if implemented, otherwise instructions to enable mic).
6. Providers that haven't implemented transcribe return a graceful 'Not supported' instead of crashing.
7. The recorded audio is not persisted server-side; it's used once and discarded.
8. All behavior validated via chrome-devtools MCP with screenshots in the PR.

## Testing approach — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

Per the AGENTS.md top rule:

- new_page / navigate to the providers page, take_snapshot, assert each STT provider card shows a 'Record sample' button.
- Click Record via click; evaluate_script to confirm a MediaRecorder instance is active and the mic-level meter is updating.
- Drive a recorded clip (synthetic injection or a few seconds of test audio if the harness supports it).
- Click Stop; wait_for the transcription text element; assert it is non-empty and provider/latency metadata is shown.
- evaluate_script to confirm no MediaStream tracks are left live after Stop (no stuck mic indicator).
- emulate a denied mic permission, click Record, assert the inline error message renders and no console errors fire (list_console_messages).
- Repeat across at least one cloud STT provider and Local Whisper to confirm parity.
- Screenshots of: idle state, recording state, transcription result, mic-denied state — embedded in the PR description.

## Related

- TTS demo (Johnny-6ij) — the analogue this is symmetric to.
- [[per-session-activity-timing-log-surfaced-in-chat-history-per-turn-pipeline-events-with-durations]] (Johnny-ckz.7) — once shipped, the test should emit a timing event into the same instrument so STT latency numbers land in the same surface.
- [[profile-plus-tune-end-to-end-voice-latency-on-real-local-stt-tts-llm-and-add-in-ui-optimization-tips-on-each-provider-settings-page]] (Johnny-ckz.8) — the in-UI optimization tips for STT providers should reference this Record-sample tool as the way to sanity-check after tweaking settings.
design: Frontend: getUserMedia → MediaRecorder → blob; POST blob to a new backend endpoint that runs the configured provider's transcribe through the same smoke-call dispatch as _smoke_test in backend/app/api/providers.py:706. Backend response carries transcript + duration + latency + provider metadata. Frontend renders into a small result panel under the button. 10s safety cap enforced client-side. Release MediaStream tracks on Stop so the mic indicator clears.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Every registered STT provider card has a Record sample button. (2) Record / Stop flow works with a 10s safety cap. (3) Transcription text + metadata (provider, duration, latency, optional confidence/language) renders after Stop. (4) Play-back control plays the recorded clip. (5) Mic-denied shows a clear inline message; optional clip-upload fallback if implemented. (6) Providers without transcribe contract show 'Not supported' instead of crashing. (7) Recorded audio is not persisted server-side. (8) All behavior validated via chrome-devtools MCP with screenshots of idle / recording / result / mic-denied states in the PR.

title: Add no-CLI bot sign-in: in-browser Chromium via noVNC helper container
description:
## Why this exists

Johnny-4ph added a UI surface for bot session connection — but the user still has to run the CLI helper (`johnny.tools.seed_auth_state`) once to generate the storage_state.json, then upload it via the UI. This bead removes that last terminal step so a user who has never opened a terminal can connect a bot session entirely from the browser.

## What to build

### Helper container with noVNC
- Extend `Dockerfile.meet-worker` (or fork a new `Dockerfile.auth-helper`) with x11vnc + websockify + noVNC. Xvfb + Playwright + Chromium are already present.
- New entrypoint mode (env-gated) that:
  - Starts the existing Xvfb + PulseAudio bring-up
  - Launches x11vnc bound to :99 and websockify serving noVNC over HTTP
  - Runs Playwright headed to the Google sign-in page (pre-typing the bot email)
  - Polls page.url until it lands on a signed-in destination
  - Writes storage_state.json into `/var/lib/johnny/google-auth/account-<id>/storage_state.json` (volume mounted RW)
  - Publishes a Redis event (`bot-session.connected:<account_id>`) when done so the API can react
  - Exits cleanly

### API endpoints
- `POST /auth/google/accounts/{account_id}/bot-session/start` — spawn the helper container via DockerContainerLauncher, return the noVNC URL (port-mapped to host)
- `GET .../bot-session/start` (or reuse existing status) — poll for completion
- `POST .../bot-session/cancel` — stop the helper container
- Re-use the existing `bot_auth_seed` module for the file-presence status check

### Frontend
- "Connect bot session" button starts the helper and opens noVNC in a modal iframe (or popup)
- Status polls until storage_state.json appears or user cancels
- Success → close modal, mark account as connected
- Failure / timeout → show error and offer to retry

## Acceptance
- User clicks "Connect bot session" → Chromium appears in the UI → signs in → modal closes → status shows "Connected". No CLI step.
- The CLI helper and the UI upload path (from Johnny-4ph) continue to work — both still write to the same on-disk location.
- Helper container is cleaned up after success / failure / cancel.

## Dependencies
- Johnny-4ph (closed): added the validate/write/delete machinery and the UI status surface that this bead extends.

## Notes
- Port mapping for noVNC: dynamic per-session port allocation is cleanest but complex; a fixed port on docker-compose is the MVP. Doesn't matter for prod since this is a local-dev tool.
- The helper container needs RW access to `google_auth_state` (today the meet-worker mounts it RO — fine, this is a different launch profile).

title: Read Google Docs/Sheets URLs linked in calendar event description and include as pre-meeting context
description:
**Why this exists**

Johnny-ckz.3 plumbed the calendar event description into the bot's system prompt as pre-meeting context. Users frequently paste Google Docs / Sheets / Drive links into the event description as the meeting agenda or background reading. Today those URLs reach the bot as plain text — the bot sees the link but can't read the document.

**What to build**

When the calendar event description contains links to Google Docs / Sheets / Drive files, fetch their contents (with the meeting identity's OAuth token), extract the text body, and append to the pipeline's calendar_context distinct from the URL list itself.

Implementation sketch:
- Add 'app/services/calendar_link_resolver.py' that detects 'docs.google.com/document/d/.*' and 'docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/.*' patterns in description text.
- For each, use the Google Drive / Docs / Sheets API (via existing GoogleApiClient) to fetch text content.
- Concatenate into 'calendar_attachments_text' on LaunchContext / PipelineConfig.
- Cap total fetched text by a reasonable size (e.g. 20k chars) so we don't blow the pipeline's token budget.
- Cache fetched content per (event_id, etag) so a polling cycle doesn't re-fetch unchanged docs.

**Out of scope**

- Slack / Notion / generic URL fetching (separate auth surface).
- Image / chart extraction from the docs (text only).

**Acceptance Criteria**
- Calendar event description with a Google Docs link → the doc's text body lands in the bot's system prompt.
- Sheets link → tabular contents lands.
- Sheets with multiple tabs → handled.
- Drive permission denied → logged + the link continues to ride as plain text (no crash).
- Fetched content cached + invalidated on Drive etag change.

**Related**

- Johnny-ckz.3 — parent that added the description column.

title: Cross-session continuity: rehydrate prior session summary for recurring events
description:
**Why this exists**

Johnny-ckz.3 lit up *in-session* context (full transcript window + cached summarisation + rehydration on container restart). The bead explicitly deferred *cross-session* continuity: when a user runs the same recurring meeting next week, the bot starts the new session with no memory of what was decided last time.

**What to build**

When a new bot_session is created for a calendar_event whose 'recurring_event_id' matches a previous bot_session, pull the most recent prior session's transcript summary and inject it as an additional context layer (distinct from `config.context` / `config.calendar_context` so the audit row can tell them apart).

Implementation sketch:
- Add 'session_summary' column to 'bot_sessions' (or a new 'session_summaries' table keyed by bot_session_id) populated at session close.
- New helper in 'app/services/history.py' to look up the prior session for a recurring event.
- New 'PipelineConfig.prior_session_context' field rendered in both router and answer LLM system prompts as 'Last session summary: <text>'.
- Pipeline_runner reads via new env var 'JOHNNY_PRIOR_SESSION_CONTEXT'.

**Out of scope**

- Multi-session retrieval (vector search across all prior sessions — separate workstream).
- Surfacing prior session summary in the UI (the bead is about pipeline context, not display).

**Acceptance Criteria**
- Pipeline emits a prior-session-summary line in the system prompt when a recurring event has past sessions.
- Snapshot/audit row carries the prior session id and the summary text.
- Tests cover: recurring event with one prior session (uses it), recurring event with no prior session (empty), non-recurring event (no lookup), summary missing (no crash).

**Related**

- Johnny-ckz.3 — parent that built the in-session context handling.
- Johnny-kgc.33 — US-033 transcript persistence.

title: Add UI button to trigger bot Google sign-in (CLI helper stays as alternative)
description:
## Why this exists

Right now seeding the bot's Google session for Playwright requires running 'uv run python -m johnny.tools.seed_auth_state --account-id N --email ...' on the host. That works for an operator but is hostile to a normal user who never opens a terminal.

The CLI helper is fine to keep — it's useful for scripting, automation, and operator setup. We just additionally need a UI surface so a normal user can do this from the browser.

## What to build

### UI button (new)
- Add a 'Connect bot session' button in the Johnny UI — likely on the bot account row in /providers or a dedicated /settings/auth page
- Clicking it triggers a server-side flow that:
  - opens a temporary Chromium window the user can sign into, OR
  - delegates to a host helper invoked by the API (same code path as the CLI)
- After successful sign-in, save storage_state.json into the shared google_auth_state docker volume under account-<id>/storage_state.json
- Surface success in the UI ('Bot session connected — meet-worker can now join meetings')
- Surface failure with a clear reason

### CLI helper (keep)
- 'uv run python -m johnny.tools.seed_auth_state --account-id N --email ...' stays available, no changes required
- Both paths should write to the same storage_state.json location so they're interchangeable

## Acceptance

- User clicks 'Connect bot session' in the UI → completes Google sign-in → UI confirms success
- After UI sign-in, meet-worker can join meetings (uses the saved storage_state.json)
- CLI helper still works for operator/automation use cases
- Both paths produce identical storage_state.json files at the same path

title: TTS providers: separate Play button to hear a demo phrase, with Stop while playing
description:
## Why this exists

The provider page at /providers has a Test button per provider that verifies the configuration works (synthesis returns frames, no errors). That stays as-is.

What's missing is a way for the user to actually *hear* what the configured voice sounds like before wiring it into a real meeting. A working TTS provider with a wrong voice (mumbly, robotic, wrong language, wrong gender) is worse than a broken one because it slips into a real Meet and embarrasses you.

## What to build

A SEPARATE button next to (or near) the existing Test button, labeled something like 'Play' or 'Try'. Only applies to TTS providers (STT and LLM providers don't have this).

### Behavior
- Click Play → backend synthesizes a short demo phrase via that provider and streams the audio back to the browser, which plays it inline
- While audio is playing, the Play button changes to a Stop button
- Click Stop → audio stops immediately
- After audio finishes naturally, button reverts to Play
- Multiple providers playing simultaneously: each card has its own independent Play/Stop state

### NOT this
- Do NOT auto-play the demo after Test runs — Play is a separate explicit user action
- Do NOT add the demo phrase to the Test path — Test stays a config-validity check; Play is a voice-quality preview

## Acceptance

- /providers page shows Play button next to Test on every TTS provider card
- Click Play → hear a short phrase synthesized by that provider in the browser
- Button becomes Stop while audio is playing
- Click Stop → audio cuts immediately
- Audio finishes → button returns to Play
- Test button behavior is unchanged
acceptance_criteria: Clicking Test on a TTS provider plays a short demo phrase in the browser using that provider's voice. A 'Play sample' control allows replay. STT and LLM Test behaviour is unchanged. Synthesis failure is reported separately from test pass/fail. New endpoint returns a valid WAV. Quality gates pass: ruff, mypy, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint.
notes: Spawned 2026-06-06 from user request — wants to hear the configured TTS voice immediately after Test so a wrong/bad voice never ships into a real Meet.

title: VoiceInk parity: add Gemini, AssemblyAI, Groq, FluidAudio STT providers (bundle)
description:
## Why
Bundle of the remaining VoiceInk-parity STT providers. Backlog priority — not blocking the catalog UI (Johnny-stt.2) or streaming UX (Johnny-stt.3). Parakeet (Johnny-stt.1) is handled separately and is the priority local/streaming option.

## Scope
Add four STT provider plugins under `backend/app/providers/`. Each follows the same pattern as the existing `faster_whisper_stt` / `deepgram_stt` / `elevenlabs_stt` providers.

### A. Gemini STT (cloud)
- Plugin: `gemini_stt`
- Reuse `gemini_llm.py` API-key plumbing.
- Audio input via Google Generative Language API (inline base64 PCM or file upload — match VoiceInk's shape).
- Config: API key, model (e.g. gemini-2.x-flash), language hint.
- Reference: `/Users/nikita/Projects/VoiceInk/VoiceInk/Transcription/Cloud/GeminiProvider.swift`

### B. AssemblyAI STT (cloud, batch + streaming)
- Plugin: `assemblyai_stt`
- BOTH batch (one-shot upload + transcribe) and streaming (WebSocket realtime) interfaces.
- Streaming consumed by Johnny-stt.3 if it ships before this; batch consumed by the catalog Test button.
- Config: API key, language hint, model variant.
- References:
  - `/Users/nikita/Projects/VoiceInk/VoiceInk/Transcription/Cloud/AssemblyAIProvider.swift`
  - `/Users/nikita/Projects/VoiceInk/VoiceInk/Transcription/Streaming/AssemblyAIStreamingProvider.swift`

### C. Groq STT (cloud, fast Whisper-large-v3)
- Plugin: `groq_stt`
- Config: API key, model (whisper-large-v3 / distil-whisper-large-v3 / etc), language hint.
- Reference: `/Users/nikita/Projects/VoiceInk/VoiceInk/Transcription/Cloud/GroqProvider.swift`

### D. FluidAudio (local, platform support TBD)
- Plugin: `fluidaudio_stt` IF cross-platform support exists.
- VoiceInk is macOS-only; Johnny ships on Linux/Docker for the worker. **Block on a platform-support investigation first.** If FluidAudio is macOS-only, downgrade scope or drop with a note (don't block the rest of the bundle).
- Reference: `/Users/nikita/Projects/VoiceInk/VoiceInk/Transcription/FluidAudio/FluidAudioModelManager.swift`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each of A/B/C: provider listed in `providers/loader.py` + `providers/schema.py` and discoverable in the catalog UI.
- [ ] Each of A/B/C: transcribes the shared `tests/fixtures/audio/` clip.
- [ ] Each of A/B/C: appears in the STT catalog UI (Johnny-stt.2) and Test button returns a transcript.
- [ ] AssemblyAI streaming path emits partials over a synthetic 10s PCM stream.
- [ ] D (FluidAudio): platform-support investigation documented; if cross-platform, same acceptance shape; if macOS-only, document the decision in this ticket's notes.
- [ ] Each cloud provider surfaces network failure as a usable error (not silent timeout).

## Validation
- Mocked-API unit tests per provider in `backend/tests/providers/test_{gemini,assemblyai,groq,fluidaudio}_stt.py`.
- `@pytest.mark.network` live tests against each real endpoint (per project rule — mocks miss redirect-shape bugs, see `piper-voice-catalog-307-fix`).
- **Browser (chrome-devtools MCP):** for each new provider — navigate /settings/stt → select provider → enter test key → click Test → assert transcript appears → screenshot for PR.

## Depends on
- Johnny-stt.2 (catalog UI) — these providers plug into it.

title: Seed providers from JSON/config file on startup
description:
## Why this exists

The user wants to fill out provider settings in the UI, export them as JSON (sibling task), commit/save that JSON somewhere, and have it auto-loaded on the next stack startup. No more re-entering keys after a clean run.

This is the import side of the provider config export feature.

## What to build

- On stack startup, check for a config file at a well-known path (e.g. /config/providers.json mounted into the api container, or env var JOHNNY_PROVIDERS_FILE)
- If present, parse it and upsert all providers into the database
- Idempotent: same file → same DB state, regardless of how many times the stack restarts
- Don't clobber UI edits silently: if a provider already exists in the DB, prefer the file ONLY if the file is newer (or guard with an explicit 'seed mode' flag)
- Surface seeding status in logs and ideally a UI banner ('Providers seeded from /config/providers.json')

## Acceptance

- Place exported JSON at the configured path
- Bring stack up → providers appear in UI matching the file
- Stack restart → no duplicates, no clobbering
- JSON shape matches the export from [[export-all-provider-configurations-as-json-from-the-ui]]

title: Export all provider configurations as JSON from the UI
description:
## Why this exists

After spending time filling out provider credentials and options in the UI, the user wants a way to preserve that configuration so it survives a fresh stack reset, a new machine, or a teammate's setup. Today the only persistence is the database — re-entering everything by hand is painful.

A one-click 'Export configuration' button on /providers that downloads all provider configs as a single JSON file solves this.

## What to build

- 'Export configuration' button on /providers (or in a settings menu)
- Click → download a JSON file containing every provider's:
  - kind (stt / llm / tts)
  - provider name (openai, elevenlabs, etc.)
  - structured settings (per Johnny-mma refactor)
  - credentials (encrypted? plaintext? — decide based on threat model; at minimum offer 'with secrets' vs 'without secrets' modes)
- JSON shape should match the import format consumed by [[seed-providers-from-json-config-file-on-startup]]
- Filename: 'johnny-providers-YYYY-MM-DD.json'

## Acceptance

- /providers shows Export button
- Click → JSON downloads
- JSON has every configured provider with all settings
- Re-importing the same JSON (via the sibling import task) reproduces the exact provider state
